<a> Anchor (hyperlink)

current Category: Text-level semantics · Versions: HTML 1 (1991), HTML 2.0, HTML 3.2, HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <a> element (anchor) creates a hyperlink to another web page, a file, a location within the same page, an email address, a telephone number, or any other resource that can be identified by a URL. Hyperlinks are the defining feature of the World Wide Web and <a> was one of the very first elements created by Tim Berners-Lee in 1991.

The content of the <a> element is what the visitor sees and clicks. It is usually text, but in HTML5 it may also be an image, a whole card of content, or any other flow content, as long as the link does not contain another link or an interactive element such as a button.

If the href attribute is missing the element is a placeholder: it is rendered as plain text, is not focusable and is not announced as a link by screen readers. This is useful, for example, for the current page in a navigation menu.

In HTML 4 the <a> element was also used to define named anchors (<a name="top">) that other links could jump to. In HTML5 the name attribute is obsolete; use the id attribute on any element instead.

Syntax

<a href="URL">link text</a>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayinline
Content categoriesFlow content, phrasing content, interactive content (when href is present), palpable content
Permitted contentTransparent (whatever the parent allows), but it must not contain interactive content or another <a>
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts phrasing content or flow content
Tag omissionNeither the start tag nor the end tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLAnchorElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
hrefURLThe address the link points to. It may be absolute (https://example.com/page), relative (about.html, ../images/photo.jpg), a fragment (#section-2), or a special scheme (mailto:, tel:, sms:, javascript:). Without href the element is not a link.HTML 1
target_self | _blank | _parent | _top | frame-nameWhere to open the linked document. _self (default) opens it in the same browsing context; _blank opens a new tab or window; _parent opens it in the parent frame; _top opens it in the full window, replacing all frames. A custom name targets an <iframe> with that name.HTML 4.01
relspace-separated link typesThe relationship between the current document and the linked document. Common values: nofollow, noopener, noreferrer, external, alternate, author, bookmark, help, license, next, prev, search, tag. See the link types table in Part 9.HTML 4.01
downloadempty or filenameInstructs the browser to download the resource instead of navigating to it. If a value is given it is used as the suggested file name. Only works for same-origin URLs and blob:/data: URLs.HTML5
hreflangBCP 47 language tagThe language of the linked document, for example en, ar, fr-CA. Purely advisory.HTML 4.01
typeMIME typeThe media type of the linked resource, for example application/pdf. Advisory only.HTML 4.01
referrerpolicyno-referrer | no-referrer-when-downgrade | origin | origin-when-cross-origin | same-origin | strict-origin | strict-origin-when-cross-origin | unsafe-urlHow much referrer information is sent when following the link.HTML5
pingspace-separated URLsA list of URLs that receive a POST request with the body PING when the link is followed. Used for tracking.HTML5
attributionsrcempty or URLExperimental: registers an attribution source for the Attribution Reporting API.Living Standard
charsetcharacter encodingObsolete. The character encoding of the linked resource. Use the HTTP Content-Type header instead.HTML 4.01 (obsolete in HTML5)
coordscomma-separated numbersObsolete. Coordinates for use with shape in old image maps. Use <area> instead.HTML 4.01 (obsolete in HTML5)
nametextObsolete. Defined a named anchor that could be linked to with #name. Use id instead.HTML 1 (obsolete in HTML5)
revlink typesObsolete. Reverse relationship. Use rel instead.HTML 4.01 (obsolete in HTML5)
shaperect | circle | poly | defaultObsolete. Shape of a clickable region. Use <area> instead.HTML 4.01 (obsolete in HTML5)

Examples

Basic links

<p>Read the <a href="https://developer.mozilla.org/">MDN documentation</a>.</p>
<p>See our <a href="about.html">About page</a>.</p>
<p>Jump to the <a href="#footer">bottom of this page</a>.</p>

The first link is absolute, the second is relative to the current page, and the third is a fragment link that scrolls to the element whose id is footer.

Opening in a new tab safely

<a href="https://example.com" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">
  Example (opens in a new tab)
</a>

When you use target="_blank" add rel="noopener" so the new page cannot access your page through window.opener. Modern browsers do this automatically, but adding it is still good practice. Tell the user that the link opens in a new tab.

Email, telephone and download links

<a href="mailto:info@example.com?subject=Hello">Email us</a>
<a href="tel:+201001234567">Call us: 010 0123 4567</a>
<a href="report.pdf" download="annual-report-2026.pdf">Download the report (PDF)</a>

mailto: opens the visitor's email program; tel: dials on a phone; download forces a save dialog with the suggested file name.

A link wrapping a whole card (HTML5)

<a href="product.html" class="card">
  <img src="shoe.jpg" alt="Red running shoe">
  <h3>Running shoe</h3>
  <p>450 EGP</p>
</a>

Since HTML5 an anchor may contain block-level content. The entire card becomes clickable.

A placeholder link for the current page

<nav>
  <a>Home</a>
  <a href="shop.html">Shop</a>
  <a href="contact.html">Contact</a>
</nav>

Home has no href, so it is shown as text and is not focusable, which is correct for the page the visitor is already on. You could also add aria-current="page" to a real link instead.

Default browser CSS

a:-webkit-any-link { color: -webkit-link; cursor: pointer; text-decoration: underline; }

Accessibility

  • Link text must make sense on its own. Screen reader users often read a list of all links on a page; 'click here' or 'read more' tells them nothing. Prefer 'Download the 2026 price list'.
  • Do not use the same link text for links that go to different places.
  • When a link contains only an image, the image's alt text becomes the link text, so it must describe the destination.
  • Links should look different from ordinary text (usually underlined) and have a visible focus outline.
  • Do not use javascript: URLs; use a <button> for actions that are not navigation.

Common mistakes

  • Nesting an <a> inside another <a>, or putting a <button> inside an <a>.
  • Using an <a> without href as a button. Use <button> instead.
  • Forgetting rel="noopener" with target="_blank" on old browsers.
  • Using onclick="location.href=..." on a <div> instead of a real link, which breaks keyboard access, right-click and search engines.
  • Writing the URL with spaces or with backslashes instead of forward slashes.

See also

<area>, <link>, <button>, <nav>

<abbr> Abbreviation

current Category: Text-level semantics · Versions: HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <abbr> element marks an abbreviation or acronym. The optional title attribute holds the full expansion, which most browsers show as a tooltip when the mouse hovers over the text.

Use <abbr> the first time an abbreviation appears in a document, ideally writing the expansion in the text as well, because tooltips are not available on touch screens and are not read by every screen reader.

HTML 4.01 also had an <acronym> element for pronounceable abbreviations such as NASA. It was removed in HTML5; use <abbr> for both.

Syntax

<abbr title="expansion">ABBR</abbr>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayinline
Content categoriesFlow content, phrasing content, palpable content
Permitted contentPhrasing content
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts phrasing content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
titletextThe full expansion of the abbreviation. On <abbr> this attribute has a specific meaning and should contain nothing else.HTML 4.01

Examples

Abbreviation with tooltip

<p>The <abbr title="World Health Organization">WHO</abbr> was founded in 1948.</p>

Hovering WHO shows 'World Health Organization'.

Defining an abbreviation with <dfn>

<p><dfn><abbr title="HyperText Markup Language">HTML</abbr></dfn> is the language of the web.</p>

Wrapping in <dfn> marks this as the place where the term is defined.

Styling the dotted underline

<style>
  abbr[title] { text-decoration: underline dotted; cursor: help; }
</style>
<p>Pages are served over <abbr title="HyperText Transfer Protocol Secure">HTTPS</abbr>.</p>

Most browsers already show a dotted underline; this rule makes it consistent.

Default browser CSS

abbr[title] { text-decoration: underline dotted; }

Accessibility

  • Provide the expansion in plain text at least once; do not rely on the tooltip alone.
  • Some screen readers can be set to read the title attribute, but it is off by default.

Common mistakes

  • Using <acronym>, which is obsolete.
  • Putting long explanations in title; it is for the expansion only.

See also

<dfn>, <acronym>

<acronym> Acronym (obsolete)

obsolete Category: Obsolete text-level · Versions: HTML 4.01; obsolete in HTML5

Description

The <acronym> element marked an acronym: an abbreviation pronounced as a word, such as NASA or laser. HTML5 removed it because the distinction from <abbr> was confusing and browsers treated the two identically.

Replace every <acronym> with <abbr>.

Syntax

<acronym title="expansion">NASA</acronym>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayinline
Content categoriesPhrasing content (historical)
Permitted contentPhrasing content
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts phrasing content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
titletextThe expansion of the acronym.HTML 4.01

Examples

Old code and its replacement

<!-- HTML 4.01 -->
<acronym title="National Aeronautics and Space Administration">NASA</acronym>

<!-- HTML5 -->
<abbr title="National Aeronautics and Space Administration">NASA</abbr>

Default browser CSS

acronym { text-decoration: underline dotted; }

Accessibility

  • Same as <abbr>.

Common mistakes

  • Using it at all in new pages.

See also

<abbr>

<address> Contact address

current Category: Content sectioning · Versions: HTML 1, HTML 2.0, HTML 3.2, HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <address> element indicates that its content provides contact information for a person, people or an organisation. When placed inside an <article> it gives the contact details of the article's author; when placed in the page <footer> or <body> it gives the contact details for the whole document.

The contact information may be any kind: physical address, email, telephone, URL, social media handle, geographic coordinates. Despite its name, <address> is not meant for arbitrary postal addresses (such as the shipping address in an order); it is only for contact details of the author or owner of the content.

Browsers display <address> in italics by default, exactly as they did in 1991.

Syntax

<address>contact information</address>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayblock
Content categoriesFlow content, palpable content
Permitted contentFlow content, but no heading content, no sectioning content, and no <header>, <footer> or nested <address>
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts flow content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLElement

Attributes

Only the global attributes and event handler attributes.

Examples

Contact details in the page footer

<footer>
  <address>
    Written by <a href="mailto:jane@example.com">Jane Doe</a>.<br>
    Visit us at:<br>
    Example Ltd.<br>
    12 Nile Street<br>
    Giza, Egypt
  </address>
</footer>

Author contact inside an article

<article>
  <h2>Learning HTML</h2>
  <p>...</p>
  <address>Contact the author: <a href="tel:+201000000000">+20 100 000 0000</a></address>
</article>

Here the address applies to the article only.

Default browser CSS

address { display: block; font-style: italic; }

Accessibility

  • Screen readers may announce the element as 'contact information', which helps users find it.

Common mistakes

  • Using <address> for every postal address on a page (for example in an order form).
  • Placing headings or sections inside it.

See also

<footer>, <article>, <a>

<applet> Java applet (obsolete)

obsolete Category: Obsolete embedded content · Versions: HTML 3.2, HTML 4.01 (deprecated); obsolete in HTML5

Description

The <applet> element embedded a Java applet in the page. Applets were small Java programs that ran inside the browser with the help of a plug-in. Java applets were popular in the late 1990s but were slow, insecure and not supported on mobile devices. HTML 4.01 deprecated <applet> in favour of <object>, and HTML5 removed it entirely. No modern browser runs applets.

Syntax

<applet code="MyApplet.class" width="300" height="200"></applet>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayinline-block
Content categoriesEmbedded content (historical)
Permitted contentZero or more <param> elements followed by fallback content
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts embedded content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLUnknownElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
codeclass file nameThe name of the compiled applet class file.HTML 3.2
codebaseURLThe base URL for the applet's class files.HTML 3.2
archivecomma-separated URLsJAR archives to preload.HTML 4.01
objectfile nameA serialised applet file.HTML 4.01
alttextAlternative text for browsers without Java.HTML 3.2
nametextA name so that applets on the same page can find each other.HTML 3.2
width / heightpixelsSize of the applet display area.HTML 3.2
alignleft | right | top | middle | bottomAlignment relative to surrounding text.HTML 3.2
hspace / vspacepixelsHorizontal and vertical margins.HTML 3.2

Examples

Historical example

<applet code="Clock.class" width="200" height="200">
  <param name="timezone" value="Africa/Cairo">
  Your browser does not support Java applets.
</applet>

For comparison, modern pages implement such features with JavaScript and <canvas>.

Default browser CSS

applet { display: inline-block; }

Accessibility

  • Applets were inaccessible to assistive technology.

Common mistakes

  • Any use in a modern page.

See also

<object>, <embed>, <canvas>

<area> Image map area

current Category: Image and multimedia · Versions: HTML 3.2, HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <area> element defines a clickable region inside an image map. An image map is an image (<img usemap="#name">) linked to a <map name="name"> element that contains one or more <area> elements. Each area has a shape and coordinates, and behaves like a hyperlink.

<area> is a void element: it has no content and no closing tag. It may only be used inside <map>.

Syntax

<area shape="rect" coords="x1,y1,x2,y2" href="URL" alt="text">

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementYes (no closing tag)
Default displayinline
Content categoriesFlow content, phrasing content
Permitted contentNone (void element)
Permitted parents<map> (the <area> may be a descendant of <map> at any depth, as long as there is no intervening <a>)
Tag omissionNo end tag
DOM interfaceHTMLAreaElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
alttextAlternative text for the area. Required when href is present so that the link has an accessible name.HTML 3.2
coordscomma-separated numbersThe coordinates of the shape in CSS pixels measured from the top-left corner of the image. rect: x1,y1,x2,y2 (top-left and bottom-right). circle: x,y,radius. poly: x1,y1,x2,y2,... (any number of points).HTML 3.2
shaperect | circle | poly | defaultThe shape of the region. default covers the whole image.HTML 3.2
hrefURLThe destination of the link.HTML 3.2
target_self | _blank | _parent | _top | nameWhere to open the destination.HTML 4.01
downloadempty or filenameDownload the resource instead of navigating.HTML5
rellink typesRelationship of the linked resource.HTML5
pingURLsURLs to ping when the link is followed.HTML5
referrerpolicyreferrer policy keywordReferrer policy for the navigation.HTML5
nohrefbooleanObsolete. Indicated the area had no link. Simply omit href instead.HTML 3.2 (obsolete)
typeMIME typeObsolete in HTML5. Type of the linked resource.HTML 4.01

Examples

A world map with three clickable regions

<img src="map.png" alt="Map of the office" usemap="#office" width="400" height="300">
<map name="office">
  <area shape="rect" coords="0,0,200,150" href="kitchen.html" alt="Kitchen">
  <area shape="circle" coords="300,75,50" href="meeting.html" alt="Meeting room">
  <area shape="poly" coords="0,150,200,150,100,300" href="desks.html" alt="Desks">
  <area shape="default" href="office.html" alt="Whole office">
</map>

The rectangle covers the top-left quarter, the circle has centre (300,75) and radius 50, and the polygon is a triangle. The default area catches clicks anywhere else.

Default browser CSS

area { display: inline; }

Accessibility

  • Every <area> with href needs a meaningful alt.
  • Image maps do not scale well on small screens; consider SVG with real links instead.

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting the # in usemap="#name".
  • Coordinates that do not match the displayed image size.
  • Writing a closing </area> tag.

See also

<map>, <img>, <a>

<article> Self-contained article

current Category: Content sectioning · Versions: HTML5

Description

The <article> element represents a complete, self-contained piece of content that would make sense on its own if it were distributed independently, for example in an RSS feed. Typical uses are a blog post, a news story, a forum post, a product card, a user comment or an interactive widget.

An <article> usually has its own heading, and may have its own <header>, <footer> and <address>. Articles can be nested: comments on a blog post are articles inside the post's article.

The test for choosing <article> rather than <section> or <div> is: 'Could this piece be copied to another site and still make sense?' If yes, it is an article.

Syntax

<article>...</article>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayblock
Content categoriesFlow content, sectioning content, palpable content
Permitted contentFlow content
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts flow content, but not inside <address>
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLElement

Attributes

Only the global attributes and event handler attributes.

Examples

A blog post

<article>
  <header>
    <h2>How I learned HTML</h2>
    <p>Posted <time datetime="2026-09-11">11 September 2026</time> by Ahmed</p>
  </header>
  <p>It started with a single footer tag...</p>
  <footer>
    <p>Tags: html, learning</p>
  </footer>
</article>

Nested articles for comments

<article>
  <h2>Post title</h2>
  <p>Post text.</p>
  <section>
    <h3>Comments</h3>
    <article>
      <p>Great post!</p>
      <footer>- Sara</footer>
    </article>
  </section>
</article>

Product cards in a shop

<article class="product">
  <img src="book.jpg" alt="Cover of Learn HTML">
  <h3>Learn HTML</h3>
  <p>120 EGP</p>
  <button>Add to cart</button>
</article>

Default browser CSS

article { display: block; }

Accessibility

  • Screen readers expose <article> with the role 'article' and may let users jump between articles.
  • Give each article a heading so it can be identified.

Common mistakes

  • Using <article> for every box on the page; use <section> or <div> for content that is not self-contained.
  • Omitting a heading inside the article.

See also

<section>, <aside>, <header>, <footer>, <main>, <nav>

<aside> Aside (sidebar / tangential content)

current Category: Content sectioning · Versions: HTML5

Description

The <aside> element represents content that is only indirectly related to the main content around it. It is often displayed as a sidebar or a call-out box: pull quotes, related links, advertising, author biographies, glossary definitions, or a list of other articles.

Inside an <article>, an <aside> holds content related to that article. Directly inside <body> or <main>, it holds content related to the page as a whole, such as a site-wide sidebar.

Syntax

<aside>...</aside>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayblock
Content categoriesFlow content, sectioning content, palpable content
Permitted contentFlow content
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts flow content, but not inside <address>
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLElement

Attributes

Only the global attributes and event handler attributes.

Examples

A sidebar with related links

<main>
  <article>
    <h1>The Nile</h1>
    <p>The Nile is the longest river in Africa...</p>
  </article>
  <aside>
    <h2>Related</h2>
    <ul>
      <li><a href="aswan.html">Aswan Dam</a></li>
      <li><a href="delta.html">Nile Delta</a></li>
    </ul>
  </aside>
</main>

A pull quote inside an article

<article>
  <p>Learning takes time, but every tag you learn is a tool you keep.</p>
  <aside><q>Every tag you learn is a tool you keep.</q></aside>
  <p>...</p>
</article>

Default browser CSS

aside { display: block; }

Accessibility

  • Exposed as a 'complementary' landmark so users can skip to or over it.

Common mistakes

  • Using <aside> for parenthetical text inside a paragraph; use parentheses or <span> for that.
  • Putting the main content in an <aside>.

See also

<article>, <section>, <main>, <nav>

<audio> Embedded audio

current Category: Image and multimedia · Versions: HTML5

Description

The <audio> element embeds sound content: music, podcasts, sound effects or recorded speech. The source may be given with the src attribute or with one or more <source> child elements so that the browser can choose a format it supports. Content placed inside the element after the <source> elements is shown only by browsers that do not support <audio> at all.

By default nothing is displayed. Add the controls attribute to show the browser's built-in play, pause, volume and progress controls, or control playback from JavaScript with the HTMLMediaElement methods play() and pause().

Browsers block automatic playback with sound until the user has interacted with the page, so autoplay usually works only together with muted.

Syntax

<audio src="file.mp3" controls></audio>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayinline
Content categoriesFlow content, phrasing content, embedded content; interactive and palpable if controls is present
Permitted contentIf src is present: zero or more <track> elements then transparent content with no media elements. If src is absent: zero or more <source>, then zero or more <track>, then transparent content with no media elements
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts embedded content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLAudioElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
srcURLThe URL of the audio file. Alternatively use <source> children.HTML5
controlsbooleanShow the browser's playback controls.HTML5
autoplaybooleanStart playing as soon as enough data has loaded. Usually blocked unless muted.HTML5
loopbooleanRestart from the beginning when the end is reached.HTML5
mutedbooleanStart with the sound muted.HTML5
preloadnone | metadata | autoA hint about how much to download before playback: nothing, only metadata such as duration (default in most browsers), or the whole file.HTML5
crossoriginanonymous | use-credentialsHow to handle cross-origin requests, needed when the audio will be processed with the Web Audio API or canvas.HTML5
controlslistnodownload | nofullscreen | noremoteplaybackHides specific built-in controls (non-standard, Chromium).Living Standard
disableremoteplaybackbooleanDisables casting to remote devices.Living Standard

Examples

Simple player

<audio src="song.mp3" controls>
  Your browser does not support the audio element.
  <a href="song.mp3">Download the song</a>.
</audio>

Multiple formats with <source>

<audio controls preload="metadata">
  <source src="podcast.opus" type="audio/ogg; codecs=opus">
  <source src="podcast.mp3" type="audio/mpeg">
  <p>Download the <a href="podcast.mp3">MP3</a>.</p>
</audio>

The browser uses the first source it can play. Opus is smaller; MP3 works everywhere.

Controlling playback with JavaScript

<audio id="beep" src="beep.wav"></audio>
<button onclick="document.getElementById('beep').play()">Play beep</button>

Background music that loops (muted by default)

<audio src="ambient.mp3" autoplay loop muted></audio>

The user must unmute it themselves.

Default browser CSS

audio:not([controls]) { display: none !important; }

Accessibility

  • Provide a transcript for spoken content; <track> captions are supported only on <video> in most browsers.
  • Always include controls or provide your own accessible buttons.
  • Never autoplay sound; it is disorienting and can hide a screen reader's speech.

Common mistakes

  • Expecting autoplay with sound to work.
  • Using a single format that not all browsers support.
  • Forgetting the type attribute on <source>, which forces the browser to download each file to test it.

See also

<video>, <source>, <track>, <embed>, <object>

<b> Bring attention to (bold)

current Category: Text-level semantics · Versions: HTML 2.0, HTML 3.2, HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <b> element draws the reader's attention to a span of text without giving it extra importance, emphasis or an alternative voice. Browsers render it in bold. Typical uses are keywords in a summary, product names in a review, or the lead sentence of an article.

In HTML 4 <b> was a purely presentational element meaning 'bold'. HTML5 redefined it with the meaning above so that it remains valid, but the standard says to use <b> only as a last resort when no other element is more appropriate: <strong> for importance, <em> for emphasis, <mark> for relevance, <h1>-<h6> for headings, and CSS font-weight for pure styling.

Syntax

<b>text</b>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayinline
Content categoriesFlow content, phrasing content, palpable content
Permitted contentPhrasing content
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts phrasing content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLElement

Attributes

Only the global attributes and event handler attributes.

Examples

Keywords in a product description

<p>This laptop has a <b>15-inch display</b>, <b>16 GB of RAM</b> and a <b>1 TB SSD</b>.</p>

The keywords stand out but are not more 'important' in the <strong> sense.

Difference between <b> and <strong>

<p><strong>Warning:</strong> the <b>red</b> wire carries current.</p>

'Warning' is important (strong); 'red' is merely highlighted as a keyword (b).

Default browser CSS

b { font-weight: bold; }

Accessibility

  • Screen readers do not announce <b> in any special way. Use <strong> when the boldness carries meaning.

Common mistakes

  • Using <b> for headings instead of <h1>-<h6>.
  • Using <b> for emphasis instead of <em> or <strong>.

See also

<strong>, <em>, <i>, <mark>

<base> Document base URL

current Category: Document metadata · Versions: HTML 2.0, HTML 3.2, HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <base> element specifies the base URL used to resolve all relative URLs in the document, and/or the default target for all links and forms. There may be only one <base> element per document and it must be placed in <head>, before any element that uses a URL.

It is a void element. At least one of href or target must be present.

Syntax

<base href="URL" target="_blank">

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementYes (no closing tag)
Default displaynone
Content categoriesMetadata content
Permitted contentNone (void element)
Permitted parents<head> (only one allowed)
Tag omissionNo end tag
DOM interfaceHTMLBaseElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
hrefURLThe base URL. Relative URLs such as images/logo.png are resolved against it.HTML 2.0
target_self | _blank | _parent | _top | nameThe default browsing context for links and forms that do not specify their own target.HTML 4.01

Examples

Making all relative links point to another server

<head>
  <base href="https://cdn.example.com/assets/">
</head>
<body>
  <img src="logo.png" alt="Logo">
  <!-- loads https://cdn.example.com/assets/logo.png -->
</body>

Opening every link in a new tab

<head>
  <base target="_blank">
</head>

Individual links can still override this with their own target.

Default browser CSS

base { display: none; }

Accessibility

  • Opening all links in new tabs without warning is confusing; use with care.

Common mistakes

  • Placing <base> after a <link> or <script> that uses a relative URL; it does not apply retroactively.
  • Having more than one <base>.
  • Forgetting that fragment links (#top) are also affected and will navigate to the base URL.

See also

<head>, <link>, <a>

<basefont> Base font (obsolete)

obsolete Category: Obsolete presentational · Versions: HTML 3.2, HTML 4.01 (deprecated); obsolete in HTML5

Description

The <basefont> element set the default font size, colour and face for the whole document. It was a presentational element from HTML 3.2 and was deprecated in HTML 4.01 in favour of CSS. HTML5 removed it. Use CSS on the body element instead.

Syntax

<basefont size="3" color="black" face="Arial">

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementYes (no closing tag)
Default displaynone
Content categoriesHistorical
Permitted contentNone
Permitted parents<head> or <body>
Tag omissionNo end tag
DOM interfaceHTMLUnknownElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
size1 to 7Default font size on the 1-7 HTML scale (3 = normal).HTML 3.2
colorcolourDefault text colour.HTML 4.01
facecomma-separated font namesDefault font family.HTML 4.01

Examples

Replacement in CSS

<!-- Old -->
<basefont size="4" face="Arial" color="#333">

<!-- New -->
<style>
  body { font: 18px Arial, sans-serif; color: #333; }
</style>

Common mistakes

  • Any use.

See also

<font>, <body>

<bdi> Bidirectional isolate

current Category: Text-level semantics · Versions: HTML5

Description

The <bdi> element isolates a span of text that might be written in a different direction from the text around it, so that its direction does not affect the surrounding text. It is essential when you insert user-generated text of unknown direction, such as user names, into a sentence.

Without isolation, an Arabic or Hebrew name followed by a number in an English sentence can cause the number and punctuation to appear in the wrong place. <bdi> tells the bidirectional algorithm to treat the inner text as a separate unit.

It is equivalent to CSS unicode-bidi: isolate, and by default its direction is auto (detected from the content).

Syntax

<bdi>text of unknown direction</bdi>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayinline
Content categoriesFlow content, phrasing content, palpable content
Permitted contentPhrasing content
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts phrasing content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
dirltr | rtl | autoOn <bdi> the default is auto, unlike other elements where dir is inherited.HTML5

Examples

User names in a leaderboard

<ul>
  <li><bdi>Ahmed</bdi>: 120 points</li>
  <li><bdi>محمد</bdi>: 95 points</li>
  <li><bdi>Sara</bdi>: 80 points</li>
</ul>

Without <bdi> the second line could render as ': 95 points محمد' with the colon misplaced.

Default browser CSS

bdi { unicode-bidi: isolate; }

Accessibility

  • Improves reading order for screen readers as well as visual order.

Common mistakes

  • Using <bdo> when you want isolation; <bdo> forces a direction, <bdi> isolates.

See also

<bdo>, <span>

<bdo> Bidirectional text override

current Category: Text-level semantics · Versions: HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <bdo> element overrides the current text direction and forces its content to be displayed in the direction given by the dir attribute, character by character, ignoring the Unicode bidirectional algorithm. The dir attribute is required.

It is rarely needed; use it when you must display text backwards, for example to show how a right-to-left string is stored, or to fix a badly encoded document.

Syntax

<bdo dir="rtl">text</bdo>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayinline
Content categoriesFlow content, phrasing content, palpable content
Permitted contentPhrasing content
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts phrasing content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
dirltr | rtlRequired. The direction to force.HTML 4.01

Examples

Displaying English backwards

<p><bdo dir="rtl">This text is reversed</bdo></p>

Renders as 'desrever si txet sihT'.

Default browser CSS

bdo { unicode-bidi: isolate-override; }

Accessibility

  • Screen readers read the characters in the overridden order, which may be nonsense; use sparingly.

Common mistakes

  • Omitting dir, which is required.
  • Using <bdo> for isolation; use <bdi>.

See also

<bdi>

<bgsound> Background sound (non-standard, obsolete)

obsolete Category: Obsolete embedded content · Versions: Internet Explorer extension, never standard; obsolete

Description

The <bgsound> element was an Internet Explorer extension that played a sound file automatically when the page loaded. It was never part of any HTML standard and is not supported by any modern browser. Use <audio> instead.

Syntax

<bgsound src="music.mid" loop="infinite">

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementYes (no closing tag)
Default displaynone
Content categoriesHistorical
Permitted contentNone
Permitted parents<head> or <body>
Tag omissionNo end tag
DOM interfaceHTMLUnknownElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
srcURLThe sound file.IE
loopnumber | infiniteRepeat count.IE
balance-10000 to 10000Stereo balance.IE
volume-10000 to 0Volume.IE

Examples

Replacement

<audio src="music.mp3" autoplay loop muted></audio>

Common mistakes

  • Any use.

See also

<audio>

<big> Bigger text (obsolete)

obsolete Category: Obsolete presentational · Versions: HTML 3.2, HTML 4.01; obsolete in HTML5

Description

The <big> element rendered its content one font size larger than the surrounding text. It was purely presentational and was removed in HTML5. Its counterpart <small> survived because it was given a new meaning (side comments and fine print). Use CSS font-size instead of <big>.

Syntax

<big>text</big>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayinline
Content categoriesPhrasing content (historical)
Permitted contentPhrasing content
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts phrasing content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLElement

Attributes

Only the global attributes and event handler attributes.

Examples

Replacement

<!-- Old -->
<p>Only <big>3 days</big> left!</p>

<!-- New -->
<p>Only <span style="font-size: larger">3 days</span> left!</p>

Default browser CSS

big { font-size: larger; }

Common mistakes

  • Any use in new pages.

See also

<small>, <span>

<blink> Blinking text (non-standard, obsolete)

obsolete Category: Obsolete presentational · Versions: Netscape extension, never standard; obsolete

Description

The <blink> element made its text flash on and off. It was a Netscape Navigator extension from 1994, was never part of any standard, and was widely considered the most annoying element ever created. All browsers removed support by 2013. Blinking content is also an accessibility hazard for people with photosensitive epilepsy and attention disorders.

Syntax

<blink>text</blink>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayinline
Content categoriesHistorical
Permitted contentPhrasing content
Permitted parentsAny
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLUnknownElement

Attributes

Only the global attributes and event handler attributes.

Examples

Do not do this

<blink>Sale!</blink>

If you must animate, use a CSS animation with a slow, subtle effect and respect prefers-reduced-motion.

Accessibility

  • Flashing content can trigger seizures. WCAG forbids flashing more than three times per second.

Common mistakes

  • Any use.

See also

<marquee>

<blockquote> Block quotation

current Category: Text content · Versions: HTML 2.0, HTML 3.2, HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <blockquote> element indicates that the enclosed text is an extended quotation from another source. Browsers indent it on both sides by default. The optional cite attribute holds the URL of the source; a visible citation should be given with the <cite> element, usually in a <footer> inside the blockquote or in a following paragraph.

For short quotations that sit inside a sentence use <q> instead.

Syntax

<blockquote cite="URL">quoted text</blockquote>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayblock
Content categoriesFlow content, sectioning root, palpable content
Permitted contentFlow content
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts flow content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLQuoteElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
citeURLThe URL of the source document or message. Not displayed by browsers; readable by scripts and tools.HTML 4.01

Examples

Quotation with source

<blockquote cite="https://www.w3.org/People/Berners-Lee/">
  <p>The Web does not just connect machines, it connects people.</p>
  <footer>- <cite>Tim Berners-Lee</cite></footer>
</blockquote>

Custom styling

<style>
  blockquote {
    margin: 1em 0; padding: 0.5em 1em;
    border-left: 4px solid #c8a24a; background: #fdf8f0;
  }
</style>
<blockquote><p>Practice is the only tutorial that always works.</p></blockquote>

Default browser CSS

blockquote { display: block; margin: 1em 40px; }

Accessibility

  • Screen readers announce 'blockquote' so users know the text is quoted.

Common mistakes

  • Using <blockquote> just to indent text; use CSS margin for that.
  • Putting the author's name inside the quotation as if it were quoted.

See also

<q>, <cite>, <footer>

<body> Document body

current Category: Sectioning root · Versions: HTML 2.0, HTML 3.2, HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <body> element contains all the content of the document that is displayed to the visitor: text, images, links, forms, media, and the scripts that operate on them. There is exactly one <body> in a document and it is the second child of <html>, after <head>.

In HTML 3.2 and 4.01 <body> carried presentational attributes (bgcolor, text, link, vlink, alink, background) that set page colours and background images. They are obsolete in HTML5; use CSS. The <body> element also accepts window event handler attributes such as onload and onresize, because events on the window are reflected onto the body.

The start and end tags of <body> may technically be omitted and the browser will create the element automatically, but always write them for clarity.

Syntax

<body>...</body>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayblock
Content categoriesSectioning root
Permitted contentFlow content
Permitted parents<html>, as its second child
Tag omissionStart tag may be omitted if the body is empty or starts with non-whitespace content that is not a comment, <script> or <style>; end tag may be omitted if not followed by a comment
DOM interfaceHTMLBodyElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
onafterprint, onbeforeprintscriptFired after and before the document is printed.HTML5
onbeforeunloadscriptFired when the user is about to leave; can prompt for confirmation.HTML5
onhashchangescriptFired when the URL fragment (#...) changes.HTML5
onlanguagechangescriptFired when the preferred language changes.HTML5
onloadscriptFired when the whole page, including images, has loaded.HTML 4.01
onmessage, onmessageerrorscriptFired when a message is received via postMessage.HTML5
onoffline, ononlinescriptFired when network connectivity is lost or regained.HTML5
onpagehide, onpageshowscriptFired when navigating away from or back to the page (including from the back-forward cache).HTML5
onpopstatescriptFired when the active history entry changes.HTML5
onresizescriptFired when the window is resized.HTML 4.01
onstoragescriptFired when localStorage or sessionStorage changes in another tab.HTML5
onunloadscriptFired when the document is unloaded. Unreliable; prefer pagehide.HTML 4.01
alinkcolourObsolete. Colour of active (being clicked) links. Use CSS a:active.HTML 3.2
backgroundURLObsolete. Background image. Use CSS background-image.HTML 3.2
bgcolorcolourObsolete. Background colour. Use CSS background-color.HTML 3.2
linkcolourObsolete. Colour of unvisited links. Use CSS a:link.HTML 3.2
textcolourObsolete. Text colour. Use CSS color.HTML 3.2
vlinkcolourObsolete. Colour of visited links. Use CSS a:visited.HTML 3.2
bottommargin, leftmargin, rightmargin, topmarginpixelsObsolete, non-standard. Page margins. Use CSS margin.IE/Netscape

Examples

Minimal document

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <title>Hello</title>
</head>
<body>
  <h1>Hello, world!</h1>
</body>
</html>

HTML 3.2 colours and their CSS replacement

<!-- HTML 3.2 -->
<body bgcolor="#ffffff" text="#000000" link="#0000ff" vlink="#800080">

<!-- HTML5 + CSS -->
<style>
  body { background: #fff; color: #000; }
  a:link { color: blue; }
  a:visited { color: purple; }
</style>
<body>

Running code when the page has loaded

<body onload="console.log('Page loaded')">

Prefer addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', ...) in a script.

Default browser CSS

body { display: block; margin: 8px; }

Accessibility

  • Set the page language on <html>, not <body>.
  • Keep a logical reading order in the body; CSS can rearrange the visual layout but assistive technology follows the source order.

Common mistakes

  • Having two <body> elements.
  • Putting <title> or <meta> in the body.
  • Using the obsolete colour attributes.

See also

<html>, <head>, <main>, <header>, <footer>

<br> Line break

current Category: Text-level semantics · Versions: HTML 1, HTML 2.0, HTML 3.2, HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <br> element produces a line break in text: the text after it starts on a new line. It is a void element with no closing tag. Use it only where the division of lines is part of the content, as in a postal address or a poem.

Do not use <br> to create space between paragraphs or blocks. Use separate <p> elements and CSS margins instead. A series of <br><br><br> to push content down is a classic beginner mistake that breaks on different screen sizes and confuses screen readers.

Syntax

<br>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementYes (no closing tag)
Default displayinline
Content categoriesFlow content, phrasing content
Permitted contentNone (void element)
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts phrasing content
Tag omissionNo end tag
DOM interfaceHTMLBRElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
clearleft | right | all | noneObsolete. Moved the following text below any floated images. Use CSS clear.HTML 3.2

Examples

An address

<p>
  Example Ltd.<br>
  12 Nile Street<br>
  Giza, Egypt
</p>

A poem

<p>
  Roses are red,<br>
  Violets are blue,<br>
  HTML is easy,<br>
  And so are you.
</p>

Wrong and right

<!-- Wrong: spacing with br -->
<p>First</p><br><br>
<p>Second</p>

<!-- Right: spacing with CSS -->
<style>p { margin-bottom: 2em; }</style>
<p>First</p>
<p>Second</p>

Default browser CSS

br { display: inline; }

Accessibility

  • Screen readers may announce each <br>, so many consecutive breaks are noisy.

Common mistakes

  • Using <br> for vertical spacing.
  • Writing </br>, which is invalid (browsers treat it as <br>).
  • Using <br> to separate list items instead of <ul>/<li>.

See also

<p>, <wbr>, <hr>, <pre>

<button> Button

current Category: Forms · Versions: HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <button> element represents a clickable button that the user can activate with a mouse, keyboard, finger or voice to perform an action. Unlike <input type="button">, a <button> may contain rich content: text, images, icons and other phrasing content.

Inside a <form>, a button submits the form by default (type="submit"). Set type="button" for buttons that only run JavaScript, and type="reset" to clear the form. Because the default is submit, forgetting type="button" is a frequent cause of forms submitting unexpectedly.

The button's form-related attributes (formaction, formmethod and so on) let one form have several submit buttons that send the data to different places or in different ways.

Syntax

<button type="button">label</button>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayinline-block
Content categoriesFlow content, phrasing content, interactive content, listed, labelable, submittable, form-associated, palpable
Permitted contentPhrasing content, but no interactive content and no descendant with the tabindex attribute
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts phrasing content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLButtonElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
typesubmit | reset | buttonsubmit (default) sends the form; reset restores default values; button does nothing by itself.HTML 4.01
nametextThe name sent with the form data when this button submits the form.HTML 4.01
valuetextThe value sent with the name.HTML 4.01
disabledbooleanThe button cannot be clicked or focused and is not submitted.HTML 4.01
autofocusbooleanFocus this button when the page loads (global in HTML5).HTML5
formform idAssociates the button with a form elsewhere in the document.HTML5
formactionURLOverrides the form's action for this button.HTML5
formenctypeapplication/x-www-form-urlencoded | multipart/form-data | text/plainOverrides the form's enctype.HTML5
formmethodget | post | dialogOverrides the form's method.HTML5
formnovalidatebooleanSkips validation when this button submits.HTML5
formtarget_self | _blank | _parent | _top | nameOverrides the form's target.HTML5
popovertargetelement idThe popover element this button shows, hides or toggles.Living Standard
popovertargetactionshow | hide | toggleWhat to do to the popover (default toggle).Living Standard
commandshow-modal | close | request-close | show-popover | hide-popover | toggle-popover | customExperimental: declarative action to perform on commandfor's target.Living Standard
commandforelement idExperimental: the element the command applies to.Living Standard

Examples

Three button types in a form

<form action="/save" method="post">
  <label>Name <input name="name"></label>
  <button type="submit">Save</button>
  <button type="reset">Clear</button>
  <button type="button" onclick="alert('Just a script')">Help</button>
</form>

Button with an icon

<button type="button">
  <img src="cart.svg" alt="" width="16" height="16">
  Add to cart
</button>

The image is decorative (empty alt) because the text already labels the button.

Two submit buttons going to different URLs

<form action="/save" method="post">
  <input name="title">
  <button>Save draft</button>
  <button formaction="/publish">Publish</button>
</form>

Toggling a popover without JavaScript

<button popovertarget="tip">Show tip</button>
<div id="tip" popover>Press Ctrl+S to save.</div>

Icon-only button with an accessible name

<button type="button" aria-label="Close">&times;</button>

Default browser CSS

button { display: inline-block; text-align: center; cursor: default; padding: 1px 6px; }

Accessibility

  • Buttons are focusable and activated with Enter or Space automatically; a <div onclick> is not.
  • Every button needs a text label or aria-label.
  • Use <button> for actions and <a> for navigation.
  • Do not remove the focus outline without providing an alternative.

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting type="button" and accidentally submitting the form.
  • Nesting an <a> or another <button> inside.
  • Using <div> or <span> styled as a button.
  • Using <input type="button"> when you need HTML content inside.

See also

<input>, <form>, <a>, <label>

<canvas> Graphics canvas

current Category: Scripting · Versions: HTML5

Description

The <canvas> element provides a blank, resolution-dependent bitmap surface on which JavaScript can draw graphics: shapes, text, images, animations, charts, games and image processing. The element itself does nothing; all drawing is done through the 2D context (getContext('2d')) or a WebGL / WebGPU context.

The width and height attributes set the size of the drawing surface in pixels (default 300 x 150). Setting the size with CSS instead scales the bitmap and makes it blurry; always set the attributes.

Content placed between the tags is fallback content shown by browsers that do not support canvas and read by screen readers, because the drawn pixels are invisible to assistive technology.

Syntax

<canvas id="c" width="400" height="300">fallback</canvas>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayinline
Content categoriesFlow content, phrasing content, embedded content, palpable content
Permitted contentTransparent, but no interactive content other than <a>, <button>, <input> of certain types and <select> with focusable descendants
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts phrasing content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLCanvasElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
widthpositive integerWidth of the bitmap in CSS pixels. Default 300.HTML5
heightpositive integerHeight of the bitmap in CSS pixels. Default 150.HTML5
moz-opaquebooleanFirefox only: hints that there is no transparency, for faster rendering.Non-standard

Examples

Drawing a rectangle and text

<canvas id="demo" width="300" height="150">
  A blue rectangle with the text Hello.
</canvas>
<script>
  const ctx = document.getElementById('demo').getContext('2d');
  ctx.fillStyle = '#1b6fd8';
  ctx.fillRect(10, 10, 120, 80);
  ctx.fillStyle = 'white';
  ctx.font = '20px sans-serif';
  ctx.fillText('Hello', 30, 60);
</script>

Simple animation

<canvas id="ball" width="200" height="100"></canvas>
<script>
  const c = document.getElementById('ball'), ctx = c.getContext('2d');
  let x = 0;
  function frame() {
    ctx.clearRect(0, 0, c.width, c.height);
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(x, 50, 10, 0, Math.PI * 2); ctx.fill();
    x = (x + 2) % c.width;
    requestAnimationFrame(frame);
  }
  frame();
</script>

Default browser CSS

canvas { display: inline; }

Accessibility

  • Canvas content is invisible to screen readers. Provide fallback content, an aria-label, or a text alternative next to it.
  • For charts, provide the data as a table too.
  • For diagrams and icons, SVG is usually more accessible than canvas.

Common mistakes

  • Sizing the canvas with CSS instead of width/height attributes.
  • Forgetting to clear before redrawing.
  • Using canvas for content that should be real HTML text.

See also

<svg>, <img>, <script>

<caption> Table caption

current Category: Table content · Versions: HTML 3.2, HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <caption> element gives a table a title or explanation. It must be the first child of the <table> element, and a table may have only one. By default it is displayed centred above the table; the CSS caption-side property can move it below.

A caption is important for accessibility: screen readers announce it when the user enters the table, so the user knows what the data is about before hearing the cells.

Syntax

<table>
  <caption>Title</caption>
  ...
</table>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displaytable-caption
Content categoriesNone
Permitted contentFlow content, but no descendant <table>
Permitted parents<table>, as its first child
Tag omissionEnd tag may be omitted if the caption is not followed by whitespace or a comment
DOM interfaceHTMLTableCaptionElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
aligntop | bottom | left | rightObsolete. Position of the caption. Use CSS caption-side and text-align.HTML 3.2

Examples

Table with caption

<table>
  <caption>Monthly sales, 2026</caption>
  <tr><th>Month</th><th>Sales</th></tr>
  <tr><td>January</td><td>120</td></tr>
  <tr><td>February</td><td>150</td></tr>
</table>

Caption below the table

<style>
  table { caption-side: bottom; }
</style>

Default browser CSS

caption { display: table-caption; text-align: center; }

Accessibility

  • Prefer <caption> over a heading above the table; it is programmatically linked to the table.
  • If the table is inside a <figure>, use <figcaption> instead of <caption>, not both.

Common mistakes

  • Placing <caption> after <tr>.
  • Multiple captions.

See also

<table>, <figcaption>

<center> Centred block (obsolete)

obsolete Category: Obsolete presentational · Versions: HTML 3.2, HTML 4.01 (deprecated); obsolete in HTML5

Description

The <center> element horizontally centred its content. It was introduced by Netscape, standardised in HTML 3.2, deprecated in HTML 4.01 and removed in HTML5. It is equivalent to <div align="center">. Use CSS instead: text-align: center for inline content, or margin: 0 auto with a width for blocks.

Syntax

<center>content</center>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayblock
Content categoriesFlow content (historical)
Permitted contentFlow content
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts flow content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLElement

Attributes

Only the global attributes and event handler attributes.

Examples

Replacement

<!-- Old -->
<center><h1>Welcome</h1></center>

<!-- New: centre text -->
<h1 style="text-align: center">Welcome</h1>

<!-- New: centre a block -->
<div style="width: 600px; margin: 0 auto">...</div>

Default browser CSS

center { display: block; text-align: -webkit-center; }

Common mistakes

  • Any use in new pages.

See also

<div>

<cite> Citation (title of a work)

current Category: Text-level semantics · Versions: HTML 2.0, HTML 3.2, HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <cite> element marks the title of a creative work that is being referenced: a book, article, film, song, painting, play, poem, website, legal case, computer program, and so on. Browsers render it in italics.

In HTML 4 <cite> could also mark the name of a person being quoted. The HTML Living Standard restricts it to titles of works; a person's name is not a title. In practice many pages use it for author names inside <blockquote> footers, and validators accept it.

Syntax

<cite>Title of Work</cite>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayinline
Content categoriesFlow content, phrasing content, palpable content
Permitted contentPhrasing content
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts phrasing content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLElement

Attributes

Only the global attributes and event handler attributes.

Examples

Book title

<p>I am reading <cite>The Pragmatic Programmer</cite> this month.</p>

Source of a quotation

<blockquote>
  <p>Any fool can write code that a computer can understand.</p>
  <footer>- Martin Fowler, <cite>Refactoring</cite></footer>
</blockquote>

Default browser CSS

cite { font-style: italic; }

Accessibility

  • No special announcement; the meaning is mainly for search engines and styling.

Common mistakes

  • Using <cite> for the URL of a source; that belongs in the cite attribute of <blockquote> or <q>.
  • Using <i> instead of <cite> for titles.

See also

<blockquote>, <q>, <i>

<code> Inline code

current Category: Text-level semantics · Versions: HTML 2.0, HTML 3.2, HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <code> element marks a fragment of computer code: an element name, a file name, a variable, a function, a command, or any other string a computer would recognise. Browsers render it in a monospace font.

For a multi-line block of code, wrap a <code> element in a <pre> element so that line breaks and indentation are preserved. The class attribute may be used to indicate the language, conventionally as language-xxx.

Syntax

<code>snippet</code>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayinline
Content categoriesFlow content, phrasing content, palpable content
Permitted contentPhrasing content
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts phrasing content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLElement

Attributes

Only the global attributes and event handler attributes.

Examples

Inline

<p>Use the <code>&lt;footer&gt;</code> element for the bottom of the page and save the file as <code>index.html</code>.</p>

Note that < and > inside code must still be written as &lt; and &gt;.

Code block

<pre><code class="language-css">footer {
  text-align: center;
  color: gray;
}</code></pre>

Default browser CSS

code { font-family: monospace; }

Accessibility

  • Some screen readers switch to reading punctuation when they encounter <code>.

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting to escape < and & inside code.
  • Using <code> alone for multi-line blocks (line breaks collapse without <pre>).

See also

<pre>, <kbd>, <samp>, <var>

<col> Table column

current Category: Table content · Versions: HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <col> element defines one or more columns in a table so that attributes and styles can be applied to whole columns at once. It is a void element and lives inside a <colgroup>. The span attribute makes one <col> stand for several consecutive columns.

Only a few CSS properties apply to columns: background, border, width and visibility. Text colour and font cannot be set on a column; set them on the cells.

Syntax

<colgroup>
  <col span="2" style="background: #eee">
</colgroup>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementYes (no closing tag)
Default displaytable-column
Content categoriesNone
Permitted contentNone (void element)
Permitted parents<colgroup> that does not have a span attribute
Tag omissionNo end tag
DOM interfaceHTMLTableColElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
spanpositive integerHow many consecutive columns this element represents. Default 1.HTML 4.01
alignleft | center | right | justify | charObsolete. Horizontal alignment of the cells. Use CSS text-align.HTML 4.01
bgcolorcolourObsolete. Background colour. Use CSS.HTML 4.01
charcharacterObsolete. Alignment character (for align=char).HTML 4.01
charoffnumberObsolete. Offset from the alignment character.HTML 4.01
valigntop | middle | bottom | baselineObsolete. Vertical alignment. Use CSS vertical-align.HTML 4.01
widthpixels or percentageObsolete. Column width. Use CSS width.HTML 4.01

Examples

Shading the first column and widening the last

<table>
  <colgroup>
    <col style="background: #f0f0f0">
    <col>
    <col style="width: 200px">
  </colgroup>
  <tr><th>Item</th><th>Qty</th><th>Notes</th></tr>
  <tr><td>Pen</td><td>3</td><td>Blue ink</td></tr>
</table>

Default browser CSS

col { display: table-column; }

Accessibility

  • Columns have no accessibility role; use <th scope="col"> for column headers.

Common mistakes

  • Placing <col> outside <colgroup> (browsers insert an implicit colgroup, but be explicit).
  • Trying to set font or colour on <col>.

See also

<colgroup>, <table>

<colgroup> Table column group

current Category: Table content · Versions: HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <colgroup> element groups one or more columns of a table for the purpose of styling and structure. It is placed inside <table> after the optional <caption> and before any <thead>, <tbody>, <tfoot> or <tr>. It either has a span attribute (and no children) or contains <col> elements.

Syntax

<colgroup span="2"></colgroup>
<!-- or -->
<colgroup><col><col></colgroup>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displaytable-column-group
Content categoriesNone
Permitted contentIf span is absent: zero or more <col> and <template>. If span is present: nothing
Permitted parents<table>, after <caption> and before <thead>, <tbody>, <tfoot> and <tr>
Tag omissionStart tag may be omitted if the first thing inside is a <col>; end tag may be omitted if not followed by whitespace or a comment
DOM interfaceHTMLTableColElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
spanpositive integerNumber of columns in the group when there are no <col> children.HTML 4.01
align, bgcolor, char, charoff, valign, widthvariousObsolete presentational attributes; see <col>.HTML 4.01

Examples

Two groups with different backgrounds

<table>
  <colgroup style="background: #e8f4ff"><col><col></colgroup>
  <colgroup style="background: #fff4e8"><col></colgroup>
  <tr><th>First</th><th>Last</th><th>Age</th></tr>
  <tr><td>Ahmed</td><td>Ali</td><td>20</td></tr>
</table>

Default browser CSS

colgroup { display: table-column-group; }

Common mistakes

  • Mixing a span attribute with <col> children.
  • Placing colgroup after tbody.

See also

<col>, <table>

<content> Shadow DOM insertion point (obsolete)

obsolete Category: Obsolete web components · Versions: Shadow DOM v0 (Chrome, 2013); obsolete

Description

The <content> element was part of the first, experimental version of Shadow DOM (v0). It marked the point where light DOM children were inserted into a shadow tree. It was replaced by the standardised <slot> element and removed from browsers in 2019.

Syntax

<content select=".title"></content>

<!-- Old -->
<content select=".title"></content>

<!-- New -->
<slot name="title"></slot>

  • Any use.

<slot>, <template>, <shadow>

<data> Machine-readable value

current Category: Text-level semantics · Versions: HTML5

Description

The <data> element links a piece of human-readable content with a machine-readable version of the same value held in the required value attribute. It is useful for product codes, numeric values written in words, sorting keys and similar cases where a script or search engine needs the exact value while the visitor sees a friendly form.

If the value is a date or time, use <time> instead, which has the same purpose but a defined format.

Syntax

<data value="machine value">human text</data>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayinline
Content categoriesFlow content, phrasing content, palpable content
Permitted contentPhrasing content
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts phrasing content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLDataElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
valuetextRequired. The machine-readable form of the content.HTML5

Examples

Product codes

<ul>
  <li><data value="SKU-1001">Blue notebook</data></li>
  <li><data value="SKU-1002">Red notebook</data></li>
</ul>

Numbers written in words

<p>We sold <data value="1000000">one million</data> copies.</p>

Default browser CSS

data { display: inline; }

Accessibility

  • The value attribute is not read by screen readers; the visible text must be understandable alone.

Common mistakes

  • Using <data> for dates; use <time>.

See also

<time>, <meter>

<datalist> Predefined options for an input

current Category: Forms · Versions: HTML5

Description

The <datalist> element contains a set of <option> elements that represent suggested values for an <input>. The input is linked to the list with its list attribute, which must equal the datalist's id. The user can pick a suggestion or type any other value, which makes it a combination of a text box and a drop-down list (a 'combobox').

The datalist itself is never displayed. Browsers show the suggestions in their own way, usually as a drop-down that filters as the user types. It works with text, search, url, tel, email, number, range, color, date and time inputs, though support for non-text types varies.

Syntax

<input list="id">
<datalist id="id">
  <option value="...">
</datalist>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displaynone
Content categoriesFlow content, phrasing content
Permitted contentEither phrasing content or zero or more <option> elements
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts phrasing content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLDataListElement

Attributes

Only the global attributes and event handler attributes.

Examples

Browser suggestions

<label for="browser">Favourite browser</label>
<input id="browser" name="browser" list="browsers">
<datalist id="browsers">
  <option value="Chrome">
  <option value="Firefox">
  <option value="Safari">
  <option value="Edge">
</datalist>

Labelled values

<input list="codes" name="country">
<datalist id="codes">
  <option value="EG">Egypt</option>
  <option value="SA">Saudi Arabia</option>
</datalist>

Some browsers show the label next to the value.

Tick marks on a range slider

<input type="range" min="0" max="100" list="ticks">
<datalist id="ticks">
  <option value="0">
  <option value="50">
  <option value="100">
</datalist>

Default browser CSS

datalist { display: none; }

Accessibility

  • Support in screen readers is inconsistent; consider a visible hint about available values.

Common mistakes

  • Mismatched id and list values.
  • Expecting the user to be limited to the options (use <select> for that).

See also

<input>, <option>, <select>

<dd> Description details

current Category: Text content · Versions: HTML 1, HTML 2.0, HTML 3.2, HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <dd> element provides the description, definition or value for the preceding term (<dt>) in a description list (<dl>). One term may have several <dd> elements, and several terms may share one <dd>. Browsers indent <dd> from the left by default.

Syntax

<dl>
  <dt>Term</dt>
  <dd>Description</dd>
</dl>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayblock
Content categoriesNone
Permitted contentFlow content
Permitted parents<dl> or <div> inside <dl>, after a <dt> or <dd>
Tag omissionEnd tag may be omitted if followed by another <dd> or <dt>, or if there is no more content in the parent
DOM interfaceHTMLElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
nowrapyes | noObsolete, non-standard. Prevented wrapping.IE

Examples

Glossary

<dl>
  <dt>HTML</dt>
  <dd>The language that structures web pages.</dd>
  <dt>CSS</dt>
  <dd>The language that styles web pages.</dd>
</dl>

Several descriptions for one term

<dl>
  <dt>Footer</dt>
  <dd>The bottom section of a page.</dd>
  <dd>An HTML element: &lt;footer&gt;.</dd>
</dl>

Default browser CSS

dd { display: block; margin-inline-start: 40px; }

Accessibility

  • Screen readers announce the list structure so users know which description belongs to which term.

Common mistakes

  • Using <dd> outside <dl>.
  • Using <dd> just for indentation.

See also

<dl>, <dt>

<del> Deleted text

current Category: Demarcating edits · Versions: HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <del> element marks text that has been deleted from a document, typically to show changes between versions ('track changes'). Browsers render it with a line through it. It is usually paired with <ins>, which marks inserted text.

<del> may contain either phrasing or flow content depending on where it is placed, but it should not cross the boundaries of block elements: to delete two paragraphs, wrap each in its own <del>.

For text that is no longer accurate but not part of an edit history (such as an old price), use <s> instead.

Syntax

<del datetime="YYYY-MM-DD" cite="URL">deleted text</del>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayinline
Content categoriesFlow content, phrasing content, palpable content
Permitted contentTransparent
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts phrasing content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLModElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
citeURLA URL explaining the change, such as a link to a change log or meeting minutes.HTML 4.01
datetimedate or date-time stringWhen the change was made, in the format YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ.HTML 4.01

Examples

Showing a correction

<p>The meeting is on <del datetime="2026-09-10">Monday</del> <ins datetime="2026-09-10">Tuesday</ins>.</p>

A completed to-do item

<ul>
  <li><del>Buy milk</del></li>
  <li>Write HTML</li>
</ul>

Default browser CSS

del { text-decoration: line-through; }

Accessibility

  • Most screen readers do not announce <del> by default. If the deletion is important, add visually hidden text such as 'deleted:' or use CSS ::before content with speak.

Common mistakes

  • Using <del> for a discounted price; use <s>.
  • Using <strike>, which is obsolete.

See also

<ins>, <s>, <strike>

<details> Disclosure widget

current Category: Interactive elements · Versions: HTML5 (5.1)

Description

The <details> element creates a disclosure widget: a box that can be opened and closed by the user to show or hide its content, with no JavaScript at all. The first child should be a <summary> element, which provides the always-visible label and the clickable arrow. If there is no <summary> the browser shows the word 'Details'.

The open attribute controls whether the content is visible. Adding or removing it from script opens or closes the widget, and the element fires a toggle event when its state changes. Giving several <details> the same name attribute makes them exclusive, like an accordion: opening one closes the others.

Syntax

<details>
  <summary>Label</summary>
  content
</details>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayblock
Content categoriesFlow content, sectioning root, interactive content, palpable content
Permitted contentOne <summary> followed by flow content
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts flow content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLDetailsElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
openbooleanThe details are visible. Absent means collapsed.HTML5
nametextGroups details elements so that only one in the group can be open at a time.Living Standard

Examples

FAQ item

<details>
  <summary>How do I centre a div?</summary>
  <p>Use <code>display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center;</code> on the parent.</p>
</details>

Open by default

<details open>
  <summary>Shipping information</summary>
  <p>Delivery takes 2-4 days.</p>
</details>

Accordion with the name attribute

<details name="faq"><summary>Question 1</summary><p>Answer 1</p></details>
<details name="faq"><summary>Question 2</summary><p>Answer 2</p></details>

Styling the arrow

<style>
  summary { cursor: pointer; font-weight: bold; }
  details[open] summary { color: #b90000; }
</style>

Default browser CSS

details { display: block; }

Accessibility

  • Fully keyboard accessible and announced as a button with expanded/collapsed state, out of the box.
  • Do not put interactive elements inside <summary>.

Common mistakes

  • Putting <summary> anywhere other than first.
  • Using open="false" (which still means open).

See also

<summary>, <dialog>

<dfn> Definition term

current Category: Text-level semantics · Versions: HTML 3.2, HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <dfn> element marks the term that is being defined in the surrounding sentence or paragraph. The nearest paragraph, description list group or section is the definition. Browsers render it in italics. If the element has a title attribute, that is the term being defined; if it contains an <abbr> with a title, the abbreviation's expansion is the term; otherwise the text content is the term.

Syntax

<dfn>term</dfn>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayinline
Content categoriesFlow content, phrasing content, palpable content
Permitted contentPhrasing content, but no <dfn> descendants
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts phrasing content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
titletextThe term being defined, if different from the content.HTML 4.01

Examples

Defining a term

<p>A <dfn>void element</dfn> is an element that cannot have any content and therefore has no closing tag.</p>

Linking to the definition

<p>A <dfn id="def-footer">footer</dfn> is the bottom section of a page.</p>
...
<p>Put the copyright in the <a href="#def-footer">footer</a>.</p>

Default browser CSS

dfn { font-style: italic; }

Accessibility

  • No special announcement; purely semantic.

Common mistakes

  • Using <dfn> on every occurrence of a term; use it only where it is defined.

See also

<abbr>, <dl>, <dt>

<dialog> Dialog box

current Category: Interactive elements · Versions: HTML 5.2 / Living Standard

Description

The <dialog> element represents a dialog box or other interactive component such as a confirmation prompt, an alert, a subwindow or a modal overlay. It is hidden by default and is shown with the open attribute or, preferably, with the JavaScript methods show() (non-modal) and showModal() (modal). A modal dialog blocks interaction with the rest of the page, is displayed on top of everything else, and can be closed with the Escape key.

A <form method="dialog"> inside the dialog closes it when submitted and sets the dialog's returnValue to the value of the submit button. The ::backdrop pseudo-element styles the dimmed area behind a modal dialog.

Syntax

<dialog id="d">...</dialog>
<script>document.getElementById('d').showModal()</script>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayblock
Content categoriesFlow content, sectioning root
Permitted contentFlow content
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts flow content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLDialogElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
openbooleanThe dialog is visible. Set it with showModal() rather than by hand so that focus and the backdrop work correctly.HTML 5.2
closedbyany | closerequest | noneWhich user actions close the dialog: any (Escape, backdrop click, close request), closerequest (Escape only, the default for modal), or none.Living Standard

Examples

Modal confirmation

<dialog id="confirm">
  <form method="dialog">
    <p>Delete this item?</p>
    <button value="cancel">Cancel</button>
    <button value="ok">Delete</button>
  </form>
</dialog>
<button onclick="document.getElementById('confirm').showModal()">Delete</button>
<script>
  const d = document.getElementById('confirm');
  d.addEventListener('close', () => console.log('User chose', d.returnValue));
</script>

Styling the backdrop

<style>
  dialog::backdrop { background: rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.6); }
  dialog { border: none; border-radius: 12px; padding: 24px; }
</style>

Default browser CSS

dialog { position: absolute; inset-inline: 0; width: fit-content; margin: auto; border: solid; padding: 1em; background: Canvas; color: CanvasText; }
dialog:not([open]) { display: none; }

Accessibility

  • showModal() traps focus inside the dialog and returns it when closed, which custom modals often get wrong.
  • Give the dialog an accessible name with aria-labelledby pointing at its heading.
  • Always provide a visible close button.

Common mistakes

  • Setting the open attribute directly for modals (no backdrop, no focus trap).
  • Nesting a dialog inside a button or link.

See also

<details>, <form>, <button>

<dir> Directory list (obsolete)

obsolete Category: Obsolete text content · Versions: HTML 1, HTML 2.0, HTML 3.2, HTML 4.01 (deprecated); obsolete in HTML5

Description

The <dir> element was a list of short items, intended to be shown in columns like a file directory listing. Browsers never implemented the columns and rendered it like <ul>. It was deprecated in HTML 4.01 and removed in HTML5. Use <ul> instead.

Syntax

<dir><li>item</li></dir>

Technical summary

Default displayblock
Content categoriesHistorical

Permitted parentsFlow content
Tag omissionNeither

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince

Replacement

<!-- Old -->
<dir><li>index.html</li><li>style.css</li></dir>

<!-- New -->

Default browser CSS
