Examples

Do not use

<!-- No modern replacement in HTML; see crypto.subtle.generateKey() -->

Common mistakes

  • Any use.

See also

<input>, <form>

<label> Form control label

current Category: Forms · Versions: HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <label> element gives a caption to a form control. Associating a label with a control has two big benefits: clicking the label focuses or toggles the control (a much larger click target for checkboxes and radio buttons), and screen readers announce the label when the control gets focus.

There are two ways to associate them. Explicit: give the control an id and set the label's for attribute to that id. Implicit: nest the control inside the label. You may combine both. A label may be associated with only one control, but a control may have several labels.

Labelable elements are <button>, <input> (except hidden), <meter>, <output>, <progress>, <select> and <textarea>.

Syntax

<label for="id">Text</label> <input id="id">
<!-- or -->
<label>Text <input></label>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayinline
Content categoriesFlow content, phrasing content, interactive content, form-associated, palpable content
Permitted contentPhrasing content, but no other <label> and at most one labelable descendant
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts phrasing content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLLabelElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
forid of a labelable elementThe control this label describes.HTML 4.01
formform idObsolete in the Living Standard; was meant to associate the label with a form.HTML5 (removed)

Examples

Explicit association

<label for="city">City</label>
<input id="city" name="city">

Implicit association (wrapping)

<label>
  <input type="checkbox" name="news"> Send me the newsletter
</label>

Clicking anywhere on the text toggles the box.

Labels stacked above fields

<style>
  label { display: block; margin-bottom: 4px; font-weight: 600; }
  input, select, textarea { display: block; width: 100%; margin-bottom: 16px; }
</style>

Required-field indicator

<label for="n">Name <span aria-hidden="true">*</span></label>
<input id="n" name="n" required aria-required="true">

Default browser CSS

label { cursor: default; }

Accessibility

  • A label is the correct way to name a control; aria-label is a fallback when no visible text is possible.
  • Do not put headings or interactive elements inside a label.
  • Keep the label visible; placeholder text is not a label.

Common mistakes

  • for pointing to a name instead of an id.
  • Two controls inside one label.
  • Using <label> for text that is not a caption for a control.

See also

<input>, <select>, <textarea>, <button>, <fieldset>, <legend>

<legend> Fieldset caption

current Category: Forms · Versions: HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <legend> element provides a caption for its parent <fieldset>. It must be the first child of the fieldset. Browsers draw it on top of the fieldset's border. Screen readers announce the legend together with the label of each control inside the group, which is why fieldset/legend is the recommended way to caption groups of radio buttons or checkboxes.

Syntax

<fieldset>
  <legend>Caption</legend>
  ...
</fieldset>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayblock
Content categoriesNone
Permitted contentPhrasing content and optionally heading content
Permitted parents<fieldset>, as its first child
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLLegendElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
alignleft | center | right | top | bottomObsolete. Use CSS.HTML 4.01

Examples

Captioned group

<fieldset>
  <legend>Contact preference</legend>
  <label><input type="radio" name="c" value="email"> Email</label>
  <label><input type="radio" name="c" value="phone"> Phone</label>
</fieldset>

Legend containing a heading

<fieldset>
  <legend><h2>Billing address</h2></legend>
  ...
</fieldset>

Allowed since the Living Standard; keeps the document outline while still captioning the group.

Default browser CSS

legend { display: block; padding-inline: 2px; }

Accessibility

  • Keep legends short; they are repeated by some screen readers for every control in the group.

Common mistakes

  • Legend not first in the fieldset.
  • Using legend outside a fieldset.

See also

<fieldset>, <label>

<li> List item

current Category: Text content · Versions: HTML 1, HTML 2.0, HTML 3.2, HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <li> element represents one item in a list. It must be contained in an ordered list (<ol>), an unordered list (<ul>) or a menu (<menu>). In ordered lists the value attribute sets the number of the item, and subsequent items continue counting from it.

A list item may contain any flow content: paragraphs, images, nested lists, even tables. To nest a list, place the inner <ul> or <ol> inside the <li>, not between two <li> elements.

Syntax

<ul>
  <li>Item</li>
</ul>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displaylist-item
Content categoriesNone
Permitted contentFlow content
Permitted parents<ul>, <ol>, <menu>
Tag omissionEnd tag may be omitted if followed by another <li> or if there is no more content in the parent
DOM interfaceHTMLLIElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
valueintegerIn <ol>: the ordinal number of this item. Following items count from it.HTML 3.2
type1 | a | A | i | I | disc | circle | squareObsolete. Bullet or numbering style for this item. Use CSS list-style-type.HTML 3.2

Examples

Unordered list

<ul>
  <li>Milk</li>
  <li>Bread</li>
  <li>Eggs</li>
</ul>

Displays with bullets.

Ordered list with a custom start value

<ol>
  <li value="10">Tenth</li>
  <li>Eleventh</li>
  <li>Twelfth</li>
</ol>

Nested list (correct)

<ul>
  <li>Fruit
    <ul>
      <li>Apples</li>
      <li>Oranges</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li>Vegetables</li>
</ul>

The inner list is inside the first <li>.

Rich list items

<ol>
  <li>
    <h3>Step one</h3>
    <p>Open your editor.</p>
    <img src="editor.png" alt="Editor window" width="300" height="200">
  </li>
</ol>

Horizontal menu with CSS

<style>
  nav ul { list-style: none; padding: 0; margin: 0; display: flex; gap: 16px; }
</style>
<nav><ul><li><a href="/">Home</a></li><li><a href="/shop">Shop</a></li></ul></nav>

Default browser CSS

li { display: list-item; text-align: match-parent; }

Accessibility

  • Screen readers announce the number of items in a list and the position of each; this is lost if list-style: none is combined with display: contents in some browsers, or if you fake a list with <br>.

Common mistakes

  • Placing <li> directly in <div> or <body>.
  • Nesting a list between <li> elements rather than inside one.
  • Using <br> instead of separate items.

See also

<ul>, <ol>, <menu>, <dl>

<link> External resource link

current Category: Document metadata · Versions: HTML 2.0, HTML 3.2, HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <link> element specifies a relationship between the current document and an external resource. By far its most common use is loading a CSS style sheet (rel="stylesheet"), but it is also used for site icons (rel="icon"), web app manifests, preloading and prefetching resources, canonical URLs for search engines, alternate language versions, RSS feeds and more. It is a void element and normally lives in <head>, though body-ok link types such as stylesheet may appear in <body>.

The rel attribute is required and determines everything else. The media attribute lets a style sheet apply only to certain devices or screen sizes; the browser still downloads it but with low priority. The full list of link types is in Part 9.

Syntax

<link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementYes (no closing tag)
Default displaynone
Content categoriesMetadata content; flow and phrasing content if itemprop or a body-ok rel is present
Permitted contentNone (void element)
Permitted parents<head>; <body> for body-ok types
Tag omissionNo end tag
DOM interfaceHTMLLinkElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
relspace-separated link typesRequired. Relationship: stylesheet, icon, apple-touch-icon, manifest, canonical, alternate, preload, prefetch, preconnect, dns-prefetch, modulepreload, prerender, author, license, help, next, prev, search, pingback, privacy-policy, terms-of-service, expect.HTML 2.0
hrefURLThe resource URL.HTML 2.0
typeMIME typeThe type of the resource, for example text/css, image/png, application/rss+xml.HTML 2.0
mediamedia queryApply the style sheet only when the query matches: screen, print, (max-width: 600px), (prefers-color-scheme: dark).HTML 4.01
asaudio | document | embed | fetch | font | image | object | script | style | track | video | workerWith rel=preload or modulepreload: the type of content being loaded, so the browser can prioritise it correctly.Living Standard
crossoriginanonymous | use-credentialsCORS mode for the request. Required when preloading fonts.HTML5
hreflanglanguage tagLanguage of the linked resource (with rel=alternate).HTML 4.01
sizesany or WxH listIcon sizes, for example 16x16 32x32 or any (for SVG).HTML5
titletextFor style sheets: the name of an alternate style sheet set. For feeds: the feed title.HTML 2.0
integrityhashSubresource Integrity hash; the browser refuses the file if it does not match.SRI spec
referrerpolicyreferrer policyReferrer to send when fetching.HTML5
fetchpriorityhigh | low | autoDownload priority hint.Living Standard
blockingrenderBlock rendering until the resource is loaded (for stylesheets/preloads/expect).Living Standard
disabledbooleanFor style sheets: do not apply.HTML5
imagesrcset / imagesizessrcset / sizes syntaxWith rel=preload as=image: responsive image candidates.Living Standard
colorcolourWith rel=mask-icon (Safari pinned tab).Non-standard
charsetencodingObsolete. Character set of the resource.HTML 4.01
revlink typesObsolete. Reverse relationship.HTML 4.01
targetbrowsing contextObsolete on link.HTML 4.01

Examples

Style sheets

<link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="print.css" media="print">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="dark.css" media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)">

Icons

<link rel="icon" href="favicon.ico" sizes="32x32">
<link rel="icon" href="icon.svg" type="image/svg+xml">
<link rel="apple-touch-icon" href="apple-touch-icon.png">
<link rel="manifest" href="manifest.webmanifest">

Performance hints

<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin>
<link rel="preload" href="hero.jpg" as="image" fetchpriority="high">
<link rel="preload" href="font.woff2" as="font" type="font/woff2" crossorigin>
<link rel="prefetch" href="next-page.html">

SEO and alternates

<link rel="canonical" href="https://example.com/books/html">
<link rel="alternate" hreflang="ar" href="https://example.com/ar/books/html">
<link rel="alternate" type="application/rss+xml" title="Blog feed" href="/feed.xml">

Google Fonts

<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com">
<link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Cairo:wght@400;700&display=swap" rel="stylesheet">

Default browser CSS

link { display: none; }

Accessibility

  • Alternate style sheets (rel="alternate stylesheet" title="High contrast") can offer accessible themes in browsers that support switching.

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting rel.
  • Using <link> to make a hyperlink (that is <a>).
  • Wrong path to the CSS file (check the browser's network tab).
  • Writing </link>.

See also

<style>, <a>, <script>, <meta>, <head>

<listing> Listing (obsolete)

obsolete Category: Obsolete text content · Versions: HTML 1, HTML 2.0 (deprecated); obsolete

Description

The <listing> element, from the 1991 tag set, displayed its content in a monospace font exactly as written, like <pre> but originally at a smaller size and without interpreting markup. It was deprecated already in HTML 2.0 and removed in HTML 3.2. Use <pre>, optionally with <code>.

Syntax

<listing>text</listing>

Void elementNo
Default displayblock
Content categoriesHistorical
Permitted contentText
Permitted parentsFlow content
Tag omissionNeither
DOM interfaceHTMLPreElement

Attributes

Only the global attributes and event handler attributes.

Examples

Replacement

<pre><code>line 1
line 2</code></pre>

Default browser CSS

listing { display: block; font-family: monospace; white-space: pre; margin: 1em 0; }

Common mistakes

  • Any use.

See also

<pre>, <xmp>, <plaintext>

<main> Main content

current Category: Content sectioning · Versions: HTML 5.1 (2016)

Description

The <main> element represents the dominant content of the <body>: the content that is directly related to, or expands upon, the central topic of the page or the central function of the application. It excludes content repeated across pages such as the site header, navigation, sidebars, search box, logo and footer.

A document must not have more than one visible <main>; additional <main> elements are allowed only if all but one carry the hidden attribute. <main> must not be a descendant of <article>, <aside>, <footer>, <header> or <nav>. It is exposed as the 'main' landmark, which lets screen reader users skip straight to the content, and it is the natural target for a 'skip to content' link.

Syntax

<main>...</main>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayblock
Content categoriesFlow content, palpable content
Permitted contentFlow content
Permitted parents<html>, <body>, <div>, <form> without an accessible name, and autonomous custom elements; not inside article, aside, footer, header or nav
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLElement

Attributes

Only the global attributes and event handler attributes.

Examples

Page structure with skip link

<body>
  <a href="#content" class="skip">Skip to main content</a>
  <header>...</header>
  <nav>...</nav>
  <main id="content">
    <h1>Page title</h1>
    <p>The unique content of this page.</p>
  </main>
  <aside>...</aside>
  <footer>...</footer>
</body>

Visually hidden skip link that appears on focus

<style>
  .skip { position: absolute; left: -999px; }
  .skip:focus { left: 8px; top: 8px; background: #fff; padding: 8px; }
</style>

Single-page app views

<main id="home">Home view</main>
<main id="cart" hidden>Cart view</main>

Only one is visible at a time.

Default browser CSS

main { display: block; }

Accessibility

  • The 'main' landmark is one of the most used shortcuts in screen readers; every page should have exactly one.

Common mistakes

  • Two visible mains.
  • Placing main inside article or nav.
  • Putting the header and footer inside main.

See also

<header>, <footer>, <nav>, <aside>, <article>, <section>

<map> Image map

current Category: Image and multimedia · Versions: HTML 3.2, HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <map> element, together with <area> elements, defines a client-side image map: an image with several clickable regions each linking to a different destination. The map is connected to an <img> through the img's usemap attribute, which must be # followed by the map's name.

Syntax

<map name="n">
  <area ...>
</map>
<img usemap="#n" ...>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayinline
Content categoriesFlow content, phrasing content, palpable content
Permitted contentTransparent
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts phrasing content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLMapElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
nametextRequired. The map's name, without #, unique among maps. If id is also given it must have the same value.HTML 3.2

Examples

Navigation image with two regions

<img src="banner.png" alt="Shop banner" usemap="#banner" width="600" height="100">
<map name="banner">
  <area shape="rect" coords="0,0,300,100" href="books.html" alt="Books">
  <area shape="rect" coords="300,0,600,100" href="deals.html" alt="Deals">
</map>

Default browser CSS

map { display: inline; }

Accessibility

  • Each area needs alt text. Provide an equivalent text list of links if the map is complex.

Common mistakes

  • usemap without #.
  • Map name mismatching.
  • Coordinates for a different image size than displayed.

See also

<area>, <img>

<mark> Highlighted (marked) text

current Category: Text-level semantics · Versions: HTML5

Description

The <mark> element represents text that is marked or highlighted for reference because of its relevance in the current context. Typical uses: highlighting the search terms in a page of results, or drawing attention to a passage in a quotation that the current text discusses. Browsers render it with a yellow background, like a highlighter pen.

Do not confuse it with <strong> (importance) or <em> (emphasis). <mark> is about relevance to the reader's current activity, not about the author's intent.

Syntax

<mark>text</mark>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayinline
Content categoriesFlow content, phrasing content, palpable content
Permitted contentPhrasing content
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts phrasing content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLElement

Attributes

Only the global attributes and event handler attributes.

Examples

Search results

<p>Results for 'footer': ... the <mark>footer</mark> element represents the <mark>footer</mark> of its section ...</p>

Highlighting part of a quotation

<blockquote><p>Any tag you learn is <mark>a tool you keep</mark>.</p></blockquote>
<p>The phrase 'a tool you keep' is the key idea.</p>

Custom colour

<style>
  mark { background: #ffe58a; color: inherit; padding: 0 2px; }
</style>

Default browser CSS

mark { background-color: yellow; color: black; }

Accessibility

  • Not announced by default; if the highlight matters, add visually hidden text such as '[highlight start]'.

Common mistakes

  • Using <mark> for decorative colour.
  • Using <mark> instead of <strong>.

See also

<strong>, <em>, <span>

<marquee> Scrolling text (obsolete)

obsolete Category: Obsolete presentational · Versions: Internet Explorer 2 (1995), never standard; obsolete in HTML5 (but its behaviour is specified for compatibility)

Description

The <marquee> element scrolled its content horizontally or vertically across the screen. It was a Microsoft extension that became infamous alongside Netscape's <blink>. HTML5 lists it as obsolete but, because so many old pages use it, browsers still implement it. Moving text is hard to read and distracting; if you need an animation, use CSS animations with a pause control and respect the prefers-reduced-motion media query.

Syntax

<marquee>text</marquee>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayinline-block
Content categoriesHistorical
Permitted contentFlow content
Permitted parentsFlow content
Tag omissionNeither
DOM interfaceHTMLMarqueeElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
behaviorscroll | slide | alternateScrolling style.IE
directionleft | right | up | downScroll direction.IE
loopinteger | -1Repeat count.IE
scrollamountpixelsDistance per step.IE
scrolldelaymsDelay between steps.IE
truespeedbooleanAllow delays under 60 ms.IE
bgcolorcolourBackground.IE
width / heightsizeSize.IE
hspace / vspacepixelsMargins.IE

Examples

CSS replacement

<style>
  @keyframes slide { from { transform: translateX(100%); } to { transform: translateX(-100%); } }
  .ticker { white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; }
  .ticker span { display: inline-block; animation: slide 12s linear infinite; }
  @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ticker span { animation: none; } }
</style>
<div class="ticker"><span>Breaking news...</span></div>

Default browser CSS

marquee { display: inline-block; text-align: initial; }

Accessibility

  • Moving text violates WCAG unless it can be paused.

Common mistakes

  • Any use.

See also

<blink>

<math> MathML root

current Category: Embedded content (MathML) · Versions: HTML5 (inline MathML)

Description

The <math> element is the top-level element of MathML (Mathematical Markup Language), which can be written directly inside HTML5 documents to display mathematical formulas. Inside <math> you use MathML elements such as <mi> (identifier), <mn> (number), <mo> (operator), <mrow> (group), <mfrac> (fraction), <msup> (superscript), <msqrt> (square root) and <mtable>. All modern browsers support MathML Core.

Syntax

<math>
  <mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn>
</math>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayinline
Content categoriesFlow content, phrasing content, embedded content, palpable content
Permitted contentMathML elements
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts phrasing content
Tag omissionNeither
DOM interfaceMathMLElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
displayblock | inlineWhether the formula is a block on its own line or inline in text.MathML
xmlnshttp://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathMLNamespace; optional in HTML.MathML

Examples

Quadratic formula

<math display="block">
  <mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo>
  <mfrac>
    <mrow><mo>-</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>&#xB1;</mo><msqrt><msup><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>a</mi><mi>c</mi></msqrt></mrow>
    <mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow>
  </mfrac>
</math>

Inline formula

<p>The area of a circle is <math><mi>&#x3C0;</mi><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>.</p>

Default browser CSS

math { display: inline; math-style: compact; }
math[display=block] { display: block math; math-style: normal; }

Accessibility

  • MathML is read by modern screen readers as mathematics; images of formulas are not.

Common mistakes

  • Writing formulas as plain text or images.
  • Forgetting display="block" for standalone equations.

See also

<svg>, <canvas>

<menu> Menu (toolbar list)

current Category: Text content · Versions: HTML 1, HTML 2.0, HTML 3.2, HTML 4.01 (deprecated), HTML5 (redefined)

Description

The <menu> element is a semantic alternative to <ul> for a list of commands or actions, such as a toolbar of buttons. Each command is an <li> containing a <button> or similar control. Browsers render it identically to <ul>.

Its history is long: in HTML 1 and 2 it was a compact list like <dir>; HTML 4.01 deprecated it; early HTML5 drafts turned it into a rich context-menu system with type="context" and <menuitem> children, which no browser except Firefox implemented and which was removed; the current definition is simply 'an unordered list of interactive items'.

Syntax

<menu>
  <li><button>Action</button></li>
</menu>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayblock
Content categoriesFlow content; palpable if it has at least one <li>
Permitted contentZero or more <li>, <script>, <template>
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts flow content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLMenuElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
compactbooleanObsolete. Compact rendering.HTML 2.0
typecontext | toolbar | listObsolete. From the abandoned HTML5 context menu design.HTML5 draft (removed)
labeltextObsolete. Menu label (context menus).HTML5 draft (removed)

Examples

Editor toolbar

<menu>
  <li><button onclick="copy()">Copy</button></li>
  <li><button onclick="cut()">Cut</button></li>
  <li><button onclick="paste()">Paste</button></li>
</menu>

Horizontal toolbar styling

<style>
  menu { display: flex; gap: 8px; list-style: none; padding: 0; margin: 0; }
</style>

Default browser CSS

menu { display: block; list-style-type: disc; margin: 1em 0; padding-inline-start: 40px; }

Accessibility

  • Exposed as a list, the same as <ul>. Add role="toolbar" if the list is a real toolbar with arrow-key navigation.

Common mistakes

  • Expecting native context menus from type="context".
  • Using <menu> for navigation links (use <nav><ul>).

See also

<ul>, <li>, <button>, <nav>, <menuitem>

<menuitem> Menu item (obsolete)

obsolete Category: Obsolete interactive · Versions: HTML5 draft (Firefox only); removed 2017

Description

The <menuitem> element represented a command in a <menu type="context">, letting a page add custom items to the browser's right-click menu. Only Firefox implemented it; it was removed from the standard in 2017 and from Firefox in 2020. Build custom menus with lists, buttons and JavaScript (or the popover attribute) instead.

Syntax

<menuitem label="Refresh" onclick="...">

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementYes (no closing tag)
Default displaynone
Content categoriesHistorical
Permitted contentNone
Permitted parents<menu>
Tag omissionNo end tag
DOM interfaceHTMLUnknownElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
labeltextItem text.HTML5 draft
typecommand | checkbox | radioKind of item.HTML5 draft
iconURLIcon image.HTML5 draft
checked, disabled, default, radiogroup, commandvariousState and grouping.HTML5 draft

Examples

Replacement

<button popovertarget="m">Options</button>
<menu id="m" popover>
  <li><button>Refresh</button></li>
</menu>

Common mistakes

  • Any use.

See also

<menu>, <button>

<meta> Metadata

current Category: Document metadata · Versions: HTML 2.0, HTML 3.2, HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <meta> element represents metadata about the document that cannot be expressed by <title>, <base>, <link>, <style> or <script>. It is a void element placed in <head>. Depending on which attributes are present it does one of four things: declares the character encoding (charset); provides document-level metadata as a name/content pair (name); simulates an HTTP response header (http-equiv); or supplies microdata (itemprop).

The most important meta tags on every page are charset and viewport. Other frequently used names are description (shown in search results), robots, author, theme-color and the Open Graph (property="og:...") and Twitter card tags used when a page is shared on social networks. Part 9 contains the full list of standard meta names.

Syntax

<meta charset="utf-8">
<meta name="description" content="...">

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementYes (no closing tag)
Default displaynone
Content categoriesMetadata content; flow and phrasing content if itemprop is present
Permitted contentNone (void element)
Permitted parents<head>; <noscript> in head; anywhere if itemprop is present
Tag omissionNo end tag
DOM interfaceHTMLMetaElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
charsetutf-8Declares the document's character encoding. The only valid value in HTML5 is utf-8 (case-insensitive). Must be in the first 1024 bytes.HTML5
namemetadata nameThe kind of metadata: application-name, author, description, generator, keywords, referrer, theme-color, color-scheme, viewport, robots, googlebot, creator, publisher, and more.HTML 2.0
contenttextThe value for name or http-equiv. Required with them.HTML 2.0
http-equivcontent-type | default-style | refresh | content-security-policy | x-ua-compatiblePragma directive that acts like an HTTP header.HTML 2.0
mediamedia queryWith name=theme-color: apply only when the query matches.Living Standard
propertytextNot in the HTML standard but universally used for RDFa / Open Graph tags such as og:title.RDFa
itemproptextMicrodata property name.HTML5 microdata
schemetextObsolete. Interpretation scheme for content.HTML 4.01

Examples

The essential pair

<meta charset="utf-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">

Without the viewport tag, phones render the page as if it were 980px wide and shrink it.

Search engine metadata

<meta name="description" content="Buy PDF books in Arabic and English; pay with mobile wallet and download instantly.">
<meta name="robots" content="index, follow">
<meta name="author" content="Book Store team">

Social sharing (Open Graph and Twitter)

<meta property="og:title" content="Learn HTML">
<meta property="og:description" content="A complete reference.">
<meta property="og:image" content="https://example.com/cover.jpg">
<meta property="og:url" content="https://example.com/html">
<meta name="twitter:card" content="summary_large_image">

Theme colour and colour scheme

<meta name="theme-color" content="#e60000">
<meta name="theme-color" content="#111" media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)">
<meta name="color-scheme" content="light dark">

Redirect after 5 seconds (use sparingly)

<meta http-equiv="refresh" content="5; url=https://example.com/new-page">

Content Security Policy

<meta http-equiv="content-security-policy" content="default-src 'self'; img-src https:">

Old HTML 4 encoding declaration

<!-- HTML 4.01 -->
<meta http-equiv="Content-Type" content="text/html; charset=utf-8">

<!-- HTML5 -->
<meta charset="utf-8">

Default browser CSS

meta { display: none; }

Accessibility

  • Never use <meta name="viewport" content="user-scalable=no"> or maximum-scale=1; it stops users zooming and fails WCAG.
  • Automatic refresh/redirect disorients users; prefer server-side redirects.

Common mistakes

  • Placing charset after other content or after 1024 bytes.
  • Using keywords meta (ignored by search engines since 2009).
  • Writing </meta>.

See also

<head>, <title>, <link>, <base>

<meter> Scalar measurement (gauge)

current Category: Forms · Versions: HTML5

Description

The <meter> element represents a scalar measurement within a known range, or a fractional value: disk usage, the relevance of a search result, password strength, a score out of ten, temperature within safe limits. Browsers render it as a gauge bar whose colour changes depending on whether the value is in the optimum, suboptimal or bad region defined by low, high and optimum.

Do not use <meter> for progress of a task; that is what <progress> is for. And do not use it for values with no known maximum (such as a bank balance) because the gauge needs a range.

Syntax

<meter value="0.6">60%</meter>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayinline-block
Content categoriesFlow content, phrasing content, labelable, palpable content
Permitted contentPhrasing content, but no <meter> descendants
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts phrasing content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLMeterElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
valuenumberRequired. The current value, between min and max.HTML5
minnumberLower bound of the range. Default 0.HTML5
maxnumberUpper bound. Default 1.HTML5
lownumberUpper bound of the 'low' region.HTML5
highnumberLower bound of the 'high' region.HTML5
optimumnumberThe ideal value. Determines which region is shown as good (green) versus bad (red/yellow).HTML5
formform idAssociated form (for labelling purposes).HTML5

Examples

Disk usage

<label for="disk">Disk usage</label>
<meter id="disk" value="70" min="0" max="100" low="60" high="85" optimum="20">70%</meter>

Because optimum is low, 70 (above low) shows in yellow and anything above 85 in red.

Score out of ten

<p>Rating: <meter value="8" min="0" max="10">8 out of 10</meter></p>

Fraction

<meter value="0.25">25%</meter>

Default range 0 to 1.

Default browser CSS

meter { display: inline-block; appearance: auto; }

Accessibility

  • Provide the value as text inside the element or in a label; the bar alone is not enough.
  • Always label the meter.

Common mistakes

  • Using it as a progress bar.
  • Omitting value.
  • Value outside min-max (it is clamped).

See also

<progress>, <output>, <input>

<multicol> Multi-column text (non-standard, obsolete)

obsolete Category: Obsolete presentational · Versions: Netscape 3 only; never standard

Description

The <multicol> element split its content into newspaper-style columns. It existed only in Netscape Navigator 3 and 4 and was never standardised. Use the CSS multi-column properties (column-count, column-width, column-gap) instead.

Syntax

<multicol cols="3" gutter="20">text</multicol>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayblock
Content categoriesHistorical
Permitted contentFlow content
Permitted parentsFlow content
Tag omissionNeither

In addition to the global and event attributes:

gutterpixelsSpace between columns.Netscape
widthpixelsColumn width.Netscape

Examples

CSS replacement

<div style="column-count: 3; column-gap: 20px">Long text...</div>

Common mistakes

  • Any use.

See also

<div>

<nav> Navigation section

current Category: Content sectioning · Versions: HTML5

Description

The <nav> element represents a section of the page whose purpose is to provide navigation links, either within the current document or to other documents. Typical uses are the main site menu, a table of contents, breadcrumbs, pagination and 'previous/next' links.

Not every group of links needs a <nav>; it is intended for major navigation blocks. The list of links in a page footer, for example, is usually fine as a plain list, although a <nav> there is also acceptable. A page can have several <nav> elements; give each an aria-label so screen reader users can tell them apart. Links inside a <nav> are conventionally wrapped in a <ul>.

Syntax

<nav>
  <ul>
    <li><a href="...">Link</a></li>
  </ul>
</nav>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayblock
Content categoriesFlow content, sectioning content, palpable content
Permitted contentFlow content
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts flow content, but not <address>
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLElement

Attributes

Only the global attributes and event handler attributes.

Examples

Main site navigation

<nav aria-label="Main">
  <ul>
    <li><a href="/" aria-current="page">Home</a></li>
    <li><a href="/books">Books</a></li>
    <li><a href="/about">About</a></li>
    <li><a href="/contact">Contact</a></li>
  </ul>
</nav>

Breadcrumbs

<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">
  <ol>
    <li><a href="/">Home</a></li>
    <li><a href="/books">Books</a></li>
    <li aria-current="page">Learn HTML</li>
  </ol>
</nav>

Horizontal menu CSS

<style>
  nav ul { display: flex; gap: 24px; list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; }
  nav a { text-decoration: none; color: #1b2431; font-weight: 600; }
  nav a[aria-current="page"] { border-bottom: 2px solid #e60000; }
</style>

Table of contents

<nav aria-label="On this page">
  <h2>Contents</h2>
  <ol>
    <li><a href="#intro">Introduction</a></li>
    <li><a href="#tags">Tags</a></li>
  </ol>
</nav>

Default browser CSS

nav { display: block; }

Accessibility

  • Exposed as the 'navigation' landmark.
  • Label multiple navs with aria-label.
  • Mark the current page with aria-current="page".
  • Provide a skip link so keyboard users can bypass long menus.

Common mistakes

  • Wrapping every link group in <nav>.
  • Putting non-navigation content inside.
  • Not using a list for the links.

See also

<header>, <footer>, <a>, <ul>, <menu>, <main>

<nextid> Next identifier (HTML 1 editor hint)

obsolete Category: Obsolete · Versions: HTML 1 / HTML 2.0 (RFC 1866); removed in HTML 3.2

Description

The <nextid> element was used by the very first HTML editors (the NeXT-based editor written at CERN) to remember the next automatically generated anchor name, so that the editor could continue numbering anchors (z1, z2, z3...) when a document was reopened. It carried a single attribute, n, holding that name. It had no visible effect and was placed in the <head>.

It was already marked as an editor-only feature in HTML 2.0 and was dropped from HTML 3.2. Modern browsers ignore it entirely. It is documented here only for completeness, because it appears in the earliest HTML specifications and in archived pages from 1991 to 1995.

Syntax

<nextid n="z12">

Default displaynone
Content categoriesNone (obsolete)
Permitted contentNone (void element)
Permitted parents<head> (historically)
Tag omissionNo end tag
DOM interfaceHTMLUnknownElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
nText (anchor name)The next anchor name the editor should generate.HTML 1

Examples

Historical usage

<head>
  <title>Welcome</title>
  <nextid n="z5">
</head>

Ignored by all modern browsers.

Default browser CSS

nextid { display: none; }

Common mistakes

  • Any use in a new document.

See also

<head>, <isindex>, <listing>

obsolete Category: Obsolete presentational · Versions: Netscape / IE extension, never standard; obsolete

Description

The <nobr> element prevented the browser from wrapping its text onto a new line. It was never standardised. Use CSS white-space: nowrap instead.

  • Any use.

<wbr>, <br>

<noembed> Fallback for embed (obsolete)

Description

The <noembed> element provided fallback content for browsers that did not support <embed>. It was never standard and is obsolete. Use <object> with fallback content, or <video>/<audio> with fallback content inside them.

  • Any use.

<noframes> Fallback for frames (obsolete)

Description

The <noframes> element contained content to display in browsers that did not support frames. It became obsolete together with <frameset> and <frame> in HTML5.

  • Any use.

<noscript> Fallback when scripting is disabled

current Category: Scripting · Versions: HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <noscript> element defines content to be shown only if scripting is disabled in the browser or the browser does not support scripting. When scripting is enabled the content is ignored entirely (in fact the parser treats it as raw text). It may be used in <head> (containing only <link>, <style> and <meta>) and in <body>.

Common uses: a warning that the site requires JavaScript, a non-JavaScript version of a widget, or a <link> to a style sheet that only applies when scripts are off. Tracking pixels from analytics services also use it as a fallback.

Syntax

<noscript>fallback content</noscript>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayinline
Content categoriesMetadata content, flow content, phrasing content
Permitted contentIn <head>: <link>, <style>, <meta>. In <body>: transparent content, but no <noscript> descendants
Permitted parents<head> and any element that accepts phrasing content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLElement

Attributes

Only the global attributes and event handler attributes.

Examples

Warning message

<noscript>
  <p><strong>This page works best with JavaScript enabled.</strong></p>
</noscript>

Non-JavaScript style sheet

<head>
  <noscript><link rel="stylesheet" href="no-js.css"></noscript>
</head>

Image fallback for lazy-loaded pictures

<img data-src="big.jpg" alt="Sunset" class="lazy">
<noscript><img src="big.jpg" alt="Sunset"></noscript>

noscript { display: inline; }

Accessibility

  • Do not assume screen reader users have scripts disabled; almost all use JavaScript-enabled browsers.

Common mistakes

  • Nesting noscript.
  • Expecting noscript content to appear when a script merely fails to load (it appears only when scripting is off).

See also

<script>, <template>

<object> External object

current Category: Embedded content · Versions: HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <object> element represents an external resource, treated as an image, a nested browsing context (like an iframe) or a resource handled by a plug-in, depending on its type. It was introduced in HTML 4.01 as a universal replacement for <img>, <applet> and <embed>. Unlike <embed>, it accepts fallback content between its tags, shown if the resource cannot be displayed, and it may contain <param> elements (now obsolete) that pass parameters to plug-ins.

Today <object> is mainly used to embed PDFs and SVG images with fallback. For video, audio and other pages, the dedicated elements are better.

Syntax

<object data="URL" type="MIME" width="W" height="H">fallback</object>

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayinline
Content categoriesFlow content, phrasing content, embedded content, listed, form-associated, palpable content; interactive if usemap
Permitted contentTransparent (fallback content); historically zero or more <param> first
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts embedded content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLObjectElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
dataURLThe resource URL. Required (or classid historically).HTML 4.01
typeMIME typeThe content type of the resource, for example application/pdf, image/svg+xml.HTML 4.01
nametextName of the browsing context (for use as a target).HTML 4.01

PDF with fallback link

<object data="catalogue.pdf" type="application/pdf" width="100%" height="600">
  <p>Your browser cannot display the PDF. <a href="catalogue.pdf">Download it</a>.</p>
</object>

SVG with PNG fallback

<object data="chart.svg" type="image/svg+xml" width="400" height="300">
  <img src="chart.png" alt="Sales chart for 2026" width="400" height="300">
</object>

Default browser CSS

object { display: inline; }

Accessibility

  • Provide fallback content that is accessible; there is no alt attribute on object.
  • Add a title for screen readers when the object is a nested page.

Common mistakes

  • Using <object> for video.
  • Nested objects several levels deep as a 'fallback chain' for old plug-ins.

See also

<embed>, <iframe>, <img>, <param>, <video>

<ol> Ordered list

current Category: Text content · Versions: HTML 1, HTML 2.0, HTML 3.2, HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <ol> element represents an ordered list of items: a list where the order matters, such as the steps of a recipe, the ranking of a competition, or the chapters of a book. Browsers number the items automatically. Each item is an <li>. If the order is not meaningful, use <ul> instead.

The type attribute selects the numbering system (numbers, letters, roman numerals), start sets the first number and reversed counts downward. These attributes are not presentational and remain valid in HTML5 because changing the numbering style can change the meaning of references such as 'see item iv'. For purely visual changes use CSS list-style-type.

Syntax

<ol>
  <li>First</li>
  <li>Second</li>
</ol>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayblock
Content categoriesFlow content; palpable if it has at least one <li>
Permitted contentZero or more <li>, <script>, <template>
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts flow content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLOListElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
type1 | a | A | i | INumbering type: decimal (default), lowercase letters, uppercase letters, lowercase roman, uppercase roman.HTML 3.2
startintegerThe number of the first item (always a decimal integer even if type is a or i).HTML 3.2
reversedbooleanNumber the items in descending order.HTML5
compactbooleanObsolete. Compact rendering.HTML 2.0

Examples

Steps

<ol>
  <li>Open the editor.</li>
  <li>Write the HTML.</li>
  <li>Save as index.html.</li>
  <li>Open it in the browser.</li>
</ol>

Letters and roman numerals

<ol type="A">
  <li>Option A</li>
  <li>Option B</li>
</ol>
<ol type="i" start="4">
  <li>iv</li>
  <li>v</li>
</ol>

Countdown

<ol reversed>
  <li>Third place</li>
  <li>Second place</li>
  <li>Winner</li>
</ol>

Numbers 3, 2, 1.

Nested numbering with CSS counters

<style>
  ol { counter-reset: item; list-style: none; }
  ol li::before { counter-increment: item; content: counters(item, '.') ' '; }
</style>
<ol>
  <li>Intro
    <ol>
      <li>History</li>
      <li>Syntax</li>
    </ol>
  </li>
</ol>

Produces 1, 1.1, 1.2.

Removing the numbers

<ol style="list-style: none; padding: 0">...</ol>

Default browser CSS

ol { display: block; list-style-type: decimal; margin: 1em 0; padding-inline-start: 40px; }

Accessibility

  • Screen readers announce 'list, 4 items' and the number of each item, which is very helpful for instructions.

Common mistakes

  • Using <ol> when order does not matter.
  • Writing the numbers by hand inside the items.
  • Putting text directly inside <ol> outside of <li>.

See also

<ul>, <li>, <menu>, <dl>

<optgroup> Option group

current Category: Forms · Versions: HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <optgroup> element groups related <option> elements inside a <select> under a non-selectable heading given by the label attribute. Groups cannot be nested. Disabling an optgroup disables all its options.

Syntax

<select>
  <optgroup label="Group">
    <option>...</option>
  </optgroup>
</select>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayblock
Content categoriesNone
Permitted contentZero or more <option>, <script>, <template>; optionally a <legend> first in newer browsers with customisable select
Permitted parents<select>
Tag omissionEnd tag may be omitted if followed by another <optgroup> or if there is no more content in the parent
DOM interfaceHTMLOptGroupElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
labeltextRequired. The group heading shown in the list.HTML 4.01
disabledbooleanDisables all options in the group.HTML 4.01

Examples

Cities grouped by country

<label for="city">City</label>
<select id="city" name="city">
  <optgroup label="Egypt">
    <option value="cai">Cairo</option>
    <option value="giz">Giza</option>
    <option value="alx">Alexandria</option>
  </optgroup>
  <optgroup label="Saudi Arabia">
    <option value="ruh">Riyadh</option>
    <option value="jed">Jeddah</option>
  </optgroup>
</select>

Default browser CSS

optgroup { display: block; font-weight: bold; font-style: normal; }

Accessibility

  • Screen readers announce the group label when entering the group.

Common mistakes

  • Omitting label.
  • Nesting optgroups.
  • Trying to make the group heading selectable.

See also

<select>, <option>

<option> Option

current Category: Forms · Versions: HTML 2.0, HTML 3.2, HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <option> element defines one item in a <select> drop-down list, an <optgroup>, or a <datalist> of suggestions. Its text content is what the user sees; the value attribute is what is submitted with the form. If value is omitted the text content is submitted instead.

The selected attribute pre-selects the option. In a single-select list only one option should be selected; in a <select multiple> several may be. The end tag may be omitted.

Syntax

<option value="v">Text</option>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayblock
Content categoriesNone
Permitted contentText, optionally with escaped characters
Permitted parents<select>, <optgroup>, <datalist>
Tag omissionEnd tag may be omitted if followed by another <option> or <optgroup>, or if there is no more content in the parent
DOM interfaceHTMLOptionElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
valuetextThe value submitted when this option is selected. Defaults to the text content.HTML 2.0
selectedbooleanInitially selected.HTML 2.0
disabledbooleanCannot be selected.HTML 4.01
labeltextAlternative label shown instead of the text content (used mainly in datalist).HTML 4.01

Examples

Basic select

<select name="size">
  <option value="">-- Choose a size --</option>
  <option value="s">Small</option>
  <option value="m" selected>Medium</option>
  <option value="l">Large</option>
</select>

The first option with an empty value acts as a placeholder; combine with required to force a choice.

Disabled placeholder that cannot be re-selected

<select required>
  <option value="" disabled selected>Select a country</option>
  <option>Egypt</option>
</select>

Datalist options with labels

<datalist id="codes">
  <option value="EG" label="Egypt">
  <option value="SA" label="Saudi Arabia">
</datalist>

Default browser CSS

option { display: block; padding: 0 2px 1px; white-space: nowrap; min-height: 1.2em; }

Accessibility

  • Keep option text short and unique.
  • Do not rely on colour alone to differentiate options.

Common mistakes

  • Nesting HTML inside option (only text is allowed).
  • Multiple selected options in a single select (the last wins).
  • Forgetting the value so a long label is submitted.

See also

<select>, <optgroup>, <datalist>

<output> Calculation or user-action result

current Category: Forms · Versions: HTML5

Description

The <output> element is a container into which a site or app can inject the result of a calculation or the outcome of a user action, for example the total price in a cart, the current value of a range slider, or a status message. It is form-associated and labelable, and it is an ARIA live region by default (role="status"), which means screen readers announce changes to its content automatically.

Syntax

<output name="result" for="a b">0</output>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayinline
Content categoriesFlow content, phrasing content, listed, labelable, resettable, form-associated, palpable content
Permitted contentPhrasing content
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts phrasing content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLOutputElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
forspace-separated idsThe elements that contributed to the calculation.HTML5
formform idAssociated form.HTML5
nametextName of the output (not submitted with the form).HTML5

Examples

Live sum of two inputs

<form oninput="total.value = Number(a.value) + Number(b.value)">
  <input type="number" id="a" name="a" value="0"> +
  <input type="number" id="b" name="b" value="0"> =
  <output name="total" for="a b">0</output>
</form>

Showing a slider's value

<label for="vol">Volume</label>
<input type="range" id="vol" min="0" max="100" value="50" oninput="v.value = this.value">
<output id="v" for="vol">50</output>

Default browser CSS

output { display: inline; unicode-bidi: isolate; }

Accessibility

  • Because it is a live region, changes are announced; do not update it dozens of times per second with noise.

Common mistakes

  • Using a <span> for results that should be announced.
  • Expecting the value to be submitted.

See also

<input>, <form>, <meter>, <progress>

<p> Paragraph

current Category: Text content · Versions: HTML 1, HTML 2.0, HTML 3.2, HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <p> element represents a paragraph: a block of related text, usually a group of sentences on one topic. Browsers display paragraphs as blocks separated by vertical space (a margin of 1em above and below). Paragraphs are one of the most used elements in HTML and one of the original elements from 1991, where <p> was a separator between paragraphs rather than a container.

A paragraph may contain only phrasing content (text, links, emphasis, images, and so on). It cannot contain block-level elements such as <div>, <ul>, <table>, headings or another <p>. If the browser encounters one of these inside a <p> it automatically closes the paragraph first, which often produces layouts that look wrong for no obvious reason.

The end tag may be omitted because the browser knows a paragraph ends when the next block starts, but writing </p> makes the code much clearer. Do not use empty <p></p> elements to add space; use CSS margins.

Syntax

<p>Text of the paragraph.</p>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayblock
Content categoriesFlow content, palpable content
Permitted contentPhrasing content
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts flow content
Tag omissionEnd tag may be omitted if the <p> is immediately followed by address, article, aside, blockquote, details, dialog, div, dl, fieldset, figcaption, figure, footer, form, h1-h6, header, hgroup, hr, main, menu, nav, ol, p, pre, search, section, table or ul, or if there is no more content in the parent (except when the parent is <a>, <audio>, <del>, <ins>, <map>, <noscript> or <video>)
DOM interfaceHTMLParagraphElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
alignleft | center | right | justifyObsolete. Use CSS text-align.HTML 3.2

Examples

Two paragraphs

<p>HTML describes the structure of a page.</p>
<p>CSS describes how the page looks.</p>

Inline elements inside a paragraph

<p>I <em>really</em> love <a href="https://developer.mozilla.org">MDN</a>, and I read it <strong>every day</strong>.</p>

Wrong: a list inside a paragraph

<!-- Wrong: the browser closes the <p> before the <ul> -->
<p>Shopping:
  <ul><li>Milk</li></ul>
</p>

<!-- Right -->
<p>Shopping:</p>
<ul><li>Milk</li></ul>

Typography with CSS

<style>
  p { line-height: 1.6; max-width: 65ch; margin: 0 0 1em; }
  p + p { text-indent: 1.5em; margin-top: -0.5em; }
</style>

65ch keeps lines at a comfortable reading length; text-indent gives book-style paragraphs.

Default browser CSS

p { display: block; margin-block: 1em; }

Accessibility

  • Screen readers pause between paragraphs; use real paragraphs rather than <br><br>.
  • Keep paragraphs reasonably short; long walls of text are hard for everyone.

Common mistakes

  • Block elements inside <p>.
  • Empty paragraphs for spacing.
  • Using <br><br> instead of a new paragraph.
  • Using <p> for every line in an address (use <br> inside one <p>).

See also

<br>, <div>, <span>, <blockquote>, <pre>

<param> Object parameter (deprecated)

deprecated Category: Embedded content · Versions: HTML 3.2, HTML 4.01, HTML5; deprecated in the Living Standard

Description

The <param> element defined a parameter for an <object> element, passing a name/value pair to the plug-in that displayed the object (for example the autoplay setting of a Flash movie). Since plug-ins no longer exist, the element serves no purpose; the Living Standard marks it deprecated and it is retained only for compatibility. It is a void element.

Syntax

<object data="movie.swf">
  <param name="quality" value="high">
</object>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementYes (no closing tag)
Default displaynone
Content categoriesNone
Permitted contentNone (void element)
Permitted parents<object>, before any flow content
Tag omissionNo end tag
DOM interfaceHTMLParamElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
nametextThe parameter name.HTML 3.2
valuetextThe parameter value.HTML 3.2
typeMIME typeObsolete. Type of the value when valuetype=ref.HTML 4.01
valuetypedata | ref | objectObsolete. How to interpret value.HTML 4.01

Examples

Historical Flash embed

<object data="movie.swf" type="application/x-shockwave-flash" width="400" height="300">
  <param name="quality" value="high">
  <param name="wmode" value="transparent">
  <p>Flash is no longer supported.</p>
</object>

Default browser CSS

param { display: none; }

Common mistakes

  • Any use in new pages.

See also

<object>, <embed>

<picture> Picture (responsive image container)

current Category: Image and multimedia · Versions: HTML 5.1 (2016)

Description

The <picture> element contains zero or more <source> elements and exactly one <img> element, and lets the browser choose the most suitable image from several candidates. The browser examines each <source> in order and uses the first whose media query matches and whose type it supports; if none match it falls back to the <img>. The <img> element is required: it is what is actually displayed, and it carries the alt text, width, height, loading and other attributes.

Use <picture> for three purposes: art direction (a cropped image on phones, a wide one on desktops), format selection (AVIF or WebP for modern browsers, JPEG for old ones), and dark-mode variants. For simply serving different sizes of the same image, srcset and sizes on a plain <img> are enough.

Syntax

<picture>
  <source srcset="..." media="..." type="...">
  <img src="..." alt="...">
</picture>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayinline
Content categoriesFlow content, phrasing content, embedded content, palpable content
Permitted contentZero or more <source> elements, followed by one <img>, optionally intermixed with <script> and <template>
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts embedded content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLPictureElement

Attributes

Only the global attributes and event handler attributes.

Examples

Modern formats with fallback

<picture>
  <source srcset="photo.avif" type="image/avif">
  <source srcset="photo.webp" type="image/webp">
  <img src="photo.jpg" alt="Sunset over the Nile" width="800" height="500">
</picture>

Browsers that support AVIF use it; others try WebP; the rest use JPEG.

Art direction

<picture>
  <source media="(max-width: 600px)" srcset="hero-portrait.jpg">
  <source media="(min-width: 601px)" srcset="hero-wide.jpg">
  <img src="hero-wide.jpg" alt="Our team in the office" width="1200" height="600">
</picture>

A tight portrait crop on phones, the full wide picture on larger screens.

Dark mode image

<picture>
  <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="logo-dark.svg">
  <img src="logo-light.svg" alt="Book Store" width="120" height="40">
</picture>

Combining with srcset sizes

<picture>
  <source type="image/webp" srcset="p-400.webp 400w, p-800.webp 800w" sizes="(max-width: 600px) 100vw, 600px">
  <img src="p-800.jpg" srcset="p-400.jpg 400w, p-800.jpg 800w" sizes="(max-width: 600px) 100vw, 600px" alt="..." width="800" height="533">
</picture>

Default browser CSS

picture { display: inline; }

Accessibility

  • All accessibility comes from the <img>: alt text goes there, never on <source>.

Common mistakes

  • Omitting the <img>.
  • Putting <img> before the <source> elements (sources after img are ignored).
  • Using src instead of srcset on <source>.
  • Styling the <picture> instead of the <img> (picture has no box of its own in most cases).

See also

<img>, <source>, <figure>

<plaintext> Plain text (obsolete)

obsolete Category: Obsolete text content · Versions: HTML 1, HTML 2.0 (deprecated); obsolete

Description

The <plaintext> element told the browser to treat everything after it as plain text, without interpreting any further tags, until the end of the file. It could not be closed. It was one of the 1991 elements, was deprecated in HTML 2.0 and is obsolete. Use <pre> for pre-formatted text, escaping < and & as entities, or serve the file as text/plain.

Syntax

<plaintext>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementYes (no closing tag)
Default displayblock
Content categoriesHistorical
Permitted contentEverything after it
Permitted parentsAny
Tag omissionNo end tag possible
DOM interfaceHTMLElement

Attributes

Only the global attributes and event handler attributes.

Examples

Replacement

<pre>&lt;p&gt;This shows the tag literally.&lt;/p&gt;</pre>

Default browser CSS

plaintext { display: block; font-family: monospace; white-space: pre; }

Common mistakes

  • Any use.

See also

<pre>, <xmp>, <listing>

<portal> Portal (experimental, abandoned)

experimental Category: Embedded content · Versions: Chrome experiment (2019-2022); not standardised

Description

The <portal> element was an experiment that embedded a preview of another page, like an iframe, with the ability to 'activate' it and navigate seamlessly into it with an animation. It was available only behind a flag in Chrome and the work has been superseded by the View Transitions API and prerendering with the Speculation Rules API. Do not use it.

Syntax

<portal src="https://example.com"></portal>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayinline
Content categoriesExperimental
Permitted contentNone
Permitted parentsEmbedded content
Tag omissionNeither
DOM interfaceHTMLPortalElement (Chrome only)

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
srcURLPage to preview.Experimental
referrerpolicypolicyReferrer policy.Experimental

Examples

Modern alternative

<script type="speculationrules">
{ "prerender": [{ "urls": ["/next-page.html"] }] }
</script>

Common mistakes

  • Any use.

See also

<iframe>, <fencedframe>

<pre> Pre-formatted text

current Category: Text content · Versions: HTML 1, HTML 2.0, HTML 3.2, HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <pre> element represents pre-formatted text that is displayed exactly as written in the HTML file: every space, tab and line break is preserved, and a monospace (fixed-width) font is used. It is the standard way to show source code, ASCII art, poetry with meaningful spacing, email messages and terminal output.

Markup inside <pre> is still interpreted, so to show HTML source you must escape < as &lt; and & as &amp;. For code, wrap the content in <code> inside the <pre>. A line break immediately after the opening <pre> tag is ignored by the parser, which is convenient for formatting.

Long lines in <pre> do not wrap by default and can overflow the page horizontally; add CSS overflow-x: auto or white-space: pre-wrap.

Syntax

<pre>
  text with
    preserved   spacing
</pre>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayblock
Content categoriesFlow content, palpable content
Permitted contentPhrasing content
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts flow content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLPreElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
widthintegerObsolete. Number of characters per line.HTML 2.0
wrapbooleanNon-standard. Wrap long lines. Use CSS white-space: pre-wrap.Netscape

Examples

Code block

<pre><code>&lt;footer&gt;
  &lt;p&gt;&amp;copy; 2026&lt;/p&gt;
&lt;/footer&gt;</code></pre>

The entities display as the real characters.

ASCII art

<pre>
  /\_/\
 ( o.o )
  &gt; ^ &lt;
</pre>

Scrollable, styled code

<style>
  pre { background: #1e1e1e; color: #eee; padding: 16px; border-radius: 8px; overflow-x: auto; tab-size: 2; }
</style>

Wrapping long lines

<pre style="white-space: pre-wrap; word-break: break-word">A very long line ...</pre>

Default browser CSS

pre { display: block; font-family: monospace; white-space: pre; margin: 1em 0; }

Accessibility

  • For ASCII art or diagrams, add an explanation in text or a figcaption, because screen readers read the characters one by one.
  • Use <pre> with <code> so assistive technology knows it is code.

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting to escape < and &.
  • Indenting the content in the source, which adds unwanted spaces to the output.
  • Using <pre> for layout.

See also

<code>, <samp>, <kbd>, <xmp>, <listing>, <textarea>

<progress> Progress indicator

current Category: Forms · Versions: HTML5

Description

The <progress> element displays the completion progress of a task, such as a file upload, a download, a multi-step form or a loading operation. It is rendered as a progress bar. With a value attribute it shows a determinate bar (a known percentage); without value it shows an indeterminate, animated bar meaning 'working, but I do not know how long it will take'.

Use <meter> instead for a measurement that is not progress (disk space, a score).

Syntax

<progress value="30" max="100">30%</progress>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayinline-block
Content categoriesFlow content, phrasing content, labelable, palpable content
Permitted contentPhrasing content, but no <progress> descendants
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts phrasing content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLProgressElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
valuenumberHow much has been completed, from 0 to max. Omit for an indeterminate bar.HTML5
maxnumberThe total amount of work. Default 1.HTML5

Examples

Determinate

<label for="up">Uploading photo</label>
<progress id="up" value="65" max="100">65%</progress>

Indeterminate

<progress>Loading...</progress>

Updating from JavaScript

<progress id="bar" max="100" value="0"></progress>
<script>
  let v = 0;
  const t = setInterval(() => {
    document.getElementById('bar').value = ++v;
    if (v === 100) clearInterval(t);
  }, 50);
</script>

Styling

<style>
  progress { width: 100%; height: 12px; accent-color: #0f8a4c; }
</style>

accent-color is the simplest cross-browser way to colour the bar.

Default browser CSS

progress { display: inline-block; appearance: auto; }

Accessibility

  • Label the progress bar.
  • Announce completion with a live region or by moving focus; the bar's value changes are not automatically spoken by all screen readers.

Common mistakes

  • Using it for static measurements (use <meter>).
  • Value greater than max.

See also

<meter>, <output>

<q> Inline quotation

current Category: Text-level semantics · Versions: HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <q> element indicates a short inline quotation that sits within a sentence. Browsers automatically add quotation marks around it, choosing the correct style for the language declared with lang (curly double quotes in English, guillemets in French, and so on), so you should not type quotation marks yourself. For long quotations that need their own paragraph use <blockquote>.

Syntax

<q cite="URL">quoted words</q>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayinline
Content categoriesFlow content, phrasing content, palpable content
Permitted contentPhrasing content
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts phrasing content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLQuoteElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
citeURLThe source of the quotation. Not displayed.HTML 4.01

Examples

Basic quote

<p>Tim Berners-Lee said <q>the Web is for everyone</q>.</p>

Renders as: Tim Berners-Lee said “the Web is for everyone”.

Language-aware quotation marks

<p lang="fr">Il a dit <q>bonjour</q>.</p>

Renders with « bonjour ».

Custom quote characters

<style>
  q { quotes: '„' '“'; }
</style>

Default browser CSS

q { display: inline; }
q::before { content: open-quote; }
q::after { content: close-quote; }

Accessibility

  • Screen readers may or may not announce the quotation; the generated quote marks are usually read.

Common mistakes

  • Adding manual quotation marks inside <q>, giving double marks.
  • Using <q> for irony or scare quotes.

See also

<blockquote>, <cite>

<rb> Ruby base (deprecated)

deprecated Category: Text-level semantics (ruby) · Versions: XHTML 1.1 Ruby, HTML 5.1; removed from the Living Standard

Description

The <rb> element explicitly marked the base text component of a ruby annotation, the text that the <rt> annotation is placed above. The Living Standard removed it because the base text can simply be written directly inside <ruby>. Browsers still support it.

Syntax

<ruby><rb>漢</rb><rt>kan</rt></ruby>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayruby-base
Content categoriesNone
Permitted contentPhrasing content
Permitted parents<ruby>
Tag omissionEnd tag may be omitted

Attributes

Only the global attributes and event handler attributes.

Examples

Old and new

<!-- With rb -->
<ruby><rb>東</rb><rt>tō</rt><rb>京</rb><rt>kyō</rt></ruby>

<!-- Without rb -->
<ruby>東<rt>tō</rt>京<rt>kyō</rt></ruby>

Default browser CSS

rb { display: ruby-base; }

Common mistakes

  • Relying on it in new markup.

See also

<ruby>, <rt>, <rp>, <rtc>

<rp> Ruby fallback parenthesis

current Category: Text-level semantics (ruby) · Versions: HTML5

Description

The <rp> element provides fallback parentheses for browsers that do not support ruby annotations. Browsers that support ruby hide the <rp> content; older browsers display it, so the annotation appears in brackets after the base text instead of above it. Place one <rp> before and one after each <rt>.

Syntax

<ruby>漢<rp>(</rp><rt>kan</rt><rp>)</rp></ruby>

Default displaynone
Content categoriesNone
Permitted contentText
Permitted parents<ruby>, immediately before or after an <rt>

Only the global attributes and event handler attributes.

With fallback

<ruby>明日<rp>(</rp><rt>あした</rt><rp>)</rp></ruby>

Modern browsers: annotation above. Old browsers: 明日(あした).

Default browser CSS

rp { display: none; }

Common mistakes

  • Omitting rp when supporting very old browsers.

See also

<ruby>, <rt>

<rt> Ruby text (annotation)

current Category: Text-level semantics (ruby) · Versions: HTML5

Description

The <rt> element specifies the ruby text component of a ruby annotation: the small text placed above (or beside) the base characters to show pronunciation, translation or transliteration. It is used for East Asian typography (furigana in Japanese, pinyin/zhuyin in Chinese) and increasingly for other languages. It must be inside a <ruby> element.

Syntax

<ruby>base<rt>annotation</rt></ruby>

Technical summary
