Void elementNo
Default displayruby-text
Content categoriesNone
Permitted contentPhrasing content
Permitted parents<ruby>
Tag omissionEnd tag may be omitted if followed by <rt> or <rp> or if there is no more content in the parent
DOM interfaceHTMLElement

Attributes

Only the global attributes and event handler attributes.

Examples

Japanese furigana

<ruby>漢字<rt>かんじ</rt></ruby>

Arabic word with transliteration

<ruby lang="ar">كتاب<rt lang="en">kitāb</rt></ruby>

Styling

<style>
  rt { font-size: 0.6em; color: #666; }
</style>

Default browser CSS

rt { display: ruby-text; font-size: 50%; }

Accessibility

  • Screen readers generally read only the base text; use <rt> for supplementary information, not essential content.

Common mistakes

  • Using <rt> outside <ruby>.

See also

<ruby>, <rp>, <rb>, <rtc>

<rtc> Ruby text container (deprecated)

deprecated Category: Text-level semantics (ruby) · Versions: HTML 5.1; removed from the Living Standard

Description

The <rtc> element grouped several <rt> annotations so that a base text could have two layers of annotation (for example pronunciation above and meaning below). Only Firefox implemented it, and the Living Standard removed it. Nest two <ruby> elements for double-sided annotations.

Syntax

<ruby>base<rtc><rt>a</rt></rtc><rtc><rt>b</rt></rtc></ruby>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayruby-text-container
Content categoriesNone
Permitted contentPhrasing content or <rt>
Permitted parents<ruby>
Tag omissionEnd tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLElement

Attributes

Only the global attributes and event handler attributes.

Examples

Historical

<ruby>旧金山<rtc><rt>jiù jīn shān</rt></rtc><rtc><rt>San Francisco</rt></rtc></ruby>

Default browser CSS

rtc { display: ruby-text-container; }

Common mistakes

  • Relying on it.

See also

<ruby>, <rt>, <rb>

<ruby> Ruby annotation

current Category: Text-level semantics (ruby) · Versions: XHTML 1.1 (2001), HTML5

Description

The <ruby> element represents small annotations rendered above, below or beside base text, most often used to show the pronunciation of East Asian characters. The name comes from a small typographic size called 'ruby' used by British printers. The base text is written directly inside <ruby>, each annotation in an <rt>, and optional fallback parentheses in <rp>.

Syntax

<ruby>base<rp>(</rp><rt>annotation</rt><rp>)</rp></ruby>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayruby
Content categoriesFlow content, phrasing content, palpable content
Permitted contentPhrasing content, <rt>, <rp>
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts phrasing content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLElement

Attributes

Only the global attributes and event handler attributes.

Examples

Furigana over each character

<ruby>東<rp>(</rp><rt>とう</rt><rp>)</rp>京<rp>(</rp><rt>きょう</rt><rp>)</rp></ruby>

Whole word annotation

<ruby>北京<rt>Běijīng</rt></ruby>

Annotation below with CSS

<style>
  ruby { ruby-position: under; }
</style>

Default browser CSS

ruby { display: ruby; }

Accessibility

  • Do not put essential meaning only in the annotation.

Common mistakes

  • Placing <rt> outside <ruby>.
  • Forgetting <rp> if old browser support is needed.

See also

<rt>, <rp>, <rb>, <rtc>

<s> Strikethrough (no longer accurate)

current Category: Text-level semantics · Versions: HTML 3.2, HTML 4.01 (deprecated), HTML5 (redefined)

Description

The <s> element renders text with a line through it and represents content that is no longer accurate or no longer relevant, such as an old price next to the new one, or a sold-out item. In HTML 4 it was a purely presentational strike-through synonym for <strike> and was deprecated; HTML5 gave it this meaning and made it valid again while removing <strike>.

Do not use <s> to indicate document edits; that is what <del> is for.

Syntax

<s>outdated text</s>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayinline
Content categoriesFlow content, phrasing content, palpable content
Permitted contentPhrasing content
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts phrasing content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLElement

Attributes

Only the global attributes and event handler attributes.

Examples

Old price

<p>Price: <s>150 EGP</s> <strong>99 EGP</strong></p>

Sold-out event

<p><s>Workshop: Saturday 10 am</s> (sold out)</p>

Accessible old price

<p>Price: <s><span class="sr-only">Was </span>150 EGP</s> <span class="sr-only">now </span>99 EGP</p>

Visually hidden words make the meaning clear to screen readers.

Default browser CSS

s { text-decoration: line-through; }

Accessibility

  • The strike-through is not announced; add hidden text where the meaning matters.

Common mistakes

  • Using <s> for deletions in a revision (use <del>).
  • Using <strike>.

See also

<del>, <strike>, <u>

<samp> Sample output

current Category: Text-level semantics · Versions: HTML 2.0, HTML 3.2, HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <samp> element marks sample or quoted output from a computer program or system: error messages, terminal output, log lines. Browsers render it in a monospace font. Nest <kbd> inside <samp> to show input echoed by the system, and <samp> inside <kbd> for input that names an on-screen item.

Syntax

<samp>program output</samp>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayinline
Content categoriesFlow content, phrasing content, palpable content
Permitted contentPhrasing content
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts phrasing content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLElement

Attributes

Only the global attributes and event handler attributes.

Examples

Error message

<p>If the file is missing you will see <samp>404 Not Found</samp>.</p>

Terminal session

<pre><samp>$ <kbd>ls</kbd>
index.html  style.css
$ </samp></pre>

Default browser CSS

samp { font-family: monospace; }

Common mistakes

  • Using <code> for output.
  • Using <samp> for user input.

See also

<code>, <kbd>, <pre>, <var>

<script> Script

current Category: Scripting · Versions: HTML 3.2 (reserved), HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <script> element embeds executable code, almost always JavaScript, or links to an external script file with the src attribute. It can also hold data blocks (JSON, templates, import maps, speculation rules) that the browser does not execute when type is set to a non-script MIME type.

By default a script blocks HTML parsing: the browser stops, downloads and runs the script, then continues. To avoid slowing down the page, put scripts at the end of <body> or, better, in <head> with the defer attribute (run after parsing, in order) or async (run as soon as downloaded, in any order). Module scripts (type="module") are deferred automatically and support import/export.

An element with src must be empty; inline code and src cannot be combined. Inside an inline script the sequence </script> ends the element even inside a string, so write it as '<\/script>' in JavaScript strings.

Syntax

<script src="app.js" defer></script>
<script>
  // inline code
</script>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displaynone
Content categoriesMetadata content, flow content, phrasing content, script-supporting element
Permitted contentScript code or data, depending on type; nothing if src is present
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts metadata or phrasing content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLScriptElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
srcURLExternal script file.HTML 4.01
typeomitted | module | importmap | speculationrules | MIME typeOmitted or text/javascript: classic script. module: ES module. importmap: JSON import map. Any other type: data block that is not executed.HTML 4.01 / HTML5
deferbooleanDownload in parallel, execute after the document has been parsed, in document order. Only for external classic scripts.HTML 4.01
asyncbooleanDownload in parallel, execute as soon as ready, possibly out of order. For independent scripts such as analytics.HTML5
nomodulebooleanDo not run in browsers that support modules; used to provide fallbacks for old browsers.HTML5
crossoriginanonymous | use-credentialsCORS setting; needed to get full error details from cross-origin scripts.HTML5
integrityhashSubresource Integrity hash.SRI
referrerpolicyreferrer policyReferrer to send.HTML5
fetchpriorityhigh | low | autoDownload priority hint.Living Standard
blockingrenderBlock rendering until the script runs.Living Standard
noncetextCryptographic nonce for Content Security Policy (global attribute).CSP
attributionsrcempty or URLExperimental attribution reporting.Experimental
charsetencodingObsolete. Encoding of the script; use UTF-8 for everything.HTML 4.01
languagetextObsolete. Scripting language name. Use type or omit.HTML 3.2
event, fortextObsolete. Internet Explorer event binding.HTML 4.01

Examples

Recommended: deferred external script in head

<head>
  <script src="app.js" defer></script>
</head>

The script downloads while the HTML parses and runs when the DOM is ready.

Inline script

<script>
  document.querySelector('footer').textContent = '© ' + new Date().getFullYear();
</script>

ES module

<script type="module">
  import { greet } from './greet.js';
  greet('world');
</script>

Async analytics

<script src="https://analytics.example.com/tag.js" async></script>

JSON data block

<script id="config" type="application/json">
  { "currency": "EGP", "vat": 14 }
</script>
<script>
  const cfg = JSON.parse(document.getElementById('config').textContent);
</script>

Structured data for search engines

<script type="application/ld+json">
{ "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "Book", "name": "Learn HTML" }
</script>

Import map

<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": { "lodash": "https://cdn.example.com/lodash.js" } }
</script>

HTML 4 style with comment hiding (no longer needed)

<script type="text/javascript">
<!--
  alert('old style');
//-->
</script>

The comment trick hid code from 1995 browsers that did not know <script>.

Default browser CSS

script { display: none; }

Accessibility

  • Content generated by scripts must be as accessible as static content: manage focus, announce changes with live regions, keep keyboard support.

Common mistakes

  • Placing a blocking script in head without defer, so the page appears slowly.
  • Running DOM code before the elements exist (fix with defer or DOMContentLoaded).
  • Writing <script src="x.js" /> (self-closing is not allowed; everything after it becomes script).
  • Putting </script> inside a string.

See also

<noscript>, <template>, <link>, <style>

<search> Search section

current Category: Content sectioning · Versions: Living Standard (2023)

Description

The <search> element represents a part of the document whose contents are search or filtering controls: a site search form, a filter panel in a product list, or the controls of a find-in-page feature. It has no visual effect; it exposes the 'search' landmark to assistive technology. It replaces the old pattern <form role="search">. The form itself still goes inside it.

Syntax

<search>
  <form>...</form>
</search>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayblock
Content categoriesFlow content, palpable content
Permitted contentFlow content
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts flow content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLElement

Attributes

Only the global attributes and event handler attributes.

Examples

Site search

<search>
  <form action="/search">
    <label for="q">Search books</label>
    <input id="q" name="q" type="search">
    <button>Search</button>
  </form>
</search>

Filter panel

<search aria-label="Filter products">
  <label><input type="checkbox" name="instock"> In stock only</label>
  <label>Max price <input type="range" name="max" min="0" max="500"></label>
</search>

Default browser CSS

search { display: block; }

Accessibility

  • Exposed as the 'search' landmark; screen reader users can jump straight to it.
  • In older browsers add role="search" to the <search> element for the same effect.

Common mistakes

  • Using <search> for the search results (it is for the controls).
  • Nesting several search landmarks without labels.

See also

<form>, <input>, <nav>

<section> Generic section

current Category: Content sectioning · Versions: HTML5

Description

The <section> element represents a generic, thematic grouping of content, typically with a heading. Examples: the chapters of an article, the tabs of a tabbed interface, the 'Introduction', 'Features' and 'Pricing' areas of a landing page. Each section should be identifiable, usually by an <h2>-<h6> heading as its first child.

Choosing between the sectioning elements: use <article> if the content is self-contained and could be syndicated; <nav> for navigation; <aside> for tangential content; <section> when the content is a distinct part of the page with its own heading; and <div> when the grouping is only for styling or scripting and has no meaning. A <section> without a heading is usually a sign that <div> is more appropriate.

Syntax

<section>
  <h2>Heading</h2>
  ...
</section>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayblock
Content categoriesFlow content, sectioning content, palpable content
Permitted contentFlow content
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts flow content, but not <address>
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLElement

Attributes

Only the global attributes and event handler attributes.

Examples

Landing page sections

<main>
  <section id="features">
    <h2>Features</h2>
    <p>...</p>
  </section>
  <section id="pricing">
    <h2>Pricing</h2>
    <p>...</p>
  </section>
</main>

Sections inside an article

<article>
  <h1>Learn HTML</h1>
  <section>
    <h2>Part 1: Tags</h2>
    <p>...</p>
  </section>
  <section>
    <h2>Part 2: Attributes</h2>
    <p>...</p>
  </section>
</article>

Labelled section as a region landmark

<section aria-labelledby="faq-h">
  <h2 id="faq-h">FAQ</h2>
  ...
</section>

A section with an accessible name is exposed as a 'region' landmark.

Default browser CSS

section { display: block; }

Accessibility

  • Sections become 'region' landmarks only when they have an accessible name (aria-labelledby or aria-label).
  • Always include a heading.

Common mistakes

  • Using <section> as a styling wrapper instead of <div>.
  • Sections without headings.
  • Assuming <section> resets heading levels (it does not in practice; use the correct h-level).

See also

<article>, <aside>, <nav>, <div>, <h1>, <main>

<select> Drop-down / list box

current Category: Forms · Versions: HTML 2.0, HTML 3.2, HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <select> element creates a control for choosing one option (or, with multiple, several) from a list. It contains <option> elements, optionally grouped in <optgroup>. By default it appears as a drop-down menu; with the multiple attribute or a size greater than 1 it appears as a scrolling list box. The name attribute and the value of the chosen option(s) are submitted with the form.

A select is best for lists of roughly 5 to 30 fixed choices. For 2 to 4 choices radio buttons are easier to see at a glance; for very long lists or free text with suggestions use <input> with a <datalist>. Newer browsers allow a customisable select (CSS appearance: base-select) with rich option content.

Syntax

<select name="n">
  <option value="1">One</option>
</select>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayinline-block
Content categoriesFlow content, phrasing content, interactive content, listed, labelable, resettable, submittable, form-associated, palpable
Permitted contentZero or more <option>, <optgroup>, <hr>, <script>, <template>; optionally a <button> first for customisable selects
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts phrasing content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLSelectElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
nametextName submitted with the form.HTML 2.0
multiplebooleanAllow several options to be selected (Ctrl/Cmd-click).HTML 2.0
sizeintegerNumber of visible rows. 1 (default) gives a drop-down; more gives a list box.HTML 2.0
requiredbooleanThe user must choose an option with a non-empty value.HTML5
disabledbooleanThe control cannot be used.HTML 4.01
autofocusbooleanFocus on load.HTML5
autocompletetokenAutofill hint, for example country, cc-exp-month.HTML5
formform idAssociated form.HTML5

Examples

Drop-down with placeholder

<label for="pay">Payment</label>
<select id="pay" name="pay" required>
  <option value="">-- Select --</option>
  <option value="cod">Cash on delivery</option>
  <option value="wallet">Mobile wallet</option>
</select>

Multiple selection list box

<label for="langs">Languages you read</label>
<select id="langs" name="langs" multiple size="4">
  <option>Arabic</option>
  <option>English</option>
  <option>French</option>
  <option>German</option>
</select>

Submitted as langs=Arabic&langs=English.

Reading the value in JavaScript

<select id="s"><option value="a">A</option><option value="b">B</option></select>
<script>
  document.getElementById('s').addEventListener('change', e => console.log(e.target.value));
</script>

Basic styling

<style>
  select { padding: 8px 12px; border: 1px solid #ccc; border-radius: 6px; font: inherit; }
</style>

Default browser CSS

select { display: inline-block; }

Accessibility

  • Always label the select.
  • Do not trigger navigation on change alone; keyboard users change the value with arrow keys and would be redirected before reaching their choice. Provide a Go button.
  • Multiple selects are hard to use; consider a group of checkboxes.

Common mistakes

  • No empty placeholder option with required, so the first real option is submitted silently.
  • Using select for 2 choices (use radio buttons).
  • Putting HTML inside <option>.

See also

<option>, <optgroup>, <datalist>, <input>, <label>

<selectedcontent> Selected option display (customisable select)

experimental Category: Forms · Versions: Living Standard (2025, experimental)

Description

The <selectedcontent> element is part of the customisable <select> proposal. Placed inside the <button> that sits at the start of a <select>, it mirrors the content of the currently selected <option>, so that rich option content (icons, colour swatches, descriptions) is shown in the closed control as well as in the open list. The browser clones the selected option's children into <selectedcontent> whenever the selection changes.

It only has an effect when the select opts in with the CSS declaration appearance: base-select on both the select and its ::picker(select) pseudo-element. Browser support is still limited, so always test the fallback: browsers that do not understand it render the plain native select.

Syntax

<select>
  <button><selectedcontent></selectedcontent></button>
  <option>...</option>
</select>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayinline
Content categoriesNone
Permitted contentNothing authored; the browser fills it with a clone of the selected option's content
Permitted parentsA <button> that is the first child of a <select>
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLSelectedContentElement

Attributes

Only the global attributes and event handler attributes.

Examples

Rich select with icons

<style>
  select, ::picker(select) { appearance: base-select; }
</style>
<select>
  <button><selectedcontent></selectedcontent></button>
  <option value="red"><span class="swatch" style="background:red"></span> Red</option>
  <option value="green"><span class="swatch" style="background:green"></span> Green</option>
</select>

The closed control shows the swatch and text of the chosen option.

Default browser CSS

selectedcontent { display: contents; }

Accessibility

  • The control remains a combobox for assistive technology; the option text is announced as usual.

Common mistakes

  • Placing it anywhere other than inside the leading <button> of a <select>.
  • Relying on it without the appearance: base-select opt-in.
  • Assuming support in every browser.

See also

<select>, <option>, <button>

<shadow> Shadow root insertion point (obsolete)

obsolete Category: Obsolete web components · Versions: Shadow DOM v0; obsolete

Description

The <shadow> element was part of Shadow DOM v0 and marked where an older shadow root should be rendered inside a newer one. It was removed with Shadow DOM v1, which does not support multiple shadow roots per element. Use <slot>.

Syntax

<shadow></shadow>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayinline
Content categoriesHistorical
Permitted contentAny
Permitted parentsShadow root
Tag omissionNeither
DOM interfaceHTMLUnknownElement

Attributes

Only the global attributes and event handler attributes.

Examples

Replacement

<slot></slot>

Common mistakes

  • Any use.

See also

<slot>, <template>, <content>

<slot> Shadow DOM slot

current Category: Web components · Versions: HTML5 / DOM Standard (2016)

Description

The <slot> element is a placeholder inside a web component's shadow tree that is filled with content from the light DOM (the markup written by the user of the component). A named slot receives children that have a matching slot attribute; the unnamed default slot receives all other children. Content inside the <slot> element itself is fallback content shown when nothing is slotted.

Syntax

<slot name="title">Default title</slot>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displaycontents
Content categoriesFlow content, phrasing content
Permitted contentTransparent (fallback content)
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts phrasing content (inside a shadow tree)
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLSlotElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
nametextThe slot's name. Children with slot="name" are placed here. Omit for the default slot.DOM

Examples

A user-card component

<template id="card">
  <style>.card { border: 1px solid #ccc; padding: 12px; }</style>
  <div class="card">
    <h3><slot name="name">Anonymous</slot></h3>
    <p><slot>No description</slot></p>
  </div>
</template>

<user-card>
  <span slot="name">Ahmed</span>
  Front-end developer from Giza.
</user-card>

<script>
  customElements.define('user-card', class extends HTMLElement {
    constructor() {
      super();
      this.attachShadow({ mode: 'open' }).append(document.getElementById('card').content.cloneNode(true));
    }
  });
</script>

Styling slotted content

<style>
  ::slotted(span) { color: #b90000; }
</style>

Default browser CSS

slot { display: contents; }

Accessibility

  • Slotted content keeps its own semantics; the shadow boundary is transparent to the accessibility tree.

Common mistakes

  • Using <slot> outside a shadow root (it does nothing).
  • Slot attribute on a nested descendant rather than a direct child of the host.

See also

<template>, <content>, <shadow>

<small> Side comment (fine print)

current Category: Text-level semantics · Versions: HTML 3.2, HTML 4.01, HTML5 (redefined)

Description

The <small> element represents side comments and small print: disclaimers, caveats, legal restrictions, copyright notices, attribution. It renders the text one size smaller. In HTML 3.2 and 4 it was purely presentational ('smaller text'); HTML5 kept it and gave it this meaning, while its counterpart <big> was removed.

<small> does not reduce the importance of text. It is intended for short runs of inline text, not for whole sections; for that, use CSS font-size.

Syntax

<small>fine print</small>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayinline
Content categoriesFlow content, phrasing content, palpable content
Permitted contentPhrasing content
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts phrasing content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLElement

Attributes

Only the global attributes and event handler attributes.

Examples

Copyright in the footer

<footer>
  <p><small>&copy; 2026 Book Store. All rights reserved.</small></p>
</footer>

Price disclaimer

<p>From 99 EGP <small>(excluding delivery)</small></p>

Default browser CSS

small { font-size: smaller; }

Accessibility

  • No special announcement; the meaning is visual and semantic only.

Common mistakes

  • Wrapping entire paragraphs or sections in <small> for font size.
  • Using <small> for sub-headings.

See also

<big>, <sub>, <sup>, <footer>

<source> Media or image source

current Category: Image and multimedia · Versions: HTML5

Description

The <source> element specifies one of several alternative resources for a <picture>, <audio> or <video> element. It is a void element. The browser examines the sources in order and uses the first one it can display: for <picture> it checks the media query and image type, for <audio>/<video> it checks the type (MIME type and codecs). Because it is used inside three different parents, the set of relevant attributes differs: <picture> uses srcset, sizes, media, type, width and height; media elements use src, type and (for video) media.

Syntax

<source src="file" type="MIME">  <!-- in audio/video -->
<source srcset="file" type="MIME" media="query">  <!-- in picture -->

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementYes (no closing tag)
Default displaynone
Content categoriesNone
Permitted contentNone (void element)
Permitted parents<picture> (before the <img>), <audio>, <video> (before any <track> or flow content)
Tag omissionNo end tag
DOM interfaceHTMLSourceElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
srcURLThe media file. Required in <audio>/<video>; ignored in <picture>.HTML5
srcsetcandidate listImage candidates. Required in <picture>; ignored in media elements.HTML5
sizessize listDisplay widths for width-descriptor srcset (picture only).HTML5
typeMIME type, optionally with codecsThe resource type, for example image/webp, video/mp4, video/webm; codecs="vp9, opus". Lets the browser skip unsupported files without downloading them.HTML5
mediamedia queryUse this source only when the query matches. Valid in picture and video (audio ignores it in most browsers).HTML5
width / heightpixelsIntrinsic size of the image candidate (picture only).Living Standard

Examples

Video with two formats

<video controls width="640" height="360">
  <source src="clip.webm" type="video/webm">
  <source src="clip.mp4" type="video/mp4">
  <p>Download the <a href="clip.mp4">video</a>.</p>
</video>

Picture with format and size choice

<picture>
  <source srcset="img.avif" type="image/avif">
  <source srcset="img.webp" type="image/webp">
  <img src="img.jpg" alt="..." width="800" height="600">
</picture>

Different video for small screens

<video controls>
  <source src="small.mp4" type="video/mp4" media="(max-width: 600px)">
  <source src="large.mp4" type="video/mp4">
</video>

Default browser CSS

source { display: none; }

Accessibility

  • Accessibility attributes (alt, captions) go on the <img>, <video> or <track>, not on <source>.

Common mistakes

  • Using src inside <picture> (must be srcset).
  • Placing <source> after the <img> or after <track>.
  • Omitting type, forcing the browser to download files to test them.

See also

<picture>, <audio>, <video>, <img>, <track>

<spacer> Spacer (non-standard, obsolete)

obsolete Category: Obsolete presentational · Versions: Netscape 3-4 only

Description

The <spacer> element inserted empty horizontal or vertical space, imitating the invisible 'spacer GIF' images used for layout in the 1990s. It existed only in Netscape and was never standardised. Use CSS margin, padding or gap.

Syntax

<spacer type="horizontal" size="20">

Default displaynone

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
typehorizontal | vertical | blockKind of space.Netscape
sizepixelsAmount of space.Netscape

CSS replacement

<div style="margin-top: 20px">...</div>

  • Any use.

<br>, <hr>

<span> Generic inline container

current Category: Text-level semantics · Versions: HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <span> element is a generic inline container for phrasing content. Like <div>, it has no meaning of its own and no visual effect; it exists to be a hook for CSS (via class or id) or JavaScript, or to carry attributes such as lang or dir on a part of a sentence. It should be used only when no other element is more appropriate: <em>, <strong>, <mark>, <time>, <abbr>, <code> and the other text-level elements all carry meaning that <span> does not.

<span> is inline: it does not start a new line and it takes only as much width as its content. <div> is its block-level counterpart.

Syntax

<span class="name">text</span>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayinline
Content categoriesFlow content, phrasing content, palpable content
Permitted contentPhrasing content
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts phrasing content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLSpanElement

Attributes

Only the global attributes and event handler attributes.

Examples

Styling part of a sentence

<style>
  .price { color: #e60000; font-weight: bold; }
</style>
<p>The price is <span class="price">50 EGP</span> only.</p>

Only '50 EGP' turns red; the sentence stays on one line.

Marking a language change

<p>The Arabic word for book is <span lang="ar">كتاب</span>.</p>

A hook for JavaScript

<p>Items in cart: <span id="count">0</span></p>
<script>document.getElementById('count').textContent = 3;</script>

Visually hidden text for screen readers

<style>
  .sr-only { position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; overflow: hidden; clip: rect(0 0 0 0); white-space: nowrap; }
</style>
<button>×<span class="sr-only">Close</span></button>

Default browser CSS

span { display: inline; }

Accessibility

  • A span has no role; never make it clickable without adding role="button", tabindex="0" and keyboard handlers, and even then a real <button> is better.

Common mistakes

  • Using <span> where <em>, <strong> or another semantic element fits.
  • Putting block elements inside a span.
  • Using <span> as a button.

See also

<div>, <em>, <strong>, <mark>, <b>, <i>

<strike> Strikethrough (obsolete)

obsolete Category: Obsolete presentational · Versions: HTML 3.2, HTML 4.01 (deprecated); obsolete in HTML5

Description

The <strike> element drew a line through its text. It was purely presentational, was deprecated in HTML 4.01 and removed in HTML5. Use <del> for removed content, <s> for content that is no longer accurate, or CSS text-decoration: line-through for pure styling.

Syntax

<strike>text</strike>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayinline
Content categoriesHistorical
Permitted contentPhrasing content
Permitted parentsPhrasing content
Tag omissionNeither
DOM interfaceHTMLElement

Attributes

Only the global attributes and event handler attributes.

Examples

Replacements

<!-- Old -->
<strike>150 EGP</strike>

<!-- New: no longer accurate -->
<s>150 EGP</s>

<!-- New: edit tracking -->
<del>150 EGP</del>

Default browser CSS

strike { text-decoration: line-through; }

Common mistakes

  • Any use.

See also

<s>, <del>

<strong> Strong importance

current Category: Text-level semantics · Versions: HTML 2.0, HTML 3.2, HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <strong> element indicates that its content has strong importance, seriousness or urgency: a warning, a key instruction, the most important part of a sentence. Browsers render it in bold. Nesting <strong> inside <strong> increases the importance further.

In HTML 4 the guidance was 'use <strong> instead of <b>'; HTML5 refined it. <strong> = important; <b> = draw attention without importance (keywords); <em> = spoken stress that changes meaning; <mark> = relevance to the reader's current task. A whole paragraph of <strong> text signals nothing because nothing stands out.

Syntax

<strong>important text</strong>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayinline
Content categoriesFlow content, phrasing content, palpable content
Permitted contentPhrasing content
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts phrasing content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLElement

Attributes

Only the global attributes and event handler attributes.

Examples

Warning

<p><strong>Warning:</strong> unplug the device before opening it.</p>

Key instruction in a list

<ul>
  <li>Save the file as <strong>index.html</strong>.</li>
  <li>Open it in a browser.</li>
</ul>

strong versus em

<p><strong>Do not</strong> touch the wire. I said <em>do not</em>.</p>

The first is a serious instruction; the second stresses the words.

Default browser CSS

strong { font-weight: bold; }

Accessibility

  • Most screen readers do not announce <strong> by default, but it is the correct semantic element and some users enable emphasis announcements.

Common mistakes

  • Using <strong> just for bold styling.
  • Using <strong> for headings.
  • Wrapping large blocks in <strong>.

See also

<b>, <em>, <mark>, <i>

<style> Embedded style sheet

current Category: Document metadata · Versions: HTML 3.2 (reserved), HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <style> element contains CSS rules that apply to the document. It belongs in <head>, though browsers tolerate it in <body>. A document may have any number of <style> elements; they are applied in order together with any linked style sheets. For anything larger than a few rules, an external file loaded with <link rel="stylesheet"> is better because it can be cached and shared between pages.

The media attribute restricts the rules to certain devices or conditions. The content is raw text: the sequence </style> ends the element, and HTML entities are not decoded inside it.

Syntax

<style>
  selector { property: value; }
</style>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displaynone
Content categoriesMetadata content
Permitted contentCSS text
Permitted parents<head>; also <noscript> in head; tolerated in <body>
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLStyleElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
mediamedia queryApply only when the query matches, for example print or (max-width: 600px). Default all.HTML 4.01
blockingrenderBlock rendering until the style sheet is applied (it does anyway for inline styles).Living Standard
noncetextCSP nonce (global).CSP
titletextName of an alternate style sheet set.HTML 4.01
typetext/cssObsolete. The only allowed value is text/css; omit it.HTML 4.01
scopedbooleanRemoved. Was meant to scope styles to the parent element; use Shadow DOM or @scope.HTML5 draft (removed)

Examples

Basic page styles

<head>
  <style>
    body   { font-family: Arial, sans-serif; margin: 0; }
    footer { text-align: center; color: gray; padding: 20px; }
  </style>
</head>

Print-only rules

<style media="print">
  nav, footer { display: none; }
  a::after { content: ' (' attr(href) ')'; }
</style>

Dark mode

<style>
  @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
    body { background: #111; color: #eee; }
  }
</style>

Default browser CSS

style { display: none; }

Accessibility

  • Do not use CSS to hide content that screen readers need; display: none hides it from everyone.

Common mistakes

  • Putting CSS in <style> without the tags, or putting HTML inside <style>.
  • Typing </style> inside a CSS string.
  • Writing type="text/css" (harmless but unnecessary).

See also

<link>, <head>, <script>

<sub> Subscript

current Category: Text-level semantics · Versions: HTML 3.2, HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <sub> element renders text as a subscript: smaller and below the baseline. Use it only where the subscript has a typographic meaning, such as chemical formulas (H₂O), mathematical variable indices (x₁) or footnote markers in some styles. For purely visual lowering, use CSS vertical-align.

Syntax

H<sub>2</sub>O

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayinline
Content categoriesFlow content, phrasing content, palpable content
Permitted contentPhrasing content
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts phrasing content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLElement

Attributes

Only the global attributes and event handler attributes.

Examples

Chemistry

<p>Water is H<sub>2</sub>O and carbon dioxide is CO<sub>2</sub>.</p>

Maths

<p>The sequence a<sub>1</sub>, a<sub>2</sub>, ... a<sub>n</sub>.</p>

Default browser CSS

sub { vertical-align: sub; font-size: smaller; }

Accessibility

  • Not announced; for critical meaning consider MathML.

Common mistakes

  • Using sub/sup for layout tweaks.

See also

<sup>, <math>

<summary> Disclosure summary

current Category: Interactive elements · Versions: HTML5 (5.1)

Description

The <summary> element specifies the visible heading, label or caption of a <details> element. Clicking it (or pressing Enter/Space when it is focused) toggles the details open and closed. It must be the first child of <details>. Browsers show a small triangle marker before it, which can be styled or removed with the ::marker pseudo-element or list-style: none.

Syntax

<details>
  <summary>Label</summary>
  ...
</details>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displaylist-item
Content categoriesNone
Permitted contentPhrasing content, or one heading element
Permitted parents<details>, as its first child
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLElement

Attributes

Only the global attributes and event handler attributes.

Examples

FAQ

<details>
  <summary>What is a footer?</summary>
  <p>The bottom section of a page or section.</p>
</details>

Heading inside summary

<details>
  <summary><h3>Shipping</h3></summary>
  <p>2-4 days.</p>
</details>

Keeps the document outline; style the h3 with display: inline.

Custom marker

<style>
  summary { list-style: none; cursor: pointer; }
  summary::before { content: '+ '; }
  details[open] summary::before { content: '- '; }
</style>

Default browser CSS

summary { display: list-item; counter-increment: list-item 0; list-style: disclosure-closed inside; }
details[open] > summary { list-style-type: disclosure-open; }

Accessibility

  • Announced as a button with expanded/collapsed state.
  • Do not put links or buttons inside summary; nested interactive elements confuse users.

Common mistakes

  • Placing summary anywhere but first.
  • Using summary outside details.

See also

<details>

<sup> Superscript

current Category: Text-level semantics · Versions: HTML 3.2, HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <sup> element renders text as a superscript: smaller and above the baseline. Use it where the superscript has meaning: exponents (x²), ordinal suffixes (1<sup>st</sup>), footnote references, and abbreviations like M<sup>lle</sup>. For visual raising only, use CSS.

Syntax

x<sup>2</sup>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayinline
Content categoriesFlow content, phrasing content, palpable content
Permitted contentPhrasing content
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts phrasing content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLElement

Attributes

Only the global attributes and event handler attributes.

Examples

Exponent

<p>The area is 5<sup>2</sup> = 25 m<sup>2</sup>.</p>

Footnote reference

<p>HTML was created in 1991.<sup><a href="#fn1" id="ref1">[1]</a></sup></p>

Preventing line-height changes

<style>
  sup, sub { line-height: 0; }
</style>

Superscripts can push lines apart; zero line-height fixes it.

Default browser CSS

sup { vertical-align: super; font-size: smaller; }

Accessibility

  • Not announced; complex maths should use MathML.

Common mistakes

  • Using sup for trademark symbols where the ™ character already is superscript.

See also

<sub>, <math>

<svg> Scalable Vector Graphics root

current Category: Embedded content (SVG) · Versions: HTML5 (inline SVG)

Description

The <svg> element is the root of an inline SVG (Scalable Vector Graphics) image written directly in the HTML. SVG describes shapes with elements such as <circle>, <rect>, <line>, <path>, <text> and <g>, which scale to any size without losing sharpness, can be styled with CSS and animated with CSS or JavaScript. Inline SVG is ideal for icons, logos, charts and diagrams. SVG files can also be used through <img src="x.svg">, but then CSS from the page cannot style their insides.

The viewBox attribute defines the internal coordinate system; width and height (or CSS) define the displayed size. This book documents SVG only at the level of the <svg> root; SVG has its own large specification.

Syntax

<svg viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="100" height="100">
  <circle cx="50" cy="50" r="40"/>
</svg>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayinline
Content categoriesFlow content, phrasing content, embedded content, palpable content
Permitted contentSVG elements
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts phrasing content
Tag omissionNeither
DOM interfaceSVGSVGElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
viewBoxmin-x min-y width heightThe internal coordinate system; makes the graphic scalable.SVG
width / heightlengthDisplayed size.SVG
preserveAspectRatiokeywordHow to fit the viewBox into the viewport.SVG
xmlnshttp://www.w3.org/2000/svgNamespace; optional in HTML, required in standalone .svg files.SVG
fill, stroke, stroke-widthcolour / lengthPresentation attributes for shapes (can also be CSS).SVG
role, aria-label, aria-labelledby-Accessibility name and role for the graphic.ARIA

Examples

Icon

<svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="24" height="24" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false">
  <path d="M12 2L2 7l10 5 10-5-10-5z" fill="currentColor"/>
</svg>

currentColor makes the icon follow the text colour.

Accessible logo

<svg viewBox="0 0 200 60" width="200" height="60" role="img" aria-labelledby="t">
  <title id="t">Book Store</title>
  <rect width="200" height="60" rx="8" fill="#e60000"/>
  <text x="100" y="38" text-anchor="middle" fill="#fff" font-size="24">Book Store</text>
</svg>

Responsive SVG

<style>
  svg { width: 100%; height: auto; }
</style>

Default browser CSS

svg:not(:root) { overflow: hidden; }

Accessibility

  • Decorative SVG: aria-hidden="true". Meaningful SVG: role="img" with <title> and aria-labelledby.
  • Text in SVG <text> is real text and is readable, unlike text in raster images.

Common mistakes

  • Omitting viewBox so the graphic does not scale.
  • Forgetting focusable="false" for inline icons in old Internet Explorer.
  • Huge inline SVGs repeated many times; use <use> or an external sprite.

See also

<img>, <canvas>, <math>, <picture>

<table> Table

current Category: Table content · Versions: HTML 3.2, HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <table> element represents tabular data: information arranged in a two-dimensional grid of rows and columns, where the position of each cell gives it meaning (this value belongs to this row and this column). Examples: price lists, timetables, statistics, comparison charts, spreadsheets.

A table is built row by row. <tr> creates a row; inside it <th> creates a header cell and <td> a data cell. Optional <thead>, <tbody> and <tfoot> group the rows; <caption> gives the table a title; <colgroup> and <col> describe columns. The cells of each row must add up to the same number of columns, taking colspan and rowspan into account.

Tables were introduced in HTML 3.2 and were immediately misused for page layout because there was no CSS. Layout tables are wrong today: they are inaccessible (screen readers announce rows and columns that mean nothing), not responsive, and hard to maintain. Use CSS flexbox and grid for layout; use <table> only for data.

Browsers render tables without borders by default. Add them with CSS. border-collapse: collapse merges adjacent cell borders into single lines, which is almost always what you want.

Syntax

<table>
  <caption>Title</caption>
  <thead><tr><th>Head</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody><tr><td>Data</td></tr></tbody>
</table>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displaytable
Content categoriesFlow content, palpable content
Permitted contentIn this order: an optional <caption>, zero or more <colgroup>, an optional <thead>, either zero or more <tbody> or one or more <tr>, an optional <tfoot>; <script> and <template> may be intermixed
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts flow content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLTableElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
alignleft | center | rightObsolete. Alignment of the table on the page. Use CSS margin.HTML 3.2
bgcolorcolourObsolete. Background colour. Use CSS background-color.HTML 3.2
borderpixelsObsolete. Border width around the table and cells. Use CSS border.HTML 3.2
cellpaddingpixelsObsolete. Space between cell content and cell border. Use CSS padding on td/th.HTML 3.2
cellspacingpixelsObsolete. Space between cells. Use CSS border-spacing or border-collapse.HTML 3.2
framevoid | above | below | hsides | lhs | rhs | vsides | box | borderObsolete. Which outer borders to draw. Use CSS border.HTML 4.01
rulesnone | groups | rows | cols | allObsolete. Which inner borders to draw. Use CSS border on cells.HTML 4.01
summarytextObsolete. Description of the table for screen readers. Use <caption> or aria-describedby.HTML 4.01
widthpixels or percentageObsolete. Table width. Use CSS width.HTML 3.2
heightpixelsObsolete, non-standard. Use CSS.Netscape

Examples

A complete data table

<table>
  <caption>Book prices, September 2026</caption>
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th scope="col">Title</th>
      <th scope="col">Format</th>
      <th scope="col">Price (EGP)</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td>Learn HTML</td>
      <td>PDF</td>
      <td>120</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <td>Learn CSS</td>
      <td>PDF</td>
      <td>140</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
  <tfoot>
    <tr>
      <th scope="row" colspan="2">Total</th>
      <td>260</td>
    </tr>
  </tfoot>
</table>

Essential CSS for tables

<style>
  table { border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; }
  th, td { border: 1px solid #ccc; padding: 8px 12px; text-align: left; }
  th { background: #f4f4f4; }
  tbody tr:nth-child(even) { background: #fafafa; }
  tbody tr:hover { background: #fff4e0; }
  td.num { text-align: right; }
</style>

border-collapse removes double lines; nth-child gives zebra stripes; right-align numbers.

Row and column headers together

<table>
  <tr>
    <td></td>
    <th scope="col">Mon</th>
    <th scope="col">Tue</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th scope="row">Morning</th>
    <td>HTML</td>
    <td>CSS</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th scope="row">Afternoon</th>
    <td>Practice</td>
    <td>Project</td>
  </tr>
</table>

Spanning cells

<table>
  <tr>
    <th colspan="2">Name</th>
    <th rowspan="2">Age</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th>First</th>
    <th>Last</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td>Ahmed</td>
    <td>Ali</td>
    <td>20</td>
  </tr>
</table>

Each row still totals three columns.

Responsive: horizontal scroll on small screens

<div style="overflow-x: auto">
  <table>...</table>
</div>

HTML 3.2 style attributes and their CSS replacement

<!-- Old -->
<table border="1" cellpadding="5" cellspacing="0" width="100%" bgcolor="#eeeeee">

<!-- New -->
<style>
  table { border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; background: #eee; }
  td, th { border: 1px solid #000; padding: 5px; }
</style>
<table>

Default browser CSS

table { display: table; border-collapse: separate; border-spacing: 2px; box-sizing: border-box; text-indent: initial; }

Accessibility

  • Use <th> with scope for every header so screen readers can announce 'Price, 120' instead of just '120'.
  • Give every data table a <caption>.
  • Avoid layout tables; if unavoidable, add role="presentation".
  • Do not nest tables.
  • For complex tables with multi-level headers, use the headers attribute on cells.

Common mistakes

  • Using tables for layout.
  • Rows with different numbers of cells.
  • Forgetting border-collapse and getting double borders.
  • Using <td> for headers.
  • Placing text directly inside <table> or <tr>.

See also

<tr>, <td>, <th>, <thead>, <tbody>, <tfoot>, <caption>, <colgroup>, <col>

<tbody> Table body

current Category: Table content · Versions: HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <tbody> element groups the main data rows of a table, as distinct from the header rows in <thead> and the summary rows in <tfoot>. A table may have several <tbody> elements to group rows into sections (for example one per category), which can then be styled separately. When you write <tr> directly inside <table> without a <tbody>, the browser creates one automatically, so a tbody is always present in the DOM.

Using explicit thead/tbody/tfoot lets browsers repeat the header on every printed page of a long table and lets CSS make the body scroll independently.

Syntax

<tbody>
  <tr>...</tr>
</tbody>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displaytable-row-group
Content categoriesNone
Permitted contentZero or more <tr>, <script>, <template>
Permitted parents<table>, after <caption>, <colgroup> and <thead>
Tag omissionStart tag may be omitted if the first thing inside is a <tr> and it is not preceded by a tbody, thead or tfoot whose end tag was omitted; end tag may be omitted if followed by <tbody> or <tfoot> or if there is no more content in the parent
DOM interfaceHTMLTableSectionElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
align, bgcolor, char, charoff, valignvariousObsolete presentational attributes. Use CSS.HTML 4.01

Examples

Multiple bodies for grouped rows

<table>
  <thead><tr><th>Item</th><th>Price</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><th colspan="2">Books</th></tr>
    <tr><td>Learn HTML</td><td>120</td></tr>
  </tbody>
  <tbody>
    <tr><th colspan="2">Courses</th></tr>
    <tr><td>CSS Basics</td><td>300</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

Scrolling body with fixed header

<style>
  .wrap { max-height: 300px; overflow-y: auto; }
  thead th { position: sticky; top: 0; background: #fff; }
</style>
<div class="wrap"><table>...</table></div>

Default browser CSS

tbody { display: table-row-group; vertical-align: middle; }

Accessibility

  • No special role; it exists for structure and styling.

Common mistakes

  • Putting tbody before thead.
  • Placing cells directly inside tbody without tr.

See also

<table>, <thead>, <tfoot>, <tr>

<td> Table data cell

current Category: Table content · Versions: HTML 3.2, HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <td> element defines a cell of a table that contains data. It must be inside a <tr>. Each <td> occupies one column by default; colspan makes it span several columns and rowspan several rows. The headers attribute can list the ids of the <th> cells that describe it, which is needed only for complex tables where scope is not enough.

Data cells are left-aligned and normal weight by default, in contrast to header cells (<th>) which are bold and centred. Use <th> for headers even if you restyle them, because the distinction is what screen readers rely on.

Syntax

<tr>
  <td>Data</td>
</tr>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displaytable-cell
Content categoriesSectioning root
Permitted contentFlow content
Permitted parents<tr>
Tag omissionStart tag required; end tag may be omitted if followed by <td> or <th> or if there is no more content in the parent
DOM interfaceHTMLTableCellElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
colspanpositive integerNumber of columns the cell spans. Default 1, maximum 1000.HTML 3.2
rowspannon-negative integerNumber of rows the cell spans. Default 1; 0 means to the end of the row group. Maximum 65534.HTML 3.2
headersspace-separated idsThe ids of <th> cells that provide headers for this cell.HTML 4.01
abbrtextObsolete on td (valid on th). Abbreviated description.HTML 4.01
alignleft | center | right | justify | charObsolete. Use CSS text-align.HTML 3.2
axistextObsolete. Category names.HTML 4.01
bgcolorcolourObsolete. Use CSS background-color.HTML 3.2
char / charoffcharacter / numberObsolete. Character alignment.HTML 4.01
heightpixelsObsolete. Use CSS height.HTML 3.2
nowrapbooleanObsolete. Use CSS white-space: nowrap.HTML 3.2
scope-Obsolete on td (use on th).HTML 4.01
valigntop | middle | bottom | baselineObsolete. Use CSS vertical-align.HTML 3.2
widthpixels or percentageObsolete. Use CSS width.HTML 3.2

Examples

Basic cells

<table>
  <tr>
    <th>Name</th>
    <th>Age</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td>Ahmed</td>
    <td>20</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td>Sara</td>
    <td>22</td>
  </tr>
</table>

Row 1 has header cells, rows 2 and 3 have data cells.

colspan and rowspan

<table>
  <tr>
    <td rowspan="2">Spans two rows</td>
    <td>Row 1</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td>Row 2</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td colspan="2">Spans two columns</td>
  </tr>
</table>

Complex header association

<table>
  <tr>
    <th id="n">Name</th>
    <th id="q1">Q1</th>
    <th id="q2">Q2</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th id="r1" headers="n">Ahmed</th>
    <td headers="r1 q1">10</td>
    <td headers="r1 q2">12</td>
  </tr>
</table>

Cell styling

<style>
  td { padding: 8px 12px; border-bottom: 1px solid #e0e0e0; vertical-align: top; }
  td.num { text-align: right; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
</style>

Default browser CSS

td { display: table-cell; vertical-align: inherit; padding: 1px; }

Accessibility

  • Do not leave header cells as <td>.
  • Empty cells are fine; do not fill them with &nbsp; unless needed for old-browser borders.

Common mistakes

  • Placing <td> outside <tr>.
  • Inconsistent column counts.
  • Using td for headers.

See also

<th>, <tr>, <table>

<template> Content template

current Category: Scripting / web components · Versions: HTML5 (2013)

Description

The <template> element holds HTML that is not rendered when the page loads but can be cloned and inserted into the document later by JavaScript. The content is parsed into a separate document fragment (template.content): scripts inside do not run, images do not load and the markup is invisible. It is the standard way to define reusable markup for lists, cards and web components.

Declarative Shadow DOM uses <template shadowrootmode="open"> inside a custom element to create a shadow root without JavaScript.

Syntax

<template id="t">
  <li class="item"></li>
</template>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displaynone
Content categoriesMetadata content, flow content, phrasing content, script-supporting element
Permitted contentAnything (stored in a DocumentFragment, not rendered)
Permitted parentsAlmost anywhere: head, body, and inside table, colgroup, dl, ol, ul, select...
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLTemplateElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
shadowrootmodeopen | closedCreates a declarative shadow root on the parent element.Living Standard
shadowrootdelegatesfocusbooleanSets delegatesFocus on the declarative shadow root.Living Standard
shadowrootclonablebooleanSets clonable on the declarative shadow root.Living Standard
shadowrootserializablebooleanSets serializable on the declarative shadow root.Living Standard

Examples

Cloning a row template

<table id="cart"><tbody></tbody></table>
<template id="row">
  <tr><td class="name"></td><td class="price"></td></tr>
</template>
<script>
  const items = [['Learn HTML', 120], ['Learn CSS', 140]];
  const tpl = document.getElementById('row');
  const body = document.querySelector('#cart tbody');
  for (const [name, price] of items) {
    const clone = tpl.content.cloneNode(true);
    clone.querySelector('.name').textContent = name;
    clone.querySelector('.price').textContent = price;
    body.append(clone);
  }
</script>

Declarative shadow DOM

<my-card>
  <template shadowrootmode="open">
    <style>p { color: #b90000; }</style>
    <p><slot></slot></p>
  </template>
  Hello from the light DOM
</my-card>

Default browser CSS

template { display: none; }

Accessibility

  • Template content is not in the accessibility tree until inserted.

Common mistakes

  • Using innerHTML on template instead of template.content.
  • Expecting scripts inside the template to run before insertion.

See also

<slot>, <script>, <noscript>

<textarea> Multi-line text input

current Category: Forms · Versions: HTML 2.0, HTML 3.2, HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <textarea> element creates a multi-line plain-text editing control, for comments, messages, addresses and any free-form text. Unlike <input>, it is not a void element: its initial value is the text between its tags, not a value attribute. Whitespace and line breaks inside the tags are preserved, so keep the closing tag right after the text to avoid unwanted spaces.

The rows and cols attributes set its visible size in lines and characters; CSS width/height are more flexible. Most browsers let the user drag-resize it; control this with the CSS resize property. The field-sizing: content CSS property (new) makes it grow with its content.

Syntax

<textarea name="n" rows="4" cols="40">initial text</textarea>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayinline-block
Content categoriesFlow content, phrasing content, interactive content, listed, labelable, resettable, submittable, form-associated, palpable
Permitted contentText
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts phrasing content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLTextAreaElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
nametextName submitted with the form.HTML 2.0
rowspositive integerVisible number of lines. Default 2.HTML 2.0
colspositive integerVisible width in average characters. Default 20.HTML 2.0
placeholdertextHint shown when empty. Not a label.HTML5
requiredbooleanMust not be empty.HTML5
disabledbooleanCannot be used or submitted.HTML 4.01
readonlybooleanCannot be edited; is submitted.HTML 4.01
maxlengthintegerMaximum characters.HTML5
minlengthintegerMinimum characters.HTML5
wrapsoft | hard | offsoft (default): lines wrap visually but newlines are not submitted. hard: newlines are inserted at wrap points when submitting (requires cols). off: no wrapping (non-standard).HTML5
autocompleteon | off | tokenAutofill hint (street-address, etc.).HTML5
autofocusbooleanFocus on load.HTML5
spellchecktrue | falseEnable or disable spell checking (global).HTML5
dirnametextSubmit text direction.HTML5
formform idAssociated form.HTML5

Examples

Message field

<label for="msg">Message</label>
<textarea id="msg" name="message" rows="5" placeholder="Write your message..." required maxlength="500"></textarea>

With initial text

<textarea name="bio">Write a short bio here.</textarea>

Styling and resize control

<style>
  textarea { width: 100%; min-height: 120px; padding: 8px; font: inherit; resize: vertical; box-sizing: border-box; }
</style>

Character counter

<textarea id="t" maxlength="200"></textarea>
<output id="c" for="t">0 / 200</output>
<script>
  t.addEventListener('input', () => c.value = t.value.length + ' / 200');
</script>

Default browser CSS

textarea { display: inline-block; white-space: pre-wrap; resize: both; }

Accessibility

  • Label it.
  • Do not remove the resize handle without good reason.
  • Announce character limits in the label or description.

Common mistakes

  • Writing <textarea value="..."> (value is not an attribute here).
  • Indenting the content and getting leading spaces.
  • Forgetting the closing tag; everything after becomes part of the textarea.

See also

<input>, <form>, <label>, <output>

<tfoot> Table footer

current Category: Table content · Versions: HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <tfoot> element groups the rows that summarise the columns of a table: totals, averages, counts. In HTML5 it is placed after the <tbody> elements (HTML 4.01 required it before them so that the browser could render the footer before receiving all data). When printing a long table, browsers can repeat the tfoot at the bottom of every page.

Syntax

<tfoot>
  <tr><th>Total</th><td>260</td></tr>
</tfoot>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displaytable-footer-group
Content categoriesNone
Permitted contentZero or more <tr>, <script>, <template>
Permitted parents<table>, after caption, colgroup, thead and tbody
Tag omissionEnd tag may be omitted if there is no more content in the parent
DOM interfaceHTMLTableSectionElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
align, bgcolor, char, charoff, valignvariousObsolete presentational attributes. Use CSS.HTML 4.01

Examples

Totals row

<table>
  <thead><tr><th>Item</th><th>Price</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td>Book</td><td>120</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Pen</td><td>10</td></tr>
  </tbody>
  <tfoot>
    <tr><th scope="row">Total</th><td>130</td></tr>
  </tfoot>
</table>

Styling

<style>
  tfoot { font-weight: bold; background: #f4f4f4; border-top: 2px solid #333; }
</style>

Default browser CSS

tfoot { display: table-footer-group; vertical-align: middle; }

Accessibility

  • No special role, but grouping totals in tfoot helps users understand the table structure.

Common mistakes

  • Placing tfoot in the middle of the table.
  • Multiple tfoot elements.

See also

<table>, <thead>, <tbody>

<th> Table header cell

current Category: Table content · Versions: HTML 3.2, HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <th> element defines a header cell in a table: a cell that labels a column or a row rather than holding data. Browsers render it bold and centred. The scope attribute states whether the header applies to its column (col), its row (row), a group of columns (colgroup) or a group of rows (rowgroup). Browsers can usually guess for simple tables, but stating it explicitly is best practice because screen readers use the header text when reading each data cell.

Syntax

<th scope="col">Header</th>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displaytable-cell
Content categoriesNone
Permitted contentFlow content, but no header, footer, sectioning content or heading content
Permitted parents<tr>
Tag omissionEnd tag may be omitted if followed by <td> or <th> or if there is no more content in the parent
DOM interfaceHTMLTableCellElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
scoperow | col | rowgroup | colgroupWhich cells this header describes.HTML 4.01
colspanpositive integerColumns spanned.HTML 3.2
rowspannon-negative integerRows spanned.HTML 3.2
headersspace-separated idsOther header cells that apply to this one (for multi-level headers).HTML 4.01
abbrtextA short alternative label that screen readers may use when reading the header repeatedly.HTML 4.01
align, axis, bgcolor, char, charoff, height, nowrap, valign, widthvariousObsolete presentational attributes. Use CSS.HTML 3.2 / 4.01

Examples

Column and row headers

<table>
  <tr>
    <th scope="col">Product</th>
    <th scope="col">Price</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th scope="row">Notebook</th>
    <td>25</td>
  </tr>
</table>

A screen reader on the '25' cell announces: 'Notebook, Price, 25'.

Group headers

<table>
  <tr>
    <th scope="colgroup" colspan="2">2025</th>
    <th scope="colgroup" colspan="2">2026</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <th scope="col">Q1</th><th scope="col">Q2</th>
    <th scope="col">Q1</th><th scope="col">Q2</th>
  </tr>
</table>

Left-aligned headers

<style>
  th { text-align: left; background: #f4f4f4; }
  th[scope="row"] { font-weight: 600; }
</style>

Default browser CSS

th { display: table-cell; vertical-align: inherit; font-weight: bold; text-align: center; padding: 1px; }

Accessibility

  • Always use <th> for headers and set scope.
  • Use abbr for long headers that will be repeated often.

Common mistakes

  • Using <td> with bold styling instead of <th>.
  • Omitting scope in tables with both row and column headers.

See also

<td>, <tr>, <table>, <thead>

<thead> Table header

current Category: Table content · Versions: HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <thead> element groups the rows that hold the column headers of a table. It comes after any <caption> and <colgroup> and before <tbody> and <tfoot>. Browsers repeat the thead at the top of each printed page of a long table, and CSS position: sticky on its cells keeps the headers visible while scrolling. A table may have at most one thead.

Syntax

<thead>
  <tr><th>Column</th></tr>
</thead>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displaytable-header-group
Content categoriesNone
Permitted contentZero or more <tr>, <script>, <template>
Permitted parents<table>, after caption and colgroup, before tbody, tfoot and tr
Tag omissionEnd tag may be omitted if followed by <tbody> or <tfoot>
DOM interfaceHTMLTableSectionElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
align, bgcolor, char, charoff, valignvariousObsolete presentational attributes. Use CSS.HTML 4.01

Examples

Header group

<table>
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th scope="col">Name</th>
      <th scope="col">Email</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td>Ahmed</td><td>ahmed@example.com</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

Sticky header

<style>
  thead th { position: sticky; top: 0; background: #fff; box-shadow: 0 1px 0 #ccc; }
</style>

Default browser CSS

thead { display: table-header-group; vertical-align: middle; }

Accessibility

  • Helps assistive technology identify header rows; combine with th scope="col".

Common mistakes

  • Two thead elements.
  • Putting data rows in thead.

See also

<table>, <tbody>, <tfoot>, <th>

<time> Date / time

current Category: Text-level semantics · Versions: HTML5

Description

The <time> element represents a specific period in time: a date, a time of day, a date and time, a duration, a week or a month. The optional datetime attribute holds the value in a machine-readable format so that browsers, search engines, calendars and scripts can understand it, while the visible content can be written in any human-friendly way ('11 September 2026', 'yesterday', '١١ سبتمبر'). If datetime is omitted, the text content itself must be in a valid format.

Syntax

<time datetime="2026-09-11">11 September 2026</time>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayinline
Content categoriesFlow content, phrasing content, palpable content
Permitted contentPhrasing content
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts phrasing content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLTimeElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
datetimedate/time stringMachine-readable value. Formats: 2026-09-11 (date); 14:30 or 14:30:00 (time); 2026-09-11T14:30 (local date-time); 2026-09-11T14:30Z or 2026-09-11T14:30+02:00 (with time zone); 2026-09 (month); 2026-W37 (week); 2026 (year); 09-11 (yearless date); PT2H30M or 2h 30m (duration).HTML5

Examples

Publication date

<p>Published <time datetime="2026-09-11">11 September 2026</time></p>

Event with time zone

<p>The webinar starts at <time datetime="2026-10-01T19:00+02:00">7 pm Cairo time on 1 October</time>.</p>

Duration

<p>Reading time: <time datetime="PT8M">8 minutes</time></p>

Relative text with exact value

<p>Posted <time datetime="2026-09-10T09:15Z" title="10 Sep 2026, 09:15 UTC">yesterday</time></p>

Default browser CSS

time { display: inline; }

Accessibility

  • Screen readers read the visible text, not datetime; keep the visible text understandable.

Common mistakes

  • Invalid datetime formats such as 11/09/2026.
  • Using <time> for vague periods ('the Middle Ages').

See also

<data>, <article>

<title> Document title

current Category: Document metadata · Versions: HTML 1, HTML 2.0, HTML 3.2, HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <title> element defines the title of the document, shown in the browser's title bar or tab, used as the default name for bookmarks, displayed as the clickable headline in search engine results, and announced first by screen readers when the page loads. It contains text only; any tags inside are treated as literal text. Every document must have exactly one <title>, inside <head>.

A good title is unique for each page, describes the page's content, puts the most specific information first ('Learn HTML - Book Store' rather than 'Book Store - Learn HTML'), and is under about 60 characters so search engines do not truncate it.

Syntax

<title>Page title</title>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displaynone
Content categoriesMetadata content
Permitted contentText (not inter-element whitespace only)
Permitted parents<head> (exactly one)
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLTitleElement

Attributes

Only the global attributes and event handler attributes.

Examples

Good titles

<title>Learn HTML (PDF) - Book Store</title>
<title>Contact us - Book Store</title>
<title>Order #1042 confirmed - Book Store</title>

Changing the title from JavaScript

<script>
  document.title = '(3) New messages - Chat';
</script>

Default browser CSS

title { display: none; }

Accessibility

  • The title is the first thing announced; unique, descriptive titles are a WCAG requirement (2.4.2).

Common mistakes

  • Same title on every page.
  • Empty or missing title.
  • Putting HTML tags inside.
  • Keyword stuffing.

See also

<head>, <meta>, <h1>

<tr> Table row

current Category: Table content · Versions: HTML 3.2, HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <tr> element defines a row of cells in a table. It contains <th> (header) and/or <td> (data) cells and is placed inside <table>, <thead>, <tbody> or <tfoot>. Rows are the fundamental unit of table construction: you build a table one row at a time, and the columns emerge from the cells in each row.

Syntax

<tr>
  <td>Cell 1</td>
  <td>Cell 2</td>
</tr>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displaytable-row
Content categoriesNone
Permitted contentZero or more <td>, <th>, <script>, <template>
Permitted parents<table> (directly), <thead>, <tbody>, <tfoot>
Tag omissionEnd tag may be omitted if followed by another <tr> or if there is no more content in the parent
DOM interfaceHTMLTableRowElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
alignleft | center | right | justify | charObsolete. Use CSS text-align on cells.HTML 3.2
bgcolorcolourObsolete. Use CSS background-color.HTML 3.2
char / charoffcharacter / numberObsolete.HTML 4.01
valigntop | middle | bottom | baselineObsolete. Use CSS vertical-align.HTML 3.2

Examples

Three rows

<table>
  <tr>
    <th>Name</th>
    <th>Age</th>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td>Ahmed</td>
    <td>20</td>
  </tr>
  <tr>
    <td>Sara</td>
    <td>22</td>
  </tr>
</table>

Row styling

<style>
  tr:nth-child(even) { background: #f9f9f9; }
  tr:hover { background: #eef; }
  tr.selected { outline: 2px solid #1b6fd8; }
</style>

Adding a row with JavaScript

<script>
  const row = document.querySelector('table').insertRow();
  row.insertCell().textContent = 'Omar';
  row.insertCell().textContent = '25';
</script>

Default browser CSS

tr { display: table-row; vertical-align: inherit; }

Accessibility

  • Screen readers announce row numbers; keep one logical record per row.

Common mistakes

  • Text or elements directly inside <tr> that are not td/th.
  • Different numbers of cells per row.
  • Nesting tr inside td without a new table.

See also

<table>, <td>, <th>, <thead>, <tbody>, <tfoot>

<track> Text track for media

current Category: Image and multimedia · Versions: HTML5

Description

The <track> element adds timed text tracks to <audio> or <video>: subtitles (translations), captions (dialogue plus sound descriptions for deaf and hard-of-hearing viewers), descriptions (spoken description of the video for blind users), chapters (navigation) and metadata (for scripts). Tracks are WebVTT files (.vtt). It is a void element placed after any <source> elements.

Only one track per kind may have the default attribute. Track files loaded from another origin require CORS headers and the crossorigin attribute on the media element.

Syntax

<track kind="captions" src="captions.vtt" srclang="en" label="English" default>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementYes (no closing tag)
Default displaynone
Content categoriesNone
Permitted contentNone (void element)
Permitted parents<audio>, <video>, after <source> and before flow content
Tag omissionNo end tag
DOM interfaceHTMLTrackElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
srcURLRequired. The WebVTT file.HTML5
kindsubtitles | captions | descriptions | chapters | metadataThe type of track. Default subtitles.HTML5
srclanglanguage tagLanguage of the track. Required for subtitles.HTML5
labeltextHuman-readable title shown in the track menu.HTML5
defaultbooleanEnable this track by default (one per kind).HTML5

Examples

Video with captions and subtitles

<video controls width="640" height="360">
  <source src="lesson.mp4" type="video/mp4">
  <track kind="captions" src="lesson-en.vtt" srclang="en" label="English captions" default>
  <track kind="subtitles" src="lesson-ar.vtt" srclang="ar" label="العربية">
  <track kind="chapters" src="chapters.vtt" srclang="en">
</video>

A WebVTT file

WEBVTT

00:00:00.000 --> 00:00:04.000
Welcome to the HTML course.

00:00:04.500 --> 00:00:08.000
Today we learn about the footer element.

Save as lesson-en.vtt; the first line must be WEBVTT.

Default browser CSS

track { display: none; }

Accessibility

  • Captions are required for accessible video (WCAG 1.2.2). Subtitles alone are not captions: captions also describe sounds.
  • Provide descriptions for visual-only information.

Common mistakes

  • Placing track before source.
  • Wrong MIME type on the server (should be text/vtt).
  • Two default tracks of the same kind.

See also

<video>, <audio>, <source>

<tt> Teletype text (obsolete)

obsolete Category: Obsolete presentational · Versions: HTML 2.0, HTML 3.2, HTML 4.01; obsolete in HTML5

Description

The <tt> element (teletype) rendered text in a monospace font, imitating a teletype or typewriter. It was purely presentational and HTML5 removed it. Use the semantic elements <code>, <kbd>, <samp> or <var>, or CSS font-family: monospace on a <span>.

Syntax

<tt>text</tt>

Void elementNo
Default displayinline

Permitted contentPhrasing content
Permitted parentsPhrasing content
Tag omissionNeither
