Only the global attributes and event handler attributes.

Examples

Replacements

<!-- Old -->
<tt>ls -la</tt>

<!-- New -->
<kbd>ls -la</kbd>  <!-- user input -->
<code>ls -la</code> <!-- code -->
<span style="font-family: monospace">ls -la</span> <!-- style only -->

Default browser CSS

tt { font-family: monospace; }

Common mistakes

  • Any use.

See also

<code>, <kbd>, <samp>, <var>, <pre>

<u> Unarticulated annotation (underline)

current Category: Text-level semantics · Versions: HTML 3.2, HTML 4.01 (deprecated), HTML5 (redefined)

Description

The <u> element represents a span of inline text that should be rendered in a way that indicates a non-textual annotation: most commonly, marking misspelled words (as a word processor does with a wavy red line) or labelling proper names in Chinese text. Browsers render it with a solid underline. In HTML 4 <u> simply meant 'underline' and was deprecated; HTML5 redefined it.

Because underlined text looks like a link on the web, avoid <u> for anything that is not one of its intended uses. For emphasis use <em>; for titles <cite>; for pure decoration CSS text-decoration.

Syntax

<u>text</u>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayinline
Content categoriesFlow content, phrasing content, palpable content
Permitted contentPhrasing content
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts phrasing content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLElement

Attributes

Only the global attributes and event handler attributes.

Examples

Spelling error

<p>Please chek <u class="spelling">recieve</u> before sending.</p>
<style>.spelling { text-decoration: red wavy underline; }</style>

Wrong use

<!-- Do not do this: looks like a link and carries no meaning -->
<p><u>Important</u></p>

<!-- Do this -->
<p><strong>Important</strong></p>

Default browser CSS

u { text-decoration: underline; }

Accessibility

  • Underlined non-link text confuses users; they may try to click it.

Common mistakes

  • Using <u> for emphasis or headings.

See also

<em>, <ins>, <s>, <span>

<ul> Unordered list

current Category: Text content · Versions: HTML 1, HTML 2.0, HTML 3.2, HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <ul> element represents an unordered list of items: a list where changing the order would not change the meaning, such as a shopping list, a set of features, or the links of a navigation menu. Browsers show each item with a bullet. Each item is an <li>. If the order matters, use <ol>.

Lists are among the most useful elements in HTML because they carry structure: screen readers announce how many items there are and let users jump between them. Navigation menus are almost always built as a <ul> inside a <nav>, with CSS removing the bullets and arranging the items horizontally.

Syntax

<ul>
  <li>Item</li>
  <li>Item</li>
</ul>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayblock
Content categoriesFlow content; palpable if it has at least one <li>
Permitted contentZero or more <li>, <script>, <template>
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts flow content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLUListElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
typedisc | circle | squareObsolete. Bullet style. Use CSS list-style-type.HTML 3.2
compactbooleanObsolete. Compact rendering.HTML 2.0

Examples

Shopping list

<ul>
  <li>Milk</li>
  <li>Bread</li>
  <li>Eggs</li>
</ul>

Shows three bulleted lines.

Nested lists

<ul>
  <li>Fruit
    <ul>
      <li>Apples</li>
      <li>Bananas</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li>Vegetables</li>
</ul>

Nested lists get a different bullet automatically (disc, then circle, then square).

Bullet styles

<ul style="list-style-type: square">...</ul>
<ul style="list-style-type: '✓ '">...</ul>
<ul style="list-style-image: url(star.png)">...</ul>

Navigation menu

<style>
  .menu { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; display: flex; gap: 20px; }
</style>
<nav>
  <ul class="menu">
    <li><a href="/">Home</a></li>
    <li><a href="/shop">Shop</a></li>
    <li><a href="/contact">Contact</a></li>
  </ul>
</nav>

Custom bullets with ::marker

<style>
  li::marker { color: #e60000; font-size: 1.2em; }
</style>

Default browser CSS

ul { display: block; list-style-type: disc; margin: 1em 0; padding-inline-start: 40px; }

Accessibility

  • Announced as 'list, 3 items'. In Safari, list-style: none removes list semantics; add role="list" to the ul to keep them.

Common mistakes

  • Text directly inside <ul> outside <li>.
  • Using <ul> for ordered steps.
  • Using <br> or paragraphs with dashes instead of a real list.

See also

<ol>, <li>, <menu>, <dl>, <nav>

<var> Variable

current Category: Text-level semantics · Versions: HTML 2.0, HTML 3.2, HTML 4.01, HTML5

Description

The <var> element represents the name of a variable in a mathematical expression or a programming context, or a placeholder for a value the reader must supply. Browsers render it in italics. It is one of the four 'computer' phrase elements together with <code>, <kbd> and <samp>.

Syntax

<var>x</var>

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayinline
Content categoriesFlow content, phrasing content, palpable content
Permitted contentPhrasing content
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts phrasing content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLElement

Attributes

Only the global attributes and event handler attributes.

Examples

Maths

<p>The area is <var>w</var> × <var>h</var>.</p>

Placeholder in instructions

<p>Type <kbd>cd <var>folder-name</var></kbd> to enter a folder.</p>

Default browser CSS

var { font-style: italic; }

  • Using <i> or <em> for variables.

See also

<code>, <kbd>, <samp>, <math>

<video> Embedded video

current Category: Image and multimedia · Versions: HTML5

Description

The <video> element embeds a video player in the document. The video file is given by src or by one or more <source> children (so that the browser can pick a supported format), followed by optional <track> elements for captions and subtitles, and finally fallback content for browsers without video support. Common formats are MP4 (H.264/AAC, universally supported), WebM (VP9/AV1, smaller) and, in Safari, HEVC.

The controls attribute shows the built-in play/pause, seek, volume, captions, picture-in-picture and fullscreen controls. Without it you must provide your own controls through the HTMLMediaElement API. Autoplay with sound is blocked by browsers; autoplay muted (for background video) is allowed. Set width and height or CSS aspect-ratio to prevent layout shift, and use preload="none" or "metadata" to avoid downloading large files that may never be played.

Syntax

<video src="clip.mp4" controls width="640" height="360"></video>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayinline
Content categoriesFlow content, phrasing content, embedded content; interactive and palpable if controls is present
Permitted contentIf src: zero or more <track> then transparent content with no media elements. Otherwise: zero or more <source>, zero or more <track>, then transparent content with no media elements
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts embedded content
Tag omissionNeither tag may be omitted
DOM interfaceHTMLVideoElement

Attributes

In addition to the global and event attributes:

AttributeValuesDescriptionSince
srcURLThe video file. Or use <source> children.HTML5
controlsbooleanShow built-in controls.HTML5
autoplaybooleanStart automatically (only reliable with muted).HTML5
loopbooleanRepeat when finished.HTML5
mutedbooleanStart muted.HTML5
posterURLImage shown before the video plays or while loading.HTML5
preloadnone | metadata | autoHow much to download before play.HTML5
width / heightpixelsDisplay size; also prevents layout shift.HTML5
playsinlinebooleanOn iPhone, play inline instead of forcing fullscreen.Living Standard
crossoriginanonymous | use-credentialsCORS mode for the media (needed for canvas processing and cross-origin tracks).HTML5
controlslistnodownload | nofullscreen | noremoteplaybackHide specific native controls (Chromium).Non-standard
disablepictureinpicturebooleanHide the picture-in-picture option.Living Standard
disableremoteplaybackbooleanDisable casting.Living Standard

Examples

Complete accessible video

<video controls width="640" height="360" poster="poster.jpg" preload="metadata">
  <source src="lesson.webm" type="video/webm">
  <source src="lesson.mp4" type="video/mp4">
  <track kind="captions" src="lesson-en.vtt" srclang="en" label="English" default>
  <p>Your browser cannot play this video. <a href="lesson.mp4">Download it</a>.</p>
</video>

Background hero video

<video autoplay muted loop playsinline poster="hero.jpg" aria-hidden="true">
  <source src="hero.mp4" type="video/mp4">
</video>

Muted autoplay is allowed; aria-hidden because it is decorative. Respect prefers-reduced-motion by pausing it with JavaScript.

Responsive sizing

<style>
  video { width: 100%; height: auto; aspect-ratio: 16 / 9; background: #000; }
</style>

Custom play button

<video id="v" src="clip.mp4" width="400"></video>
<button onclick="const v = document.getElementById('v'); v.paused ? v.play() : v.pause()">Play / Pause</button>

Default browser CSS

video { object-fit: contain; }
video:not([controls]) { /* nothing shown until play */ }

Accessibility

  • Provide captions with <track kind="captions">.
  • Provide a transcript for audio and visual content.
  • Never autoplay with sound.
  • Keep native controls unless your custom controls are fully keyboard accessible.
  • Avoid flashing content.

Common mistakes

  • Expecting sound autoplay to work.
  • A single format only.
  • Huge files with preload="auto".
  • No poster, showing a black box until play.
  • Missing playsinline on iOS.

See also

<audio>, <source>, <track>, <iframe>, <picture>

<wbr> Word break opportunity

current Category: Text-level semantics · Versions: Netscape / IE extension, standardised in HTML5

Description

The <wbr> element marks a position inside a word where the browser may break the line if necessary, without inserting a hyphen or a visible character. It is useful for very long words, URLs and code identifiers that would otherwise overflow their container. If no break is needed, nothing is displayed. It is a void element.

Alternatives: the zero-width space character (&#8203;) has the same effect; the soft hyphen (&shy;) breaks with a hyphen; CSS overflow-wrap: anywhere allows breaks anywhere in overflowing words.

Syntax

Super<wbr>cali<wbr>fragilistic

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementYes (no closing tag)
Default displayinline
Content categoriesFlow content, phrasing content
Permitted contentNone (void element)
Permitted parentsAny element that accepts phrasing content
Tag omissionNo end tag
DOM interfaceHTMLElement

Attributes

Only the global attributes and event handler attributes.

Examples

Long URL

<p>Visit https://example.com/<wbr>very/<wbr>long/<wbr>path/<wbr>to/<wbr>a/<wbr>resource</p>

The URL can break after each slash instead of overflowing.

Long identifier

<code>HTMLTable<wbr>Section<wbr>Element</code>

Default browser CSS

wbr { content: '\200B'; }

Accessibility

  • Invisible to screen readers; does not affect pronunciation.

Common mistakes

  • Using <br> where a soft break is wanted.
  • Writing </wbr>.

See also

<br>, <nobr>

<xmp> Example text (obsolete)

obsolete Category: Obsolete text content · Versions: HTML 1, HTML 2.0 (deprecated); obsolete

Description

The <xmp> element (example) displayed its content literally, without interpreting any markup, in a monospace font, so that authors could show HTML source without escaping < and &. It was one of the 1991 elements, deprecated in HTML 2.0 and removed in HTML 3.2, although browsers still support it for old pages. Use <pre> with escaped entities.

Syntax

<xmp><p>shown literally</p></xmp>

Technical summary

PropertyValue
Void elementNo
Default displayblock
Content categoriesHistorical
Permitted contentRaw text
Permitted parentsFlow content
Tag omissionNeither
DOM interfaceHTMLPreElement

Attributes

Only the global attributes and event handler attributes.

Examples

Replacement

<pre>&lt;p&gt;shown literally&lt;/p&gt;</pre>

Default browser CSS

xmp { display: block; font-family: monospace; white-space: pre; margin: 1em 0; }

Common mistakes

  • Any use.

See also

<pre>, <listing>, <plaintext>, <code>

Part 7: The input Element in Depth

Input types overview

typeControlSince
textSingle-line textHTML 2.0
passwordPasswordHTML 2.0
checkboxCheck boxHTML 2.0
radioRadio buttonHTML 2.0
submitSubmit buttonHTML 2.0
resetReset buttonHTML 2.0
buttonGeneric buttonHTML 3.2
hiddenHidden fieldHTML 2.0
imageImage submit buttonHTML 2.0
fileFile chooserHTML 3.2
emailEmail addressHTML5
urlWeb addressHTML5
telTelephone numberHTML5
searchSearch fieldHTML5
numberNumeric fieldHTML5
rangeSliderHTML5
colorColour pickerHTML5
dateDateHTML5
timeTime of dayHTML5
datetime-localLocal date and timeHTML5
monthMonth and yearHTML5
weekWeek of the yearHTML5

<input type="text"> Single-line text

Since: HTML 2.0

The default type. A single-line text field. Line breaks are removed from the value. Use it for names, titles, and anything that has no more specific type.

Type-specific attributes

AttributeNote
maxlength / minlengthLength limits.
patternRegular expression to validate.
placeholderHint text.
sizeVisible width in characters.
listDatalist of suggestions.
autocompleteAutofill token such as name, given-name, organization.
dirnameSubmit text direction.

Example

<label for="n">Full name</label>
<input id="n" name="name" type="text" autocomplete="name" required>

<input type="password"> Password

Since: HTML 2.0

A single-line field whose characters are obscured with dots or asterisks. The value is still sent as plain text in the form submission, so the page must be served over HTTPS. Browsers offer to save and generate passwords when autocomplete is set to current-password or new-password.

Type-specific attributes

AttributeNote
minlength / maxlengthLength rules.
patternComplexity rules (explain them in title).
autocompletecurrent-password, new-password, one-time-code.

Example

<label for="pw">Password</label>
<input id="pw" name="password" type="password" minlength="8" autocomplete="new-password" required>

Add a 'show password' toggle for usability.

<input type="checkbox"> Check box

Since: HTML 2.0

An on/off box. Each checkbox is independent; several checkboxes may share a name to send multiple values. Only checked boxes are submitted (as name=value). The indeterminate visual state can be set from JavaScript for 'some children selected'.

Type-specific attributes

AttributeNote
checkedInitially ticked.
valueSent when checked; default 'on'.
requiredMust be ticked (useful for 'I agree').

Example

<label><input type="checkbox" name="topics" value="html" checked> HTML</label>
<label><input type="checkbox" name="topics" value="css"> CSS</label>

Wrap the input in the label so the text is clickable.

<input type="radio"> Radio button

Since: HTML 2.0

One of a group of mutually exclusive options. All radio buttons with the same name form a group and only one can be selected. Arrow keys move the selection within the group. Always provide a default or make the group required, and caption the group with fieldset/legend.

Type-specific attributes

AttributeNote
checkedInitially selected.
valueSent for the selected button.
requiredOne button in the group must be selected.

Example

<fieldset>
  <legend>Delivery</legend>
  <label><input type="radio" name="d" value="standard" checked> Standard</label>
  <label><input type="radio" name="d" value="express"> Express</label>
</fieldset>

<input type="submit"> Submit button

Since: HTML 2.0

A button that submits the form. Its value is the button's label and, if it has a name, is submitted too. Prefer the <button> element, which can contain HTML content.

Type-specific attributes

AttributeNote
valueLabel (default 'Submit').
formaction, formmethod, formenctype, formtarget, formnovalidateOverride form settings.

Example

<input type="submit" value="Send message">

<input type="reset"> Reset button

Since: HTML 2.0

A button that restores all controls of the form to their initial values. Rarely useful and often clicked by mistake; most forms omit it.

Type-specific attributes

AttributeNote
valueLabel (default 'Reset').

Example

<input type="reset" value="Clear form">

<input type="button"> Generic button

Since: HTML 3.2

A button with no default behaviour, for use with JavaScript. Prefer <button type="button">.

Type-specific attributes

AttributeNote
valueLabel.

Example

<input type="button" value="Show help" onclick="alert('Help')">

<input type="hidden"> Hidden field

Since: HTML 2.0

A control that is not displayed but whose value is submitted with the form. Used for record ids, CSRF tokens and other data the user does not edit. The name _charset_ has a special meaning: the browser fills it with the form's encoding.

Type-specific attributes

AttributeNote
valueThe value to submit.

Example

<input type="hidden" name="csrf" value="a1b2c3">

Never rely on hidden fields for security; users can change them.

<input type="image"> Image submit button

Since: HTML 2.0

A graphical submit button showing the image in src. When clicked it submits the form together with the click coordinates as name.x and name.y. Requires alt.

Type-specific attributes

AttributeNote
srcImage URL.
altRequired text alternative.
width / heightSize.
formaction etc.Override form settings.

Example

<input type="image" src="go.png" alt="Search" width="32" height="32">

<input type="file"> File chooser

Since: HTML 3.2

Lets the user select one or more files from their device to upload. The form must use method="post" and enctype="multipart/form-data". The selected files are available in JavaScript as input.files. For security the value cannot be set by script and shows only a fake path.

Type-specific attributes

AttributeNote
acceptAllowed types: image/*, video/*, audio/*, .pdf, application/pdf, .doc,.docx
multipleAllow several files.
captureuser | environment: open camera/mic directly on phones.
webkitdirectoryNon-standard: choose a folder.

Example

<label for="cv">Upload your CV (PDF)</label>
<input id="cv" name="cv" type="file" accept=".pdf,application/pdf">

<input type="email"> Email address

Since: HTML5

A text field validated as an email address (or a comma-separated list with multiple). Mobile keyboards show @ and . keys. The value is trimmed and validated as user@host; a domain without a dot is accepted.

Type-specific attributes

AttributeNote
multipleAllow several addresses separated by commas.
patternAdditional restriction, for example a company domain.
listSuggestions.
maxlength / minlength / size / placeholder / readonlyAs text.

Example

<label for="e">Email</label>
<input id="e" name="email" type="email" autocomplete="email" required>

Still validate on the server.

<input type="url"> Web address

Since: HTML5

A text field validated as an absolute URL (it must include a scheme such as https://). Mobile keyboards show / and .com keys.

Type-specific attributes

AttributeNote
patternExtra restriction, for example https only.
list, maxlength, minlength, placeholder, readonly, sizeAs text.

Example

<label for="site">Website</label>
<input id="site" name="site" type="url" placeholder="https://example.com">

<input type="tel"> Telephone number

Since: HTML5

A text field for telephone numbers. It is not validated (formats vary too much worldwide), but phones show a telephone keypad. Add pattern for a specific format.

Type-specific attributes

AttributeNote
patternFor example [0-9]{11} or \+20[0-9]{10}.
list, maxlength, minlength, placeholder, readonly, sizeAs text.

Example

<label for="t">Mobile</label>
<input id="t" name="tel" type="tel" autocomplete="tel" pattern="01[0-9]{9}" title="11 digits starting with 01">

<input type="search"> Search field

Since: HTML5

A text field for search terms. Functionally identical to text, but some browsers style it with rounded corners and a clear (x) button, and mobile keyboards show a Search key. Line breaks are removed.

Type-specific attributes

AttributeNote
list, maxlength, minlength, pattern, placeholder, readonly, sizeAs text.
incrementalNon-standard (WebKit): fire search events while typing.

Example

<search>
  <label for="q">Search</label>
  <input id="q" name="q" type="search" placeholder="Search books">
</search>

<input type="number"> Numeric field

Since: HTML5

A field for entering a number, usually with spinner arrows. Only digits, sign, decimal point and exponent are accepted; the value is validated against min, max and step. Use it only for actual quantities. For identifiers such as credit card numbers or postal codes use type="text" with inputmode="numeric" because they can have leading zeros and are not meant to be incremented.

Type-specific attributes

AttributeNote
min / maxRange.
stepIncrement; 'any' allows decimals of any precision. Default 1, which rejects 2.5 unless step is 0.5 or any.
placeholder, readonly, listAs text.

Example

<label for="qty">Quantity</label>
<input id="qty" name="qty" type="number" min="1" max="99" step="1" value="1">

Scrolling the mouse wheel over a focused number input changes the value in some browsers.

<input type="range"> Slider

Since: HTML5

A slider for choosing an approximate number where the exact value is not important, such as volume or brightness. Default range 0-100, step 1. Show the current value with an <output> because the slider itself does not display it.

Type-specific attributes

AttributeNote
min / maxRange.
stepIncrement.
listDatalist for tick marks.
orientNon-standard (Firefox): vertical.

Example

<label for="vol">Volume</label>
<input id="vol" name="vol" type="range" min="0" max="100" value="40" oninput="out.value = this.value">
<output id="out">40</output>

<input type="color"> Colour picker

Since: HTML5

A control for choosing a colour, usually opening the operating system colour picker. The value is always a lowercase hexadecimal colour such as #ff0000; alpha (transparency) is not supported unless the experimental alpha attribute is used.

Type-specific attributes

AttributeNote
valueInitial colour in #rrggbb form (default #000000).
listDatalist of suggested colours.
alpha, colorspaceExperimental.

Example

<label for="c">Theme colour</label>
<input id="c" name="color" type="color" value="#e60000">

<input type="date"> Date

Since: HTML5

A control for a year, month and day, usually with a calendar pop-up. The value is always in the format YYYY-MM-DD regardless of how the browser displays it to the user, so it is safe to process on the server. Safari on macOS supports it since version 14.1.

Type-specific attributes

AttributeNote
min / maxEarliest and latest date, as YYYY-MM-DD.
stepIn days.
listSuggested dates.
readonly, requiredAs usual.

Example

<label for="d">Delivery date</label>
<input id="d" name="date" type="date" min="2026-09-12" max="2026-12-31" required>

Set min to today's date with JavaScript to prevent past dates.

<input type="time"> Time of day

Since: HTML5

A control for hours and minutes (and optionally seconds), without a time zone. The value format is HH:MM or HH:MM:SS in 24-hour form.

Type-specific attributes

AttributeNote
min / maxAs HH:MM.
stepIn seconds; 60 = minutes only (default), 1 = show seconds.
listSuggested times.

Example

<label for="t">Appointment time</label>
<input id="t" name="time" type="time" min="09:00" max="17:00" step="900">

step 900 = 15-minute increments.

<input type="datetime-local"> Local date and time

Since: HTML5

A control for a date and time with no time zone, format YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM. Convert to UTC on the server if needed. The older type="datetime" (with time zone) was removed from the standard.

Type-specific attributes

AttributeNote
min / maxAs YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM.
stepIn seconds.
listSuggestions.

Example

<label for="dt">Event start</label>
<input id="dt" name="start" type="datetime-local" value="2026-10-01T19:00">

<input type="month"> Month and year

Since: HTML5

A control for a month in a year, value format YYYY-MM. Useful for card expiry dates and reports. Not supported in Firefox or Safari desktop, which fall back to a text field.

Type-specific attributes

AttributeNote
min / maxAs YYYY-MM.
stepIn months.
listSuggestions.

Example

<label for="exp">Card expiry</label>
<input id="exp" name="exp" type="month" autocomplete="cc-exp">

<input type="week"> Week of the year

Since: HTML5

A control for an ISO week, value format YYYY-Www (for example 2026-W37). Limited browser support (Chromium only); others show a text field.

Type-specific attributes

AttributeNote
min / maxAs YYYY-Www.
stepIn weeks.
listSuggestions.

Example

<label for="w">Week</label>
<input id="w" name="week" type="week" value="2026-W37">

Part 10: Value References

Link relationship types (rel)

ValueAllowed onMeaning
alternatelink, a, areaAn alternate version of the document: another language (with hreflang), another format (RSS feed, PDF), or an alternate style sheet (with stylesheet).
authorlink, a, areaA page about the author of the document or article.
bookmarka, areaA permalink to the nearest ancestor article.
canonicallinkThe preferred URL of this page for search engines, avoiding duplicate content penalties.
dns-prefetchlinkResolve the domain name of the given origin early.
expectlinkBlock rendering until the element identified by href="#id" is parsed (for view transitions).
externala, area, formThe link leads to a different site.
helplink, a, area, formContext-sensitive help.
iconlinkThe site icon (favicon). Combine with sizes and type. Also apple-touch-icon (non-standard) for iOS home screens.
licenselink, a, area, formThe copyright licence covering the main content.
manifestlinkThe web app manifest (JSON) for installable Progressive Web Apps.
melink, a, areaThe document represents the same person as the linked profile (IndieAuth / rel-me verification).
modulepreloadlinkPreload a JavaScript module and its dependencies.
next / prevlink, a, area, formThe next or previous document in a sequence (pagination, chapters).
nofollowa, area, formThe author does not endorse the linked page; search engines should not pass ranking credit.
noopenera, area, formOpen the link without giving the new page access to window.opener. Implied by default for target=_blank in modern browsers.
noreferrera, area, formDo not send the Referer header; also implies noopener.
openera, area, formExplicitly allow window.opener for target=_blank.
pingbacklinkThe pingback server address for this document.
preconnectlinkOpen a connection (DNS, TCP, TLS) to the origin early; use for fonts and APIs.
prefetchlinkFetch a resource likely to be needed for the next navigation and store it in cache.
preloadlinkFetch a resource needed by the current page early with high priority. Requires as.
prerenderlinkDeprecated; render a page in the background. Replaced by speculation rules.
privacy-policylink, a, areaThe privacy policy for the site.
searchlink, a, area, formA search interface for the site, often an OpenSearch description.
stylesheetlinkAn external CSS style sheet. The most common link type.
taga, areaA tag (keyword) that applies to the current document.
terms-of-servicelink, a, areaThe terms of service for the site.

Standard meta names

NameMeaning
application-nameShort name of the web application the page belongs to.
authorName of the document's author.
descriptionA short summary of the page, often shown under the title in search results. Aim for 50-160 characters.
generatorSoftware that generated the page (for example a CMS).
keywordsComma-separated keywords. Ignored by major search engines; historical.
referrerDefault referrer policy for the document: no-referrer, origin, strict-origin-when-cross-origin, and so on.
theme-colorSuggested colour for the browser UI (address bar on mobile). Accepts media.
color-schemeColour schemes the page supports: light, dark, light dark, only light.
viewportControls layout on mobile: width=device-width, initial-scale=1, plus optional minimum-scale, maximum-scale, user-scalable (do not disable zoom), viewport-fit=cover, interactive-widget.
robotsIndexing directives: index/noindex, follow/nofollow, noarchive, nosnippet, max-snippet:n, max-image-preview:large, noimageindex, notranslate, unavailable_after.
googlebot / bingbotSame as robots but for one crawler.
googleGoogle-specific: nositelinkssearchbox, notranslate.
ratingContent rating: adult or RTA-5042-1996-1400-1577-RTA.
creator / publisherThe creator and publisher of the document.
format-detectioniOS: telephone=no stops phone numbers becoming links.
apple-mobile-web-app-capable / apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style / apple-mobile-web-app-titleiOS home-screen app behaviour (non-standard).
mobile-web-app-capableAndroid equivalent (non-standard).
msapplication-TileColor / msapplication-configWindows tile settings (non-standard).
twitter:card / twitter:site / twitter:title / twitter:description / twitter:imageTwitter/X card metadata.
property=og:title / og:type / og:image / og:url / og:description / og:site_name / og:localeOpen Graph metadata used by Facebook, LinkedIn, WhatsApp, Slack and others when a link is shared (uses property instead of name).
http-equiv=content-typeLegacy encoding declaration; use charset.
http-equiv=default-styleName of the preferred style sheet set.
http-equiv=refreshReload after n seconds, optionally to another URL: content="5; url=...".
http-equiv=content-security-policyContent Security Policy for the page.
http-equiv=x-ua-compatibleLegacy: content="IE=edge" for Internet Explorer document mode.
http-equiv=content-languageObsolete; use lang on <html>.
http-equiv=set-cookieObsolete; not allowed.

URL schemes

SchemeMeaning
https:Secure web page. Always use for links and resources.
http:Insecure web page.
mailto:Opens the mail client: mailto:a@b.com?subject=Hi&body=Text&cc=c@d.com
tel:Dials a telephone number: tel:+201001234567
sms:Opens SMS: sms:+2010...?body=Hello
ftp:File transfer (no longer supported by browsers).
file:A local file (only works locally).
data:Inline data: data:image/png;base64,.... or data:text/plain,Hello
blob:An object URL created with URL.createObjectURL().
javascript:Runs script when followed. Avoid; use a button.
about:Browser pages: about:blank.
geo:Geographic coordinates: geo:30.0131,31.2089
whatsapp: / tg: / skype:App links (non-standard).
web+name:Custom schemes registered with registerProtocolHandler.
#fragmentNot a scheme: a link to an id in the current page. #top and empty # scroll to the top.

Part 11: CSS Reference

CSS fundamentals

CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) is the language that describes how HTML elements look: colours, fonts, spacing, size, position and layout. HTML says what something is; CSS says how it appears. The two are kept separate so that the same HTML can be shown in many ways (desktop, phone, print, dark mode) by changing only the CSS.

Three ways to add CSS

MethodHowWhen to use
External style sheet<link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css"> in <head>; rules live in style.cssAlways, for real projects. One file styles every page and is cached by the browser.
Internal style sheet<style> ... </style> in <head>Small single-page demos, emails, or page-specific overrides.
Inline stylestyle="color: red" attribute on an elementQuick tests and values set by JavaScript. Avoid for general styling.
/* style.css */
body   { font-family: Arial, sans-serif; margin: 0; }
footer { background: #222; color: #fff; text-align: center; padding: 20px; }

Anatomy of a rule

selector {
  property: value;   /* one declaration */
  property: value;
}

footer {
  color: gray;
  text-align: center;
}
  • The selector chooses which elements the rule applies to.
  • Each declaration is a property name, a colon, a value and a semicolon.
  • Declarations are grouped in curly braces to form a rule (or rule set).
  • Comments are written /* like this */ and may span lines.

The cascade: which rule wins

When several rules apply to the same element and property, the browser decides in this order:

  • Origin and importance: author styles beat browser defaults; !important declarations beat normal ones (avoid !important; it makes styles hard to override).
  • Specificity: inline style (1,0,0,0) beats id selectors (0,1,0,0), which beat class/attribute/pseudo-class selectors (0,0,1,0), which beat element/pseudo-element selectors (0,0,0,1). Count each part; the higher total wins.
  • Source order: if specificity is equal, the rule that appears later wins.
  • Layers (@layer) and scope (@scope) add further control in modern CSS.
p { color: black; }           /* specificity 0,0,0,1 */
.note { color: blue; }        /* 0,0,1,0 - wins over p */
#intro { color: green; }      /* 0,1,0,0 - wins over .note */
<p id="intro" class="note" style="color: red">  /* inline wins: red */

Inheritance

Some properties are inherited by child elements automatically: color, font-family, font-size, line-height, text-align, visibility, and most text properties. Others are not: margin, padding, border, background, width, height, display, position. Any property can be forced with the keywords inherit, initial, unset and revert.

Units

UnitMeaningTypical use
pxCSS pixel (1/96 inch)Borders, small fixed sizes, media query breakpoints
emRelative to the element's font sizePadding and margin that scale with text
remRelative to the root (html) font size, 16px by defaultFont sizes, spacing - predictable and respects user settings
%Relative to the parent's corresponding dimensionWidths in fluid layouts
vw / vh1% of the viewport width / heightFull-screen sections, fluid type
vmin / vmax / dvh / svh / lvhViewport-relative variantsMobile-safe full-height layouts (dvh)
chWidth of the '0' characterLine length: max-width: 65ch
frFraction of free space (grid only)grid-template-columns: 1fr 2fr
deg, rad, turnAnglesRotations, gradients
s, msTimeTransitions and animations
pt, cm, mm, inPhysical unitsPrint style sheets

Colours

NotationExampleNotes
Named colourred, steelblue, transparent, currentColor148 names; see Part 9
Hex#e60000, #e60000cc (with alpha), #f00 (short)Most common
rgb()rgb(230 0 0), rgb(230 0 0 / 50%)Modern space-separated syntax; commas still work
hsl()hsl(0 100% 45%)Hue 0-360, saturation, lightness; easy to adjust
oklch() / oklab()oklch(60% 0.2 30)Perceptually uniform; wide-gamut colours
color-mix()color-mix(in oklab, red 30%, white)Mixing colours
System coloursCanvas, CanvasText, LinkText, ButtonFaceFollow the operating system theme

The box model

Every element is a rectangular box made of four layers, from inside out: content, padding, border and margin. Width and height set the content box by default; with box-sizing: border-box they include padding and border, which is far easier to reason about. Most projects begin with the reset *, *::before, *::after { box-sizing: border-box; }.

+-------------------------------- margin (transparent) ---+
|  +---------------------------- border -----------------+  |
|  |  +------------------------ padding ---------------+  |  |
|  |  |                                                |  |  |
|  |  |                  content                       |  |  |
|  |  |                                                |  |  |
|  |  +------------------------------------------------+  |  |
|  +------------------------------------------------------+  |
+------------------------------------------------------------+

Vertical margins of adjacent blocks collapse into a single margin equal to the larger of the two. Padding and borders never collapse. Backgrounds cover the content and padding (and, by default, extend under the border).

Display and layout modes

display valueBehaviour
blockStarts on a new line, fills the available width, respects width/height. div, p, h1, section, footer...
inlineFlows within text, only as wide as its content, ignores width/height and vertical margins. span, a, em, strong...
inline-blockFlows within text but respects width, height and vertical margins/padding. img, button, input.
noneRemoved from rendering entirely (also from the accessibility tree).
flexThe element becomes a flex container; children are laid out in a row or column with powerful alignment and distribution.
gridThe element becomes a grid container; children are placed in rows and columns defined by grid-template-*.
inline-flex / inline-gridAs flex/grid, but the container itself flows inline.
table, table-row, table-cell...Table layout without table elements.
list-itemGenerates a bullet or number marker (li).
contentsThe element's box disappears but its children remain.
flow-rootA block that contains its floats (clears them) and starts a new formatting context.

Positioning

position valueBehaviour
staticDefault. Normal flow; top/left/etc. have no effect.
relativeNormal flow, then shifted by top/right/bottom/left; the original space is kept. Also creates a containing block for absolute children.
absoluteRemoved from the flow and placed relative to the nearest positioned ancestor (or the initial containing block).
fixedRemoved from the flow and placed relative to the viewport; stays put when scrolling.
stickyBehaves as relative until it reaches the threshold (top: 0), then sticks like fixed within its parent.

Flexbox in one page

.row {
  display: flex;              /* children become flex items in a row */
  flex-direction: row;        /* or column, row-reverse, column-reverse */
  flex-wrap: wrap;            /* allow items to wrap onto new lines */
  justify-content: space-between; /* main-axis distribution: flex-start | center | flex-end | space-around | space-evenly */
  align-items: center;        /* cross-axis alignment: stretch | flex-start | center | flex-end | baseline */
  gap: 16px;                  /* space between items */
}
.row > .item {
  flex: 1;                    /* shorthand for flex-grow flex-shrink flex-basis: 1 1 0 */
  order: 0;                   /* visual order */
  align-self: flex-end;       /* override align-items for one item */
}

Grid in one page

.layout {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: 200px 1fr;          /* two columns */
  grid-template-rows: auto 1fr auto;         /* header, content, footer */
  grid-template-areas:
    "header header"
    "nav    main"
    "footer footer";
  gap: 16px;
  min-height: 100vh;
}
header { grid-area: header; }
nav    { grid-area: nav; }
main   { grid-area: main; }
footer { grid-area: footer; }

/* Responsive cards without media queries */
.cards { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(240px, 1fr)); gap: 24px; }

Responsive design

/* Mobile first: base styles for small screens, then enhance */
.container { padding: 16px; }

@media (min-width: 600px) {
  .container { padding: 32px; }
}
@media (min-width: 1024px) {
  .container { max-width: 1180px; margin: 0 auto; }
}

/* Container queries: respond to the parent's size */
.card-wrapper { container-type: inline-size; }
@container (min-width: 400px) {
  .card { display: flex; }
}

/* User preferences */
@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { body { background: #111; color: #eee; } }
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { * { animation: none !important; transition: none !important; } }

/* Print */
@media print { nav, footer, .no-print { display: none; } }

Custom properties (CSS variables)

:root {
  --brand: #e60000;
  --radius: 12px;
  --font: "Segoe UI", Tahoma, Arial, sans-serif;
}
.btn {
  background: var(--brand);
  border-radius: var(--radius);
  font-family: var(--font);
}
.btn.secondary { --brand: #555; }   /* override locally */

Transitions and animations

.btn { transition: background-color 0.2s ease, transform 0.2s ease; }
.btn:hover { background-color: #b90000; transform: translateY(-2px); }

@keyframes fade-in {
  from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(8px); }
  to   { opacity: 1; transform: none; }
}
.card { animation: fade-in 0.4s ease-out both; }

CSS selectors

*

Universal selector: every element.

* { box-sizing: border-box; }

element

Type selector: all elements with that tag name.

p { line-height: 1.6; }

.class

Class selector: elements with that class.

.card { border: 1px solid #ccc; }

#id

ID selector: the one element with that id.

#main { max-width: 960px; }

[attr]

Attribute present.

input[required] { border-left: 3px solid red; }

[attr="value"]

Attribute equals value.

input[type="checkbox"] { accent-color: green; }

[attr~="word"]

Attribute contains the word in a space-separated list.

[class~="featured"] { ... }

[attr|="en"]

Attribute equals en or starts with en-.

[lang|="en"] { quotes: '“' '”'; }

[attr^="https"]

Attribute starts with.

a[href^="https"]::after { content: ' ↗'; }

[attr$=".pdf"]

Attribute ends with.

a[href$=".pdf"] { background: url(pdf.svg) no-repeat left; }

[attr*="example"]

Attribute contains substring.

a[href*="example.com"] { color: green; }

[attr="v" i]

Case-insensitive match.

[type="TEXT" i] { ... }

A B

Descendant combinator: B anywhere inside A.

nav a { text-decoration: none; }

A > B

Child combinator: B directly inside A.

ul > li { list-style: square; }

A + B

Adjacent sibling: B immediately after A.

h2 + p { margin-top: 0; }

A ~ B

General sibling: any B after A with the same parent.

h2 ~ p { color: #444; }

A, B

Selector list: either.

h1, h2, h3 { font-family: Georgia, serif; }

:hover

Pointer is over the element.

a:hover { text-decoration: underline; }

:focus / :focus-visible / :focus-within

Element has focus / focus shown by keyboard / a descendant has focus.

button:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #1b6fd8; }

:active

Being clicked.

button:active { transform: scale(0.98); }

:visited / :link

Visited / unvisited link.

a:visited { color: purple; }

:first-child / :last-child / :only-child

Position among siblings.

li:first-child { font-weight: bold; }

:nth-child(an+b) / :nth-last-child()

Position formula: 2n (even), 2n+1 (odd), 3, -n+3 (first three).

tr:nth-child(even) { background: #f7f7f7; }

:first-of-type / :last-of-type / :nth-of-type()

Position among siblings of the same type.

p:first-of-type { font-size: 1.1em; }

:not(selector)

Negation.

input:not([type="submit"]) { width: 100%; }

:is(a, b) / :where(a, b)

Matches any of the list; :where has zero specificity.

:is(h1, h2, h3) a { color: inherit; }

:has(selector)

Parent selector: element that contains a match.

article:has(img) { display: grid; }
label:has(input:invalid) { color: red; }

:empty

No children (not even text).

p:empty { display: none; }

:root

The <html> element.

:root { --gap: 16px; }

:checked / :indeterminate

Checked checkbox/radio/option.

input:checked + label { font-weight: bold; }

:disabled / :enabled / :read-only / :read-write

Form control state.

button:disabled { opacity: 0.5; }

:required / :optional

Form control requirement.

input:required { border-color: #999; }

:valid / :invalid / :user-invalid / :in-range / :out-of-range / :placeholder-shown

Validation state.

input:user-invalid { border-color: red; }

:target

Element whose id matches the URL fragment.

:target { background: #fff9c4; }

:lang(ar)

Element language.

:lang(ar) { font-family: Cairo, sans-serif; }

:dir(rtl)

Text direction.

:dir(rtl) .icon { transform: scaleX(-1); }

:popover-open / :modal / :fullscreen / :open

Top-layer and open states.

dialog:modal { border-radius: 12px; }

::before / ::after

Generated content before/after the element's content (needs content property).

q::before { content: open-quote; }

::first-line / ::first-letter

First line / first letter of a block.

p::first-letter { font-size: 2em; float: left; }

::marker

List bullet or number.

li::marker { color: red; }

::placeholder

Placeholder text in inputs.

input::placeholder { color: #999; }

::selection

Text selected by the user.

::selection { background: #ffd166; }

::backdrop

The backdrop behind a modal dialog, popover or fullscreen element.

dialog::backdrop { background: rgb(0 0 0 / 0.6); }

::part(name) / ::slotted(sel)

Shadow DOM parts and slotted content.

my-el::part(label) { color: red; }

::file-selector-button

The button in a file input.

input::file-selector-button { padding: 8px; }

::cue

WebVTT captions in video.

video::cue { background: rgb(0 0 0 / 0.8); }

font-family

Group: Fonts and text · Values: family names and generic family

The typeface used for text. Give a comma-separated list, most preferred first, ending with a generic family (serif, sans-serif, monospace, cursive, fantasy, system-ui, ui-monospace, math, emoji). The browser uses the first font that is installed or loaded with @font-face. Quote names with spaces. Inherited.

body { font-family: "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif; }
code { font-family: ui-monospace, Consolas, monospace; }

font-size

Group: Fonts and text · Values: length | percentage | keyword

The size of the text. Use rem for predictable sizes that respect user preferences (1rem = 16px by default), em for sizes relative to the parent, and clamp() for fluid type. Keywords: xx-small to xxx-large, smaller, larger.

html { font-size: 100%; }
h1 { font-size: 2rem; }
p { font-size: clamp(1rem, 0.9rem + 0.5vw, 1.25rem); }

font-weight

Group: Fonts and text · Values: normal | bold | bolder | lighter | 100-900

Thickness of the strokes. 400 = normal, 700 = bold. Variable fonts support any value in between.

strong { font-weight: 700; }
h2 { font-weight: 600; }

font-style

Group: Fonts and text · Values: normal | italic | oblique

Italic or slanted text. <em>, <i>, <cite>, <var>, <dfn>, <address> are italic by default.

em { font-style: italic; }
.no-italic { font-style: normal; }

font

Group: Fonts and text · Values: shorthand

Shorthand for font-style, font-variant, font-weight, font-size/line-height and font-family in that order. Size and family are required.

body { font: 16px/1.6 Arial, sans-serif; }
h1 { font: bold 2rem Georgia, serif; }

font-variant / font-variant-numeric / font-feature-settings

Group: Fonts and text · Values: various

Typographic features: small caps, tabular numbers (align digits in tables), ligatures, fractions.

td.num { font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
.caps { font-variant: small-caps; }

@font-face

Group: Fonts and text · Values: at-rule

Loads a custom font file so it can be used in font-family. Provide woff2, set font-display: swap to show fallback text while loading, and subset by unicode-range for speed.

@font-face {
  font-family: "Cairo";
  src: url("cairo.woff2") format("woff2");
  font-weight: 400 700;
  font-display: swap;
}
body { font-family: "Cairo", sans-serif; }

line-height

Group: Fonts and text · Values: normal | number | length | percentage

Height of each line of text. A unitless number (1.5) is best because it scales with the font size and is inherited as a factor. 1.4-1.6 is comfortable for body text.

body { line-height: 1.6; }
h1 { line-height: 1.1; }

color

Group: Fonts and text · Values: colour

The colour of the text (and the default for borders and currentColor). Inherited. Ensure at least 4.5:1 contrast with the background for body text.

body { color: #1b2431; }
.muted { color: #6b7280; }

text-align

Group: Fonts and text · Values: start | end | left | right | center | justify

Horizontal alignment of inline content inside a block. start/end follow the writing direction (best for multilingual sites). Justified text can create rivers of white space; use with hyphens: auto.

footer { text-align: center; }
th { text-align: start; }

text-decoration

Group: Fonts and text · Values: none | underline | overline | line-through, style, colour, thickness

Lines drawn on text. Shorthand for text-decoration-line, -style, -color, -thickness. Links are underlined by default; keep the underline or another clear indicator.

a { text-decoration: none; }
a:hover { text-decoration: underline; }
.spelling { text-decoration: red wavy underline; }

text-transform

Group: Fonts and text · Values: none | capitalize | uppercase | lowercase

Changes letter case for display without changing the HTML. Screen readers may spell out all-caps words.

h2 { text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.05em; }

text-indent

Group: Fonts and text · Values: length | percentage

Indentation of the first line of a block.

p + p { text-indent: 1.5em; }

text-shadow

Group: Fonts and text · Values: x y blur colour

Shadow behind text. Several shadows may be listed.

h1 { text-shadow: 0 2px 4px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.3); }

letter-spacing / word-spacing

Group: Fonts and text · Values: normal | length

Extra space between letters or words.

.label { letter-spacing: 0.1em; }

white-space

Group: Fonts and text · Values: normal | nowrap | pre | pre-wrap | pre-line | break-spaces

How whitespace and line breaks in the source are handled. normal collapses spaces and wraps; nowrap collapses but never wraps; pre preserves everything (like <pre>); pre-wrap preserves but wraps; pre-line collapses spaces but keeps line breaks.

pre { white-space: pre-wrap; }
.nowrap { white-space: nowrap; }

overflow-wrap / word-break / hyphens

Group: Fonts and text · Values: normal | break-word | anywhere / normal | break-all | keep-all / none | manual | auto

Control breaking of long words. overflow-wrap: anywhere breaks only when needed to avoid overflow; word-break: break-all breaks anywhere; hyphens: auto adds hyphens based on lang.

p { overflow-wrap: anywhere; hyphens: auto; }

text-overflow

Group: Fonts and text · Values: clip | ellipsis

What to show when text is clipped by overflow: hidden on a single line. Requires white-space: nowrap and overflow: hidden.

.title { white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; }

vertical-align

Group: Fonts and text · Values: baseline | sub | super | top | middle | bottom | text-top | text-bottom | length

Vertical alignment of inline or table-cell content. Does not centre block elements; use flexbox for that.

img.icon { vertical-align: middle; }
td { vertical-align: top; }

direction / unicode-bidi / writing-mode

Group: Fonts and text · Values: ltr | rtl / normal | embed | isolate | bidi-override / horizontal-tb | vertical-rl | vertical-lr

Text direction and writing mode. Prefer the HTML dir attribute over the CSS direction property. writing-mode enables vertical text for East Asian typography and rotated headings.

.vertical { writing-mode: vertical-rl; }

list-style

Group: Fonts and text · Values: shorthand: type position image

Bullets and numbering for lists. list-style-type: disc, circle, square, decimal, lower-alpha, upper-roman, none, or a string. list-style-position: inside | outside. Applies to ul, ol and li.

ul { list-style: square inside; }
nav ul { list-style: none; padding: 0; }
ol { list-style-type: upper-roman; }
li::marker { color: #e60000; }

quotes

Group: Fonts and text · Values: pairs of strings

Quotation marks used by <q> and open-quote/close-quote.

q { quotes: '«' '»'; }

content

Group: Fonts and text · Values: string | attr() | counter() | url() | open-quote | none

Generated content for ::before and ::after.

a[href^="http"]::after { content: " (" attr(href) ")"; }

counter-reset / counter-increment

Group: Fonts and text · Values: name value

CSS counters for automatic numbering of headings, figures, nested lists.

body { counter-reset: fig; }
figcaption::before { counter-increment: fig; content: "Figure " counter(fig) ": "; }

tab-size

Group: Fonts and text · Values: integer | length

Width of tab characters in <pre>.

pre { tab-size: 2; }

user-select

Group: Fonts and text · Values: auto | none | text | all

Whether the user can select the text.

.no-copy { user-select: none; }

width / height

Group: Box model · Values: auto | length | percentage | min-content | max-content | fit-content

Size of the box (content box by default; border box with box-sizing: border-box). Percentages are relative to the containing block. Prefer max-width for fluid layouts.

.container { width: 100%; max-width: 1180px; }
img { width: 100%; height: auto; }

min-width / max-width / min-height / max-height

Group: Box model · Values: length | percentage | none

Limits on size. max-width: 100% on images stops them overflowing; min-height: 100vh makes a section fill the screen.

img { max-width: 100%; }
main { min-height: 100dvh; }

aspect-ratio

Group: Box model · Values: auto | ratio

Preferred width-to-height ratio when one dimension is auto. Replaces the old padding-top hack for responsive video.

.video { aspect-ratio: 16 / 9; width: 100%; }
.avatar { aspect-ratio: 1; }

box-sizing

Group: Box model · Values: content-box | border-box

Whether width and height include padding and border. border-box is almost always what you want.

*, *::before, *::after { box-sizing: border-box; }

margin

Group: Box model · Values: length | percentage | auto (1-4 values)

Space outside the border. One value: all sides; two: vertical horizontal; three: top horizontal bottom; four: top right bottom left (clockwise). margin: 0 auto centres a block with a width. Vertical margins collapse. Logical versions: margin-block, margin-inline.

p { margin: 0 0 1em; }
.box { margin: 20px auto; }
.card { margin-inline: auto; }

padding

Group: Box model · Values: length | percentage (1-4 values)

Space between the content and the border. Same value order as margin. Cannot be negative. Backgrounds show through padding.

button { padding: 10px 20px; }
.card { padding-block: 1rem; padding-inline: 1.5rem; }

border

Group: Box model · Values: width style colour

Shorthand for border-width, border-style and border-color on all sides. Styles: none, solid, dashed, dotted, double, groove, ridge, inset, outset. Per-side: border-top, border-right, border-bottom, border-left, or logical border-block-start etc.

.card { border: 1px solid #e7ddcb; }
blockquote { border-left: 4px solid #c8a24a; }
th, td { border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd; }

border-radius

Group: Box model · Values: length | percentage (1-4 values, optional / for elliptical)

Rounds the corners. 50% on a square makes a circle. Per-corner: border-top-left-radius etc.

.btn { border-radius: 8px; }
.avatar { border-radius: 50%; }
.pill { border-radius: 999px; }

border-collapse / border-spacing

Group: Box model · Values: separate | collapse / length

Table borders: collapse merges adjacent cell borders into one; border-spacing sets the gap between cells in separate mode (replaces cellspacing).

table { border-collapse: collapse; }
table.spaced { border-collapse: separate; border-spacing: 4px; }

outline

Group: Box model · Values: width style colour

A line drawn outside the border that does not take space. Browsers use it for the keyboard focus ring; never remove it without a replacement. outline-offset moves it away from the edge.

:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #1b6fd8; outline-offset: 2px; }

box-shadow

Group: Box model · Values: x y blur spread colour [inset]

Shadows around the box. Several shadows may be listed, separated by commas.

.card { box-shadow: 0 10px 30px rgb(27 36 49 / 0.09); }
.inset { box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px #e60000; }

overflow / overflow-x / overflow-y

Group: Box model · Values: visible | hidden | clip | scroll | auto

What happens when content is larger than the box. auto shows scrollbars only when needed. Setting overflow (other than visible) also clips absolutely positioned children and contains floats.

.table-wrap { overflow-x: auto; }
.modal-body { max-height: 70vh; overflow-y: auto; }

display

Group: Box model · Values: block | inline | inline-block | flex | grid | none | contents | flow-root | list-item | table...

How the element generates boxes and lays out its children. See the layout table in the CSS introduction.

nav ul { display: flex; }
.hidden { display: none; }
span.badge { display: inline-block; }

visibility

Group: Box model · Values: visible | hidden | collapse

hidden makes the element invisible but it still takes up space (unlike display: none). collapse removes table rows/columns.

.placeholder { visibility: hidden; }

opacity

Group: Box model · Values: 0 to 1

Transparency of the whole element including its children. 0 is invisible but still takes space and receives clicks.

.disabled { opacity: 0.5; }
.fade { transition: opacity 0.3s; }

object-fit / object-position

Group: Box model · Values: fill | contain | cover | none | scale-down / position

How a replaced element (img, video) fits its box when the box's ratio differs from the media. cover crops to fill; contain letterboxes.

.thumb { width: 200px; height: 150px; object-fit: cover; object-position: center top; }

resize

Group: Box model · Values: none | both | horizontal | vertical

Whether the user can resize the element (textarea by default).

textarea { resize: vertical; }

cursor

Group: Box model · Values: auto | pointer | default | text | move | not-allowed | grab | wait | help | zoom-in | url()

The mouse pointer shape over the element.

button, [role="button"] { cursor: pointer; }
.disabled { cursor: not-allowed; }

background-color

Group: Backgrounds · Values: colour | transparent

The colour behind the content and padding.

body { background-color: #f6f1e7; }

background-image

Group: Backgrounds · Values: url() | gradient | none

One or more images or gradients layered behind the element, first listed on top. Gradients: linear-gradient(), radial-gradient(), conic-gradient(), repeating-*.

.hero { background-image: linear-gradient(rgb(0 0 0 / 0.5), rgb(0 0 0 / 0.5)), url(hero.jpg); }

background-size / background-position / background-repeat / background-attachment / background-clip / background-origin

Group: Backgrounds · Values: various

How the image is sized (cover, contain, lengths), placed (center, top right, 50% 50%), repeated (no-repeat, repeat-x), scrolled (fixed for parallax), and which box it fills.

.hero { background: url(hero.jpg) center / cover no-repeat; }

background

Group: Backgrounds · Values: shorthand

Shorthand for all background properties: color image position / size repeat attachment origin clip.

footer { background: #222 url(pattern.png) repeat; }

filter / backdrop-filter

Group: Backgrounds · Values: blur() | brightness() | contrast() | grayscale() | drop-shadow() | ...

Graphical effects applied to the element or to what is behind it (frosted glass).

img:hover { filter: brightness(1.1); }
.glass { backdrop-filter: blur(10px); background: rgb(255 255 255 / 0.6); }

mix-blend-mode / isolation

Group: Backgrounds · Values: normal | multiply | screen | overlay | difference...

How the element blends with what is behind it.

.logo { mix-blend-mode: multiply; }

clip-path / mask

Group: Backgrounds · Values: shapes and images

Clip the element to a shape (circle(), polygon(), inset()) or mask it with an image.

.hex { clip-path: polygon(25% 0, 75% 0, 100% 50%, 75% 100%, 25% 100%, 0 50%); }

position / top / right / bottom / left / inset / z-index

Group: Layout · Values: static | relative | absolute | fixed | sticky

Positioning scheme and offsets. z-index orders positioned (and flex/grid) siblings on the z-axis; higher is in front; it creates stacking contexts.

.modal { position: fixed; inset: 0; z-index: 1000; }
.badge { position: absolute; top: -8px; right: -8px; }
header { position: sticky; top: 0; }

float / clear

Group: Layout · Values: left | right | none / left | right | both

Float takes an element out of flow and lets text wrap around it (its original purpose: images in text). Clear moves an element below floats. Not for page layout; use flex/grid.

figure.left { float: left; margin: 0 1em 1em 0; }
.after { clear: both; }

flex-direction / flex-wrap / flex-flow

Group: Layout · Values: row | row-reverse | column | column-reverse / nowrap | wrap | wrap-reverse

Direction of the main axis and whether items wrap. flex-flow is the shorthand.

.row { display: flex; flex-flow: row wrap; }

justify-content

Group: Layout · Values: flex-start | flex-end | center | space-between | space-around | space-evenly | start | end

Distribution of items along the main axis (flex) or of grid tracks along the inline axis.

.toolbar { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; }

align-items / align-self / align-content

Group: Layout · Values: stretch | flex-start | flex-end | center | baseline | start | end

Alignment on the cross axis: for all items, for one item, or for wrapped lines.

.center { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; }

justify-items / justify-self / place-items / place-content / place-self

Group: Layout · Values: start | end | center | stretch

Grid inline-axis alignment and shorthands combining align and justify.

.grid { display: grid; place-items: center; }

gap / row-gap / column-gap

Group: Layout · Values: length | percentage

Space between flex items, grid tracks or multi-column columns. Replaces margin hacks.

.cards { display: grid; gap: 24px 16px; }

flex / flex-grow / flex-shrink / flex-basis

Group: Layout · Values: number number length|auto

How a flex item grows and shrinks relative to siblings and its starting size. flex: 1 = fill equally; flex: 0 0 200px = fixed 200px; flex: auto = size to content then grow.

.sidebar { flex: 0 0 240px; }
.content { flex: 1; min-width: 0; }

order

Group: Layout · Values: integer

Visual order of flex or grid items (does not change tab order; use sparingly).

.first { order: -1; }

grid-template-columns / grid-template-rows

Group: Layout · Values: track sizes: length, %, fr, auto, min-content, max-content, minmax(), repeat(), fit-content()

Define the explicit grid tracks. repeat(auto-fit, minmax(240px, 1fr)) creates as many columns as fit.

.layout { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 240px 1fr; }
.gallery { grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(150px, 1fr)); }

grid-template-areas / grid-area

Group: Layout · Values: strings / name or line numbers

Named regions for readable layouts. Items are placed with grid-area: name.

.page { grid-template-areas: "head head" "nav main" "foot foot"; }
footer { grid-area: foot; }

grid-column / grid-row / grid-column-start etc.

Group: Layout · Values: line / span n / name

Place an item by grid lines. span 2 makes it cover two tracks.

.wide { grid-column: 1 / -1; }
.tall { grid-row: span 2; }

grid-auto-flow / grid-auto-rows / grid-auto-columns

Group: Layout · Values: row | column | dense / track size

How auto-placed items flow and how implicit tracks are sized.

.masonry { grid-auto-flow: dense; grid-auto-rows: 120px; }

columns / column-count / column-width / column-gap / column-rule / column-span / break-inside

Group: Layout · Values: various

Multi-column text like a newspaper.

.article { columns: 2 300px; column-gap: 32px; }
figure { break-inside: avoid; }

container-type / container-name / @container

Group: Layout · Values: inline-size | size | normal

Container queries: style an element based on the size of an ancestor container instead of the viewport.

.sidebar { container-type: inline-size; }
@container (max-width: 300px) { .card { flex-direction: column; } }

contain / content-visibility

Group: Layout · Values: layout | paint | size | style / visible | hidden | auto

Performance hints: isolate an element's rendering; content-visibility: auto skips rendering off-screen content.

.long-list > li { content-visibility: auto; contain-intrinsic-size: auto 80px; }

transform / transform-origin / rotate / scale / translate

Group: Motion · Values: translate() rotate() scale() skew() matrix() perspective()

Move, rotate, scale or skew the element without affecting layout; hardware accelerated. The individual properties rotate, scale and translate can be set separately.

.card:hover { transform: translateY(-4px) scale(1.02); }
.spin { rotate: 45deg; }

transition / transition-property / -duration / -timing-function / -delay

Group: Motion · Values: property time easing time

Animate changes of properties smoothly. Timing functions: ease, linear, ease-in, ease-out, ease-in-out, cubic-bezier(), steps().

a { transition: color 0.2s ease; }
.panel { transition: transform 0.3s cubic-bezier(0.2, 0.8, 0.2, 1); }

animation / @keyframes

Group: Motion · Values: name duration timing delay iteration-count direction fill-mode play-state

Keyframe animations. Respect prefers-reduced-motion.

@keyframes pulse { 50% { opacity: 0.5; } }
.dot { animation: pulse 1s infinite; }

scroll-behavior / scroll-snap-type / scroll-snap-align / scroll-margin / scroll-padding / overscroll-behavior

Group: Motion · Values: various

Smooth scrolling, snap points for carousels, and offsets for fixed headers.

html { scroll-behavior: smooth; scroll-padding-top: 80px; }
.carousel { scroll-snap-type: x mandatory; }
.carousel > * { scroll-snap-align: start; }

will-change

Group: Motion · Values: property names

Hint that a property will animate so the browser can optimise. Use sparingly.

.drawer { will-change: transform; }

pointer-events

Group: Interaction · Values: auto | none

none makes the element ignore mouse/touch events (clicks pass through).

.overlay-text { pointer-events: none; }

accent-color

Group: Interaction · Values: colour

Colour of native checkboxes, radios, range sliders and progress bars.

:root { accent-color: #e60000; }

appearance

Group: Interaction · Values: none | auto | base-select

Remove or keep the native look of form controls. none lets you restyle selects and inputs fully.

select { appearance: none; }

color-scheme

Group: Interaction · Values: light | dark | light dark

Tells the browser which colour schemes the page supports so form controls and scrollbars match.

:root { color-scheme: light dark; }

caret-color

Group: Interaction · Values: colour

Colour of the text cursor.

input { caret-color: #e60000; }

touch-action

Group: Interaction · Values: auto | none | pan-x | pan-y | manipulation

Which touch gestures the browser handles; manipulation removes the 300ms tap delay on old mobile browsers.

button { touch-action: manipulation; }

field-sizing

Group: Interaction · Values: fixed | content

Make inputs and textareas grow with their content.

textarea { field-sizing: content; }

all

Group: Interaction · Values: initial | inherit | unset | revert

Reset every property at once.

.reset { all: unset; }

@media

Group: Interaction · Values: at-rule

Conditional rules based on viewport size, orientation, resolution, hover ability, user preferences (prefers-color-scheme, prefers-reduced-motion, prefers-contrast) and output (print, screen).

@media (max-width: 600px) { nav { display: none; } }
@media (hover: hover) { a:hover { color: red; } }

@supports

Group: Interaction · Values: at-rule

Apply rules only if the browser supports a feature.

@supports (display: grid) { .layout { display: grid; } }

@import / @layer / @scope / @property

Group: Interaction · Values: at-rules

Import other style sheets (slow; prefer <link>), define cascade layers, scope styles to a subtree, register typed custom properties.

@layer reset, base, components;
@layer base { body { margin: 0; } }

@page

Group: Interaction · Values: at-rule

Page size and margins for printing.

@page { size: A4; margin: 2cm; }

Styling HTML elements: cookbook

Styling common HTML elements: a cookbook

A sensible reset

*, *::before, *::after { box-sizing: border-box; }
body { margin: 0; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, Arial, sans-serif; line-height: 1.6; color: #1b2431; }
img, video, svg { max-width: 100%; height: auto; display: block; }
button, input, select, textarea { font: inherit; color: inherit; }
h1, h2, h3, h4 { line-height: 1.2; margin-block: 0 0.5em; }
p, ul, ol, dl, table, figure, pre { margin-block: 0 1em; }

Links

a { color: #0b57d0; text-underline-offset: 2px; }
a:hover { color: #083b8f; }
a:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #0b57d0; outline-offset: 2px; border-radius: 2px; }
a[href^="http"]:not([href*="mysite.com"])::after { content: " ↗"; font-size: 0.8em; }

Headings with a fluid scale

h1 { font-size: clamp(1.8rem, 1.2rem + 2.5vw, 3rem); }
h2 { font-size: clamp(1.4rem, 1rem + 1.5vw, 2rem); }
h3 { font-size: 1.25rem; }

Lists

/* Default bullets tweaked */
ul { padding-inline-start: 1.25em; }
li + li { margin-top: 0.25em; }
li::marker { color: #e60000; }

/* Bullet-less horizontal menu */
.menu { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; display: flex; gap: 1rem; }

/* Custom check bullets */
.checks { list-style: none; padding: 0; }
.checks li::before { content: "✓ "; color: #0f8a4c; font-weight: bold; }

/* Description list as a two-column grid */
dl.specs { display: grid; grid-template-columns: max-content 1fr; gap: 0.25rem 1rem; }
dl.specs dt { font-weight: 600; }
dl.specs dd { margin: 0; }

Tables

table { border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
caption { caption-side: top; text-align: start; font-weight: 600; padding-block: 0.5rem; }
th, td { padding: 0.5rem 0.75rem; border-bottom: 1px solid #e5e5e5; text-align: start; vertical-align: top; }
thead th { background: #f5f5f5; position: sticky; top: 0; }
tbody tr:nth-child(even) { background: #fafafa; }
tbody tr:hover { background: #fff4e0; }
td.num, th.num { text-align: end; }
.table-wrap { overflow-x: auto; }   /* wrap the table for small screens */

/* Stacked table on phones */
@media (max-width: 600px) {
  .stack thead { display: none; }
  .stack tr { display: block; margin-bottom: 1rem; border: 1px solid #ddd; }
  .stack td { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; }
  .stack td::before { content: attr(data-label); font-weight: 600; }
}

Forms

.field { display: grid; gap: 0.25rem; margin-bottom: 1rem; }
label { font-weight: 600; }
input, select, textarea { padding: 0.6rem 0.75rem; border: 1px solid #c9c9c9; border-radius: 8px; background: #fff; }
input:focus-visible, select:focus-visible, textarea:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #0b57d0; outline-offset: 1px; border-color: #0b57d0; }
input:user-invalid { border-color: #b90000; }
input:disabled { background: #f0f0f0; cursor: not-allowed; }
::placeholder { color: #8a8a8a; }
fieldset { border: 1px solid #ddd; border-radius: 8px; padding: 1rem; }
legend { padding: 0 0.5rem; font-weight: 600; }
input[type="checkbox"], input[type="radio"] { width: 1.1em; height: 1.1em; accent-color: #e60000; }
button { padding: 0.65rem 1.25rem; border: 0; border-radius: 8px; background: #e60000; color: #fff; font-weight: 600; cursor: pointer; }
button:hover { background: #b90000; }
button:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; }

Header, nav, main, footer layout

body { min-height: 100dvh; display: flex; flex-direction: column; }
header { position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: 10; background: #fff; box-shadow: 0 1px 0 #eee; }
header .wrap { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 1rem; padding: 0.75rem 1rem; }
nav ul { display: flex; gap: 1.25rem; list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; }
nav a[aria-current="page"] { border-bottom: 2px solid #e60000; }
main { flex: 1; width: min(100% - 2rem, 1180px); margin-inline: auto; padding-block: 2rem; }
footer { background: #222; color: #ddd; text-align: center; padding: 2rem 1rem; margin-top: auto; }
footer a { color: #ffd166; }

Images and figures

figure { margin: 0 0 1.5rem; }
figure img { border-radius: 12px; }
figcaption { font-size: 0.9rem; color: #666; margin-top: 0.5rem; text-align: center; }
.avatar { width: 64px; aspect-ratio: 1; border-radius: 50%; object-fit: cover; }
.hero img { width: 100%; height: 50vh; object-fit: cover; }

Code and pre

code { font-family: ui-monospace, Consolas, "Courier New", monospace; font-size: 0.95em; background: #f4f4f4; padding: 0.1em 0.3em; border-radius: 4px; }
pre { background: #1e1e1e; color: #eee; padding: 1rem; border-radius: 8px; overflow-x: auto; tab-size: 2; }
pre code { background: none; padding: 0; color: inherit; }
kbd { border: 1px solid #bbb; border-bottom-width: 2px; border-radius: 4px; padding: 0 0.35em; background: #fafafa; font-size: 0.9em; }

Blockquote, hr, details

blockquote { margin: 1.5rem 0; padding: 0.75rem 1.25rem; border-inline-start: 4px solid #c8a24a; background: #fdf8f0; }
blockquote footer { font-size: 0.9rem; color: #666; }
hr { border: 0; border-top: 1px solid #e0e0e0; margin: 2rem 0; }
details { border: 1px solid #ddd; border-radius: 8px; padding: 0.5rem 1rem; }
summary { cursor: pointer; font-weight: 600; }
details[open] summary { margin-bottom: 0.5rem; }

Dialog and popover

dialog { border: 0; border-radius: 16px; padding: 1.5rem; max-width: min(90vw, 480px); box-shadow: 0 24px 60px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.25); }
dialog::backdrop { background: rgb(0 0 0 / 0.5); backdrop-filter: blur(2px); }
[popover] { border: 1px solid #ddd; border-radius: 12px; padding: 1rem; box-shadow: 0 10px 30px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.15); }
[popover]:popover-open { animation: fade-in 0.15s ease-out; }

Visually hidden (for screen readers only)

.sr-only {
  position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding: 0; margin: -1px;
  overflow: hidden; clip: rect(0 0 0 0); white-space: nowrap; border: 0;
}

Dark mode

:root { color-scheme: light dark; --bg: #fff; --ink: #1b2431; }
@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { :root { --bg: #111; --ink: #eee; } }
body { background: var(--bg); color: var(--ink); }

Lists and tables with CSS

Lists group related items; tables display structured data (information arranged in rows and columns so that it is easy to scan). Combining the right HTML element with a little CSS makes both far more readable and accessible. This chapter walks through every common styling task for <ul>, <ol>, <dl> and <table>, step by step, with complete copy-and-paste examples.

1. Unordered and ordered lists

Use <ul> for unordered lists (bullets) and <ol> for ordered lists (numbers). Each item goes in an <li>. The browser adds the bullets or numbers automatically, indents the list about 40 pixels and adds a blank line before and after it.

<ul class="features">
  <li>Responsive layout</li>
  <li>Semantic HTML</li>
  <li>Accessible components</li>
</ul>

<ol class="steps">
  <li>Plan content</li>
  <li>Structure markup</li>
  <li>Apply typography and layout</li>
</ol>

Changing the marker: list-style-type

The list-style-type property chooses the bullet or numbering style. It replaces the obsolete HTML type attribute.

ValueWorks onResult
disc (default for ul)ulFilled circle
circleulHollow circle
squareulFilled square
noneul, olNo marker at all (used for menus and navigation)
decimal (default for ol)ol1, 2, 3
decimal-leading-zerool01, 02, 03
lower-alpha / upper-alphaola, b, c / A, B, C
lower-roman / upper-romanoli, ii, iii / I, II, III
lower-greekolalpha, beta, gamma
arabic-indicolArabic-Indic digits used in Arabic-language pages
'\2192 ' or any stringulA custom character such as an arrow or a check mark
ul.a { list-style-type: circle; }
ul.b { list-style-type: square; }
ol.c { list-style-type: upper-roman; }
ol.d { list-style-type: lower-alpha; }
ul.arrows { list-style-type: '\2192 '; }   /* a right arrow before every item */

Image markers and marker position

ul { list-style-image: url('sqpurple.gif'); }

/* inside: the marker is part of the text and wraps with it;
   outside (default): the marker hangs in the left margin */
ul.inside  { list-style-position: inside; }
ul.outside { list-style-position: outside; }

The list-style shorthand

list-style sets type, position and image in one declaration, in that order. Missing values return to their defaults.

ul { list-style: square inside url('sqpurple.gif'); }

Removing default settings

To use a list as a menu, remove the marker, the margin and the padding. Setting margin and padding to 0 on the <ul> removes the indentation that browsers add; without this step the items still sit 40 pixels from the left edge.

ul.menu {
  list-style-type: none;
  margin: 0;
  padding: 0;
}

Styling the marker itself: ::marker

The ::marker pseudo-element styles only the bullet or number, leaving the item text alone. It accepts colour, font and content properties.

li::marker { color: #b90000; font-weight: bold; }
ol li::marker { content: counter(list-item) ') '; }

Custom markers with ::before (the W3Schools 'features' pattern)

For complete control replace the marker with generated content. The rules below remove the default bullets, space the items with Grid gap, give every item a card look and insert a check mark with ::before.

.features {
  list-style: none;
  padding: 0;
  margin: 0;
  display: grid;
  gap: 12px;
}
.features li {
  padding: 16px 20px;
  background: #fff;
  border-radius: 12px;
  box-shadow: 0 10px 25px rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.08);
}
.features li::before {
  content: '\2714';      /* heavy check mark */
  color: #04AA6D;
  margin-right: 12px;
}

Colouring lists

Anything added to the <ul> or <ol> affects the whole list; anything added to <li> affects one item. Padding on the list moves the markers inward as well.

ol {
  background: #ff9999;
  padding: 20px;
}
ul {
  background: #3399ff;
  padding: 20px;
}
ol li {
  background: #ffe5e5;
  color: darkred;
  padding: 5px;
  margin-left: 35px;
}
ul li {
  background: #cce5ff;
  color: darkblue;
  margin: 5px;
}

Horizontal lists: navigation bars

A navigation bar is just a list of links laid out in a row. Flexbox is the modern way; float was used before 2015.

<nav>
  <ul class="navbar">
    <li><a href="index.html">Home</a></li>
    <li><a href="books.html">Books</a></li>
    <li><a href="contact.html">Contact</a></li>
  </ul>
</nav>

<style>
.navbar {
  list-style: none;
  margin: 0;
  padding: 0;
  display: flex;
  gap: 4px;
  background: #333;
}
.navbar a {
  display: block;
  padding: 14px 16px;
  color: white;
  text-decoration: none;
}
.navbar a:hover { background: #111; }
</style>

Numbered lists with counters

CSS counters number anything, including nested headings, and let you style the number separately.

ol.fancy { counter-reset: item; list-style: none; padding: 0; }
ol.fancy li { counter-increment: item; margin: 8px 0; }
ol.fancy li::before {
  content: counter(item);
  display: inline-block;
  width: 1.6em; height: 1.6em; line-height: 1.6em;
  margin-right: .6em;
  text-align: center;
  border-radius: 50%;
  background: #b90000;
  color: white;
  font-weight: bold;
}

2. Description lists

Use <dl> with <dt> (term) and <dd> (definition) for glossaries or metadata. Browsers indent the <dd> by about 40 pixels; with CSS Grid you can lay terms and definitions out in two columns.

<dl class="glossary">
  <dt>HTML</dt>
  <dd>Structure of a web page.</dd>
  <dt>CSS</dt>
  <dd>Presentation and layout.</dd>
</dl>

<style>
.glossary {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: max-content 1fr;
  gap: 6px 16px;
}
.glossary dt { font-weight: bold; color: #b90000; }
.glossary dd { margin: 0; }
</style>

3. HTML tables

<table> organises tabular data with rows (<tr>), header cells (<th>) and data cells (<td>). Tabular data is information best shown in a grid, such as price lists or schedules. Group the header row in <thead> and the data in <tbody>, and give every <th> a scope attribute so screen readers know whether it labels a column or a row.

<table class="pricing">
  <caption>Subscription plans</caption>
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th scope="col">Plan</th>
      <th scope="col">Price</th>
      <th scope="col">Features</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <th scope="row">Starter</th>
      <td>$0</td>
      <td>Basic components</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <th scope="row">Pro</th>
      <td>$19</td>
      <td>Advanced layouts</td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

Table borders
