A table has no visible borders by default. The border property must be set on the table AND on the cells; setting it on the table alone draws only the outer frame. Because each cell has its own border you get a double line between cells until you collapse them.

table, th, td {
  border: 1px solid black;
}

Collapsed borders

border-collapse: collapse merges adjacent cell borders into a single line. This is almost always what you want. The old HTML cellspacing attribute is replaced by border-spacing (only in the separate model) and cellpadding by padding on the cells.

table {
  border-collapse: collapse;
}
th, td {
  border: 1px solid #ddd;
  padding: 8px;
}

/* alternative: keep separate borders but control the gap */
table.spaced { border-collapse: separate; border-spacing: 6px 2px; }

Rounded or borderless tables

For a light look, add only a bottom border to each row. For rounded corners set overflow: hidden and border-radius on the table.

table { border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; }
td, th { border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd; padding: 12px; }

table.rounded { border-radius: 12px; overflow: hidden; }

Table size

Width and height are set with CSS width and height on the table, rows or cells. width: 100% makes the table fill its container. The obsolete HTML width attribute did the same job.

table { width: 100%; }
th { height: 70px; }
td.narrow { width: 70px; }
table.fixed { table-layout: fixed; }   /* equal columns regardless of content */

Alignment

text-align sets horizontal alignment (th content is centred and bold by default, td content is left aligned); vertical-align sets vertical alignment (middle by default). These replace the align and valign attributes.

th { text-align: left; }
td { text-align: center; height: 50px; vertical-align: bottom; }

Padding and spacing

padding on th/td controls the space between the border and the content. To add space between cells themselves use border-spacing (separate border model only).

th, td { padding: 15px; }
th, td { padding-top: 10px; padding-bottom: 20px; padding-left: 30px; padding-right: 40px; }

Horizontal dividers, hover and zebra stripes

Highlight rows on hover with :hover on <tr>, and zebra-stripe with :nth-child(even). Both make long tables easier to read.

tr:hover { background-color: coral; }
tr:nth-child(even) { background-color: #f2f2f2; }

/* vertical zebra stripes */
th:nth-child(even), td:nth-child(even) { background-color: #d6eeee; }

/* combining both with transparency */
tr:nth-child(even) { background-color: rgba(150, 212, 212, 0.4); }
th:nth-child(even), td:nth-child(even) { background-color: rgba(150, 212, 212, 0.4); }

Styling the header row

.pricing {
  width: 100%;
  border-collapse: collapse;
  background: #fff;
  border-radius: 12px;
  overflow: hidden;
}
.pricing th, .pricing td {
  padding: 16px 20px;
  text-align: left;
}
.pricing thead {
  background: #04AA6D;
  color: #fff;
}
.pricing tbody tr:nth-child(even) {
  background: #f9fafb;
}

Key rules: border-collapse: collapse removes gaps, header styling highlights the labels, and :nth-child(even) zebra-stripes the rows.

Colouring individual columns

<table>
  <colgroup>
    <col span="2" style="background-color: #D6EEEE">
  </colgroup>
  <tr><th>MON</th><th>TUE</th><th>WED</th></tr>
  ...
</table>

Only a few properties work on <col>: width, visibility, background and border. For anything else target td:nth-child(n).

Responsive tables

Tables can overflow on small screens. Wrapping them in a scroll container preserves readability: mobile users swipe sideways instead of the table breaking the layout. The wrapper is a <div> with overflow-x: auto.

<div class="table-wrapper">
  <table>...</table>
</div>

<style>
.table-wrapper { overflow-x: auto; }
</style>

An alternative for narrow screens is to turn each row into a block and print the column label with a data attribute:

@media (max-width: 600px) {
  thead { display: none; }
  tr { display: block; margin-bottom: 1em; border: 1px solid #ddd; }
  td { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; padding: 8px; }
  td::before { content: attr(data-label); font-weight: bold; }
}

<!-- HTML -->
<td data-label="Price">$19</td>

Sticky header and caption position

thead th { position: sticky; top: 0; background: #fff; }
caption { caption-side: bottom; font-style: italic; padding: 8px; }
table.no-empty { empty-cells: hide; }

4. Accessibility tips for tables

  • Always use <th> for headers and add the scope attribute (col or row). It tells assistive technology which header belongs to which cell.
  • Provide captions with <caption> when the table's purpose is not obvious from the surrounding text.
  • Keep tables for data, not layout. Use CSS Grid or Flexbox for page layout.
  • Do not rely on colour alone (for example a red cell for 'sold out'); add text or an icon as well.
  • Avoid merged cells (rowspan/colspan) in data tables where possible; if you need them, add headers/id associations.
  • Right-align numbers so that digits line up, and use the same number of decimals in a column.

5. Complete example: course outline with a list and a table

This demo pairs a topic list with a simple table. The list uses square bullets while the table collapses its borders for a clean grid, with coloured headers to improve readability.

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <title>Course Outline</title>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css">
</head>
<body>
  <h1>Course Outline</h1>
  <ul>
    <li>HTML Basics</li>
    <li>CSS Essentials</li>
    <li>Responsive Layouts</li>
  </ul>
  <table>
    <tr><th>Module</th><th>Duration</th></tr>
    <tr><td>Getting Started</td><td>2 hrs</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Flexbox &amp; Grid</td><td>3 hrs</td></tr>
  </table>
</body>
</html>
/* styles.css */
body {
  font-family: 'Segoe UI', sans-serif;
  padding: 48px;
  background: #eef2ff;
}
ul {
  list-style: square;
}
table {
  margin-top: 32px;
  border-collapse: collapse;
  width: 100%;
  max-width: 640px;
  background: #fff;
}
th, td {
  border: 1px solid #d9e2ec;
  padding: 12px 16px;
  text-align: left;
}
th {
  background: #6366f1;
  color: #fff;
}

6. Quick reference: list and table properties

PropertyApplies toPurpose
list-style-typeul, ol, liMarker shape or numbering system
list-style-imageul, ol, liImage as marker
list-style-positionul, ol, liMarker inside or outside the item box
list-styleul, ol, liShorthand for the three above
::markerliStyle the marker only
counter-reset / counter-increment / counter()anyCustom numbering
border-collapsetablecollapse or separate cell borders
border-spacingtableGap between cells (separate model)
caption-sidetableCaption above (top) or below (bottom)
empty-cellstableshow or hide borders of empty cells
table-layouttableauto (content sized) or fixed (equal, faster)
vertical-aligntd, thtop, middle, bottom
text-aligntd, thleft, center, right
paddingtd, thSpace inside cells (replaces cellpadding)
:nth-child(even/odd)tr, tdZebra stripes
tr:hovertrRow highlight
overflow-x: autowrapper divScrollable table on small screens

7. Old HTML attributes and their CSS replacements

Old attribute (HTML 3.2 / 4)ElementUse instead
type="square"ullist-style-type: square
type="A" / type="i"ollist-style-type: upper-alpha / lower-roman (type on ol is still allowed but CSS is preferred)
compactul, ol, dlmargin / line-height
border="1"tableborder on table, th, td
cellpaddingtablepadding on th, td
cellspacingtableborder-spacing (or border-collapse: collapse)
width / heighttable, tdwidth / height in CSS
bgcolortable, tr, tdbackground-color
aligntable, tr, tdtext-align / margin: 0 auto
valigntr, tdvertical-align
nowraptdwhite-space: nowrap
frame / rulestableborder on the relevant sides
summarytable<caption> or aria-describedby

Part 12: HTML and CSS Course

Lesson 1: Introduction and environment setup

HTML gives a page its structure and meaning; CSS gives it appearance and layout. Together they are the two languages every web page is made of. HTML says 'this is a heading, this is a list of three items, this is a table of prices'; CSS says 'headings are dark red and 28 pixels, the list has no bullets and sits in a row, the table has thin grey lines'.

What you need

  • A text editor. Any editor that saves plain text works: UltraEdit, Notepad++, Sublime Text or VS Code. Turn on syntax highlighting for HTML and CSS.
  • A browser: Chrome, Edge or Firefox. Its developer tools (press F12) show you the HTML tree, the CSS applied to each element and the box model.
  • A folder for your project, for example C:\Users\you\Documents\bookshop. Keep index.html, styles.css and an images folder inside it.
  • Nothing else. No server, no installation, no account. Open the .html file in the browser by double-clicking it or dragging it into a tab.

Workflow

  • Write or change a file in the editor and save it (Ctrl+S).
  • Switch to the browser and reload (F5). The page shows the change immediately.
  • If something looks wrong, right-click it and choose Inspect. The Elements panel shows the exact HTML and the Styles panel shows which CSS rules apply and which are crossed out (overridden).
  • Validate occasionally with https://validator.w3.org/ (HTML) and https://jigsaw.w3.org/css-validator/ (CSS) to catch typos such as unclosed tags or misspelled properties.

File naming rules

  • Use lower-case names with no spaces: about-us.html, not About Us.html. Web servers are case-sensitive and spaces become %20 in URLs.
  • The home page is index.html: servers show it automatically when someone visits the folder.
  • Save with UTF-8 encoding (in UltraEdit: File > Save As > Encoding: UTF-8, no BOM). Declare it with <meta charset="utf-8"> so that Arabic, accents and symbols display correctly.

Lesson 2: Your first web page

Every page has the same skeleton. Type it once, save it as index.html and open it in the browser.

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>My first page</title>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css">
</head>
<body>
  <header>
    <h1>Hello, world</h1>
    <nav>
      <a href="index.html">Home</a>
      <a href="about.html">About</a>
    </nav>
  </header>
  <main>
    <p>This is my first web page. It has a heading, a paragraph and a link to
       <a href="https://developer.mozilla.org">MDN</a>.</p>
  </main>
  <footer>
    <p>&copy; 2026 My Name</p>
  </footer>
</body>
</html>
LineWhat it does
<!DOCTYPE html>Tells the browser this is modern HTML (standards mode). Always the first line.
<html lang="en">Root element. lang tells screen readers and translators the language (ar for Arabic, with dir="rtl").
<head>Information about the page that is not displayed: encoding, title, links to CSS.
<meta charset="utf-8">Character encoding; prevents garbled text.
<meta name="viewport" ...>Makes the page scale correctly on phones. Without it, mobile browsers pretend to be 980px wide.
<title>Text in the browser tab, bookmarks and search results.
<link rel="stylesheet">Loads the CSS file.
<body>Everything visible.
<header>, <nav>, <main>, <footer>Semantic landmarks: which part of the page is which.

Add the style sheet

Create styles.css in the same folder:

body {
  font-family: system-ui, Arial, sans-serif;
  line-height: 1.6;
  max-width: 60rem;
  margin: 0 auto;
  padding: 1rem;
  color: #1b2431;
}
h1 { color: #b90000; }
nav a { margin-right: 1rem; }
footer { margin-top: 3rem; font-size: .9rem; color: #666; }
Reload the browser. If nothing changes, check that the file is really called styles.css (not styles.css.txt), that it is in the same folder as index.html, and that the href in <link> matches exactly.

Lesson 3: Essentials - elements, attributes and nesting

An element is a start tag, content and an end tag: <p>text</p>. Attributes go inside the start tag as name="value" pairs. Some elements are void: they have no content and no end tag (<br>, <img>, <input>, <meta>, <link>, <hr>).

<a href="books.html" class="button" id="catalogue-link" title="See all books">Catalogue</a>
<img src="cover.jpg" alt="Cover of Learn HTML" width="300" height="400">

Nesting

Elements nest like boxes: close the inner one before the outer one. <p><em>right</em></p> is correct; <p><em>wrong</p></em> is not. Indent nested elements two spaces so the structure is visible in your editor.

Block and inline

Block-level elements (p, div, h1, ul, table, section...) start on a new line and stretch across the container. Inline elements (a, em, strong, span, img, code...) flow within the text. A block may contain inline elements; an inline element may not contain a block (except that <a> may wrap blocks in HTML5). CSS display can change this behaviour.

Comments and whitespace

<!-- This is a comment. Browsers ignore it. -->
<p>Multiple     spaces
   and line breaks collapse to a single space.</p>

Entities

Characters that have a meaning in HTML must be written as entities: &lt; for <, &gt; for >, &amp; for &. &nbsp; is a non-breaking space; &copy; is the copyright sign. See the entity table in the Value References part.

Lesson 4: Document structure

Use semantic elements to describe the parts of the page. They mean nothing visually (all look like a <div>) but give screen readers, search engines and other developers a map of the page.

ElementUse forHow many per page
<header>Introductory content of the page or of a section: logo, title, navigationOne per page plus one per article/section if needed
<nav>Major navigation blocksUsually one or two
<main>The unique content of this pageExactly one
<article>Self-contained composition: blog post, product, commentAny number
<section>Thematic grouping with a headingAny number
<aside>Tangential content: sidebar, pull quote, related linksAny number
<footer>Footer of the page or a section: copyright, contact, linksOne per page plus per section
<div>Generic container when no semantic element fits (mostly for styling)Any number
<body>
  <header>
    <h1>Cairo Book Shop</h1>
    <nav aria-label="Main">
      <ul>
        <li><a href="/">Home</a></li>
        <li><a href="/books/">Books</a></li>
        <li><a href="/contact/">Contact</a></li>
      </ul>
    </nav>
  </header>
  <main>
    <article>
      <h2>New arrivals</h2>
      <p>...</p>
    </article>
    <aside>
      <h2>Opening hours</h2>
      <p>Saturday to Thursday, 10:00 to 22:00</p>
    </aside>
  </main>
  <footer>
    <p>&copy; 2026 Cairo Book Shop &middot; <a href="/privacy/">Privacy</a></p>
  </footer>
</body>

Headings

Use one <h1> for the page title, then <h2> for main sections, <h3> inside them, and so on. Never skip levels for looks (h2 then h4); change the size with CSS instead. Screen reader users navigate by headings, so the outline must make sense on its own.

Lesson 5: Text content

Text elements carry meaning. Choose by what the text IS, not by how you want it to look; then style with CSS.

ElementMeaningDefault look
<p>ParagraphBlock with space above and below
<h1>-<h6>HeadingsBold, decreasing sizes
<strong>Strong importanceBold
<em>Stress emphasisItalic
<b>Keywords, product names, no extra importanceBold
<i>Different voice: technical term, foreign phrase, thoughtItalic
<mark>Highlighted for referenceYellow background
<small>Side comment, legal textSmaller
<s>No longer accurateStrikethrough
<del> / <ins>Removed / added textStrikethrough / underline
<sub> / <sup>Subscript / superscriptH2O, x2
<code>Code fragmentMonospace
<kbd>Keyboard inputMonospace
<samp>Program outputMonospace
<var>VariableItalic
<abbr title="...">AbbreviationDotted underline
<time datetime="...">Date/timePlain
<q>Short inline quotationQuotation marks
<blockquote>Long quotationIndented block
<cite>Title of a workItalic
<pre>Preformatted text (keeps spaces and line breaks)Monospace block
<br>Line break (addresses, poems only)-
<hr>Thematic breakHorizontal rule
<article>
  <h2>Learn HTML, <small>2nd edition</small></h2>
  <p>Published <time datetime="2026-03-01">1 March 2026</time>.
     <strong>Only 5 copies left.</strong> Price: <s>150 EGP</s> <mark>120 EGP</mark>.</p>
  <p>Press <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>S</kbd> to save. The <abbr title="HyperText Markup Language">HTML</abbr> file is <code>index.html</code>.</p>
  <blockquote cite="https://example.com/review">
    <p>The clearest introduction I have read.</p>
    <footer>&mdash; <cite>Web Weekly</cite></footer>
  </blockquote>
</article>

Typography basics in CSS

body { font-family: Georgia, 'Times New Roman', serif; font-size: 1.05rem; line-height: 1.6; }
h1, h2, h3 { font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; line-height: 1.2; }
p { margin: 0 0 1em; max-width: 65ch; }   /* 65 characters per line is comfortable */

Lesson 6: Lists and tables

Lists group related items; tables display structured data. This lesson is a summary; the chapter 'Lists and tables with CSS' in the CSS part covers every styling option in detail.

<ul class="features">
  <li>Responsive layout</li>
  <li>Semantic HTML</li>
  <li>Accessible components</li>
</ul>
<ol class="steps">
  <li>Plan content</li>
  <li>Structure markup</li>
  <li>Apply typography and layout</li>
</ol>
<dl class="glossary">
  <dt>HTML</dt><dd>Structure of a web page.</dd>
  <dt>CSS</dt><dd>Presentation and layout.</dd>
</dl>
/* card-style list with custom check marks */
.features { list-style: none; padding: 0; margin: 0; display: grid; gap: 12px; }
.features li { padding: 16px 20px; background: #fff; border-radius: 12px;
               box-shadow: 0 10px 25px rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.08); }
.features li::before { content: '\2714'; color: #04AA6D; margin-right: 12px; }
<table class="pricing">
  <thead>
    <tr><th scope="col">Plan</th><th scope="col">Price</th><th scope="col">Features</th></tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><th scope="row">Starter</th><td>$0</td><td>Basic components</td></tr>
    <tr><th scope="row">Pro</th><td>$19</td><td>Advanced layouts</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
.pricing { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; background: #fff; border-radius: 12px; overflow: hidden; }
.pricing th, .pricing td { padding: 16px 20px; text-align: left; }
.pricing thead { background: #04AA6D; color: #fff; }
.pricing tbody tr:nth-child(even) { background: #f9fafb; }
.table-wrapper { overflow-x: auto; }   /* wrap the table in this div for small screens */
  • Always use <th> for headers and add scope="col" or scope="row".
  • Provide a <caption> when the table's purpose is not obvious.
  • Keep tables for data, not layout.

Lesson 7: Links and navigation

The <a> element with an href attribute creates a hyperlink. The href can be absolute, relative to the current file, a fragment (#id) on the same page, or a special scheme such as mailto: or tel:.

<a href="https://example.com/">Absolute URL</a>
<a href="books/learn-html.html">Relative: file in the books folder</a>
<a href="../index.html">Relative: parent folder</a>
<a href="/contact/">Site-root relative</a>
<a href="#prices">Jump to the element with id="prices"</a>
<a href="mailto:info@example.com">Email us</a>
<a href="tel:+201001234567">Call us</a>
<a href="catalogue.pdf" download>Download the catalogue (PDF)</a>
<a href="https://partner.example" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Opens in a new tab</a>

Navigation bar

<nav aria-label="Main">
  <ul class="nav">
    <li><a href="/" aria-current="page">Home</a></li>
    <li><a href="/books/">Books</a></li>
    <li><a href="/about/">About</a></li>
  </ul>
</nav>

<style>
.nav { display: flex; gap: 4px; list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; background: #1b2431; }
.nav a { display: block; padding: 12px 18px; color: #fff; text-decoration: none; }
.nav a:hover, .nav a:focus-visible { background: #b90000; }
.nav a[aria-current="page"] { background: #444; }
</style>

Link states

Style the five states in this order (LVHFA) or later rules will override earlier ones: :link, :visited, :hover, :focus, :active.

a:link { color: #0645ad; }
a:visited { color: #551a8b; }
a:hover { text-decoration-thickness: 2px; }
a:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #ffbf47; outline-offset: 2px; }
a:active { color: #b90000; }
  • Link text must make sense alone: 'Read the shipping policy', not 'click here'.
  • Keep the underline or another non-colour cue so links are recognisable.
  • Never remove the focus outline without providing a visible replacement.
  • Use a <button> for actions (open menu, submit) and <a> for navigation.

Lesson 8: Images and media

<img src="images/cover.jpg" alt="Cover of Learn HTML: a red book with white letters" width="600" height="800" loading="lazy">

<figure>
  <img src="chart.png" alt="Sales grew from 120 in January to 340 in June">
  <figcaption>Figure 1. Monthly sales, first half of 2026.</figcaption>
</figure>

<picture>
  <source srcset="hero.avif" type="image/avif">
  <source srcset="hero.webp" type="image/webp">
  <img src="hero.jpg" alt="The shop front at night">
</picture>

<img src="small.jpg" srcset="small.jpg 480w, medium.jpg 960w, large.jpg 1600w"
     sizes="(max-width: 600px) 100vw, 50vw" alt="...">

<video controls width="640" poster="poster.jpg">
  <source src="tour.mp4" type="video/mp4">
  <track kind="captions" src="tour.en.vtt" srclang="en" label="English">
  Your browser does not support video.
</video>

<audio controls src="podcast.mp3"></audio>

Responsive images in CSS

img, video { max-width: 100%; height: auto; }          /* never overflow the container */
.thumb { width: 200px; aspect-ratio: 3 / 4; object-fit: cover; }   /* crop to a fixed shape */
.avatar { border-radius: 50%; }
  • alt is required. Describe the content and function; use alt="" for purely decorative images.
  • Always give width and height (or aspect-ratio) so the page does not jump while images load.
  • Use loading="lazy" for images below the fold, never for the main hero image.
  • Prefer AVIF/WebP with a JPEG fallback in <picture>; use SVG for logos and icons.
  • Provide captions for video and a transcript for audio.

Lesson 9: Forms and validation

<form action="/order" method="post">
  <fieldset>
    <legend>Your details</legend>
    <p>
      <label for="name">Full name</label>
      <input id="name" name="name" type="text" required autocomplete="name">
    </p>
    <p>
      <label for="email">Email</label>
      <input id="email" name="email" type="email" required autocomplete="email">
    </p>
    <p>
      <label for="qty">Quantity</label>
      <input id="qty" name="qty" type="number" min="1" max="10" value="1">
    </p>
    <p>
      <label for="format">Format</label>
      <select id="format" name="format">
        <option value="pdf">PDF</option>
        <option value="print">Printed</option>
      </select>
    </p>
    <p>
      <label for="notes">Notes</label>
      <textarea id="notes" name="notes" rows="3"></textarea>
    </p>
    <p>
      <input id="terms" name="terms" type="checkbox" required>
      <label for="terms">I accept the terms</label>
    </p>
  </fieldset>
  <button type="submit">Order</button>
</form>

Built-in validation

AttributeChecks
requiredField is not empty
type="email" / url / number / dateValue has the right format
min / max / stepNumeric or date range
minlength / maxlengthText length
pattern="[0-9]{5}"Regular expression
novalidate (on form)Turns built-in validation off

Styling forms and validation states

label { display: block; font-weight: 600; margin-bottom: .25rem; }
input, select, textarea, button { font: inherit; }
input, select, textarea {
  width: 100%; padding: .6rem .8rem; border: 1px solid #bbb; border-radius: 6px;
}
input:focus-visible, select:focus-visible, textarea:focus-visible {
  outline: 3px solid #ffbf47; outline-offset: 1px; border-color: #b90000;
}
input:user-invalid { border-color: #c00; background: #fff5f5; }
input:user-valid { border-color: #2a7; }
button[type="submit"] {
  background: #b90000; color: #fff; border: 0; padding: .7rem 1.4rem; border-radius: 999px; cursor: pointer;
}
button:disabled { opacity: .5; cursor: not-allowed; }
  • Every control needs a <label> connected by for/id (or wrapping it).
  • Group radio buttons and checkboxes in a <fieldset> with a <legend>.
  • Use the right type: it changes the mobile keyboard and adds validation for free.
  • Show error messages in text next to the field, not only by colour.

Lesson 10: Reusable components

A component is a block of HTML plus the CSS that styles it, designed so you can copy it anywhere. Give it one class name on the outer element and prefix inner classes with it (card, card__title, card--featured) so styles do not leak.

<article class="card card--featured">
  <img class="card__image" src="cover.jpg" alt="">
  <div class="card__body">
    <h3 class="card__title">Learn HTML</h3>
    <p class="card__text">From zero to a complete website.</p>
    <a class="btn" href="learn-html.html">Details</a>
  </div>
</article>
.card {
  display: flex; flex-direction: column;
  border: 1px solid #e2e8f0; border-radius: 16px; overflow: hidden; background: #fff;
}
.card__image { aspect-ratio: 3 / 4; object-fit: cover; }
.card__body { padding: 1rem 1.25rem; display: grid; gap: .5rem; }
.card__title { margin: 0; font-size: 1.1rem; }
.card--featured { border-color: #b90000; box-shadow: 0 10px 30px rgba(185, 0, 0, .15); }
.btn {
  display: inline-block; padding: .5rem 1rem; border-radius: 999px;
  background: #b90000; color: #fff; text-decoration: none; justify-self: start;
}
.btn:hover { background: #900; }

Design tokens with custom properties

:root {
  --brand: #b90000;
  --ink: #1b2431;
  --radius: 12px;
  --space-1: .5rem; --space-2: 1rem; --space-3: 2rem;
}
.card { border-radius: var(--radius); padding: var(--space-2); }
.btn { background: var(--brand); }

Change --brand once and every component follows. Put the variables in :root so they are available everywhere.

Lesson 11: Styling essentials - the three ways to add CSS

MethodHowUse when
External style sheet<link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css"> in <head>Always, for real sites: one file shared by all pages, cached by the browser
Internal style sheet<style> ... </style> in <head>Single-page demos, emails, this reference's examples
Inline stylestyle="color: red" attribute on the elementRarely: one-off values generated by a program; hard to override and maintain

Anatomy of a rule

selector {
  property: value;      /* a declaration */
  property: value;
}

h1 {
  color: #b90000;
  font-size: 2rem;
}

Comments

/* CSS comments look like this and can span
   several lines. There is no // comment in CSS. */

Units

UnitMeaningTypical use
pxCSS pixelBorders, small fixed sizes
remRelative to the root font size (16px by default)Font sizes, spacing, widths - respects user zoom settings
emRelative to the element's own font sizePadding around text, icon sizes
%Relative to the parentWidths
vw / vh1% of viewport width/heightFull-screen sections, fluid type
chWidth of the digit 0Line length (max-width: 65ch)
frFraction of free space (Grid only)Column tracks

Colours

color: red;                 /* 148 named colours */
color: #b90000;             /* hex: rr gg bb */
color: #b90000cc;           /* hex with alpha */
color: rgb(185 0 0);
color: rgb(185 0 0 / 50%);  /* 50% transparent */
color: hsl(0 100% 36%);     /* hue, saturation, lightness */
color: oklch(50% 0.2 25);   /* perceptually uniform, wide gamut */
color: currentColor;        /* the element's text colour */

Lesson 12: Selectors and specificity

Selectors are like addresses for elements: they point CSS at the exact parts of the page you want to change.

Selector typeExampleMatches
Typep { }All <p> elements
Class.btn { }Elements with class="btn"
ID#hero { }The element with id="hero"
Universal* { }All elements
Attributea[target="_blank"], input[type="email"], [class^="icon-"]Elements by attribute presence or value
Descendant.card pAny <p> inside .card
Child.card > h3<h3> directly inside .card
Adjacent siblingh2 + pThe <p> immediately after an <h2>
General siblingh2 ~ pEvery <p> after an <h2> in the same parent
Pseudo-classa:hover, input:required, li:nth-child(2n), :is(), :where(), :has()Elements in a state or position
Pseudo-elementp::first-line, p::after, li::markerParts of an element

Specificity: who wins

When two rules set the same property on the same element, the more specific selector wins. Count (IDs, classes/attributes/pseudo-classes, types/pseudo-elements). Inline styles beat everything except !important. If specificity ties, the later rule wins.

SelectorScore (id, class, type)
p0,0,1
.card p0,1,1
.card.highlight p0,2,1
#feature.card p1,1,1
style="..."1,0,0,0 (inline)
:where(.a .b)0,0,0 (where adds nothing)
<article class="card"><p>Default card text.</p></article>
<article class="card highlight"><p>Highlight card text.</p></article>
<article id="feature" class="card highlight"><p>Feature card text (ID wins).</p></article>

<style>
.card p { color: #475569; }
.card.highlight p { color: #2563eb; }
#feature.card p { color: #be123c; }   /* highest specificity: wins */
</style>

Using the cascade strategically

  • Write from general to specific: base styles first, overrides later.
  • Prefer classes; avoid IDs and long descendant chains in selectors.
  • Avoid !important. If you need it, the real fix is a better selector or order.
  • Use @layer to put resets, base, components and utilities in explicit layers.
  • Debug in DevTools: the Styles panel shows every matching rule, crossed out when overridden.

Lesson 13: Cascade and inheritance

The cascade decides which declaration wins, in this order: (1) origin and importance (user-agent < user < author; !important reverses), (2) cascade layers, (3) specificity, (4) source order. Inheritance passes some property values from parent to child automatically.

Inherited by defaultNot inherited
color, font-*, line-height, text-align, letter-spacing, visibility, cursor, list-style, directionmargin, padding, border, background, width, height, display, position
body { color: #1b2431; font-family: Georgia, serif; }   /* all text inherits these */
.box { border: 1px solid; }                              /* children do NOT get a border */

/* keywords that work on every property */
.reset { color: inherit; }     /* take the parent's value */
.plain { all: initial; }       /* specification default */
.norm  { all: unset; }         /* inherit if inheritable, otherwise initial */
.rev   { all: revert; }        /* browser default style */

Cascade layers

@layer reset, base, components, utilities;

@layer reset { * { margin: 0; box-sizing: border-box; } }
@layer base { body { font: 1rem/1.6 system-ui; } }
@layer components { .btn { padding: .5rem 1rem; } }
@layer utilities { .hidden { display: none; } }
/* later layers beat earlier ones regardless of specificity */

Lesson 14: Typography

body {
  font-family: 'Inter', system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif;
  font-size: clamp(1rem, 0.95rem + 0.3vw, 1.125rem);
  line-height: 1.6;
}
h1 { font-size: clamp(2rem, 1.5rem + 2.5vw, 3.5rem); line-height: 1.1; letter-spacing: -0.02em; }
h2 { font-size: 1.75rem; }
p  { max-width: 65ch; margin-block: 0 1em; }
.lead { font-size: 1.25rem; color: #475569; }
.caps { text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: .08em; font-size: .8rem; }
.num { font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }   /* aligned digits in tables */

Loading a web font

@font-face {
  font-family: 'Inter';
  src: url('fonts/inter.woff2') format('woff2');
  font-weight: 100 900;
  font-display: swap;
}

Or link a font service in the <head> with <link rel="preconnect"> and <link rel="stylesheet">. Always list fallback fonts after the web font.

Arabic and right-to-left text

<html lang="ar" dir="rtl">
...
body { font-family: 'Noto Naskh Arabic', 'Cairo', 'Segoe UI', Tahoma, sans-serif; line-height: 1.8; }
/* use logical properties so layout mirrors automatically */
.card { padding-inline-start: 1rem; margin-inline-end: auto; border-inline-start: 4px solid #b90000; }
  • Font stacks: preferred font first, similar fallbacks next, generic family (serif, sans-serif, monospace) last.
  • Line length 45-75 characters; line-height 1.5-1.7 for body text.
  • Use rem for font sizes so users can enlarge text in their browser settings.
  • Do not justify text on the web; ragged right reads better and avoids rivers.

Lesson 15: Colours and backgrounds

:root {
  --brand: #b90000;
  --brand-dark: color-mix(in oklab, var(--brand), black 20%);
  --surface: #fff;
  --ink: #1b2431;
}
.hero {
  background: linear-gradient(120deg, #2563eb 0%, #7c3aed 50%, #0f172a 100%);
  color: #fff;
}
.banner {
  background-image: url('hero.jpg');
  background-size: cover;
  background-position: center;
  background-repeat: no-repeat;
}
.tint { background-color: rgb(185 0 0 / 10%); }
.card { background: var(--surface); box-shadow: 0 14px 28px rgba(15, 23, 42, 0.08); }

Contrast

Text must have a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 against its background (3:1 for large text). #767676 on white is the lightest grey that passes. Check with the DevTools colour picker or a contrast checker. Never convey information by colour alone.

Dark mode

:root { color-scheme: light dark; }
@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
  :root { --surface: #14181f; --ink: #e6e9ef; }
}
body { background: var(--surface); color: var(--ink); }

Lesson 16: The box model

Every element is a rectangular box: content in the middle, padding around it, the border wrapping both, and the margin as the outside buffer between neighbours.

+---------------- margin (transparent) ----------------+
|  +------------- border ---------------------------+  |
|  |  +---------- padding ------------------------+ |  |
|  |  |                                           | |  |
|  |  |               content                     | |  |
|  |  |                                           | |  |
|  |  +-------------------------------------------+ |  |
|  +------------------------------------------------+  |
+------------------------------------------------------+

content-box versus border-box

By default (box-sizing: content-box) width and height apply to the content only, so a 300px box with 24px padding and a 2px border is really 352px wide. With border-box the declared size includes padding and border: a 300px box stays 300px. Almost every project switches to border-box globally.

*, *::before, *::after { box-sizing: border-box; }

.card {
  width: 320px;
  padding: 24px;
  border: 2px solid #cbd5f5;
  margin-bottom: 24px;
}
.callout {
  margin: 32px 0;
  padding: 16px;
  border-left: 6px solid #2563eb;
  background: #eff6ff;
}

Shorthands

DeclarationMeaning
margin: 24px;All four sides
margin: 24px 16px;top/bottom 24px, left/right 16px
padding: 8px 12px 16px;top 8, left/right 12, bottom 16
padding: 1px 2px 3px 4px;top, right, bottom, left (clockwise)
border: 2px solid #1d4ed8;width, style, colour
margin: 0 auto;Centre a block with a width
margin-inline: auto;Same, using logical properties

Collapsing margins

  • Vertical margins between block elements collapse to the largest value (a 24px bottom margin followed by a 16px top margin gives 24px, not 40px).
  • A parent and its first/last child can share margins unless padding, a border or display: flow-root intervenes.
  • Margins never collapse inside Flexbox or Grid containers - one more reason to use gap.

Visualising with DevTools

Inspect an element in Chrome or Firefox and look at the Computed panel: it shows a diagram with margin, border, padding and content measurements. Hover each part to highlight it on the page.

Spacing strategies

  • Create a spacing scale (base of 4 or 8 pixels) and stick to it: 4, 8, 16, 24, 32, 48.
  • Store it in custom properties (--space-2: 1rem) for consistency.
  • Combine gap with Flexbox or Grid to separate items instead of adding margins to each one.

Lesson 17: Layout fundamentals - normal flow

Without any layout CSS, browsers lay elements out in normal flow: block boxes stack vertically and fill the width; inline boxes flow horizontally inside lines. Every layout technique is a way of taking elements out of, or rearranging, this flow.

display valueBehaviour
blockNew line, full width, respects width/height/margins
inlineFlows in text; width/height ignored; only horizontal padding/margin effective
inline-blockFlows in text but respects width/height/vertical margins
flex / inline-flexChildren laid out along one axis
grid / inline-gridChildren placed in rows and columns
flow-rootBlock that contains its floats and stops margin collapsing
noneRemoved from rendering and from the accessibility tree
contentsBox disappears, children remain

Floats (legacy but still useful for text wrap)

img.left { float: left; margin: 0 1rem 1rem 0; }
.clearfix::after { content: ''; display: block; clear: both; }
/* modern: */ .wrapper { display: flow-root; }

Overflow

.box { height: 200px; overflow: auto; }      /* scrollbars when needed */
.clip { overflow: hidden; }                   /* cut off */
.marquee { white-space: nowrap; overflow-x: auto; }

Lesson 18: Positioning and z-index

positionBehaviour
static (default)Normal flow; top/left have no effect
relativeNormal flow, then nudged by top/left; creates a reference for absolute children
absoluteRemoved from flow; placed relative to the nearest positioned ancestor
fixedRemoved from flow; placed relative to the viewport; stays while scrolling
stickyNormal flow until it reaches the given offset, then sticks (inside its parent)
.card { position: relative; }
.card .badge {
  position: absolute; top: 12px; right: 12px;
  background: #b90000; color: #fff; padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 999px;
}
.site-header { position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: 10; background: #fff; }
.back-to-top { position: fixed; bottom: 1rem; inset-inline-end: 1rem; }
.modal-backdrop { position: fixed; inset: 0; background: rgb(0 0 0 / 50%); z-index: 100; }

z-index and stacking contexts

  • z-index only works on positioned elements (and flex/grid items).
  • Higher values are drawn on top. Keep a scale: 10 header, 100 dropdown, 1000 modal.
  • opacity < 1, transform, filter and position: fixed create a new stacking context: children cannot escape it no matter how large their z-index.

Lesson 19: Flexbox

Flexbox lays out children in one dimension - a row or a column - and distributes space between them. It is ideal for navigation bars, toolbars, card strips, media objects and form rows.

Creating a flex container

.toolbar {
  display: flex;          /* children become flex items in a row */
  gap: 16px;
  align-items: center;
}
.toolbar .spacer { flex: 1 1 auto; }   /* pushes following items to the right */

Axes and alignment

  • The main axis follows flex-direction (row = horizontal, column = vertical). Distribute items along it with justify-content.
  • The cross axis is perpendicular. Align items on it with align-items (all) or align-self (one).
  • Use gap for consistent spacing instead of margins.
Property (container)Values
flex-directionrow | row-reverse | column | column-reverse
flex-wrapnowrap | wrap | wrap-reverse
justify-contentflex-start | center | flex-end | space-between | space-around | space-evenly
align-itemsstretch | flex-start | center | flex-end | baseline
align-contentSame as justify-content, for multiple lines
gaprow-gap column-gap
Property (item)Meaning
flex: grow shrink basisHow the item takes and gives up space (default 0 1 auto)
flex: 1Equal widths, share all free space
flex: 0 0 300pxFixed 300px, never grows or shrinks
flex: 1 1 220pxIdeal 220px, may grow or shrink; wraps nicely
orderVisual order (default 0); does not change tab order
align-selfOverride align-items for one item

Card strip

<section class="cards">
  <article><h2>Prototype</h2><p>Validate ideas quickly with interactive mockups.</p></article>
  <article><h2>Build</h2><p>Create accessible, responsive components in code.</p></article>
  <article><h2>Ship</h2><p>Automate deployment pipelines and monitoring.</p></article>
</section>

<style>
.cards {
  display: flex;
  gap: 24px;
  justify-content: center;
  align-items: stretch;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
}
.cards article {
  flex: 1 1 220px;
  padding: 24px;
  border-radius: 16px;
  background: #f1f5f9;
}
</style>

Common patterns

/* centre anything */
.center { display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center; min-height: 100vh; }

/* split layout 2:1 */
.split { display: flex; gap: 2rem; }
.split > main { flex: 2; }
.split > aside { flex: 1; }

/* media object that stacks on small screens */
.media { display: flex; gap: 1rem; flex-wrap: wrap; }
.media img { flex: 0 0 120px; }
.media .body { flex: 1 1 240px; }

/* sticky footer */
body { min-height: 100vh; display: flex; flex-direction: column; }
main { flex: 1; }

Lesson 20: CSS Grid

Grid lays out children in two dimensions at once. You declare tracks (columns and rows) on the container and place items into cells or areas. A track is one column or row - imagine drawing a table with lines; Grid lets you define those lines in CSS.

.layout {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: 240px 1fr;      /* two columns */
  grid-template-rows: auto 1fr auto;     /* three rows */
  gap: 24px;
  min-height: 100vh;
}

Track sizing

PatternMeaning
300px 1fr 1frFixed sidebar, two equal flexible columns
repeat(12, minmax(0, 1fr))Classic 12-column grid
repeat(auto-fit, minmax(220px, 1fr))As many 220px+ columns as fit; collapses empty tracks
repeat(auto-fill, minmax(220px, 1fr))Same but keeps empty tracks
fit-content(300px)Shrink to content, max 300px
max-content / min-contentSize to the longest / shortest content

Placing items

.hero .copy   { grid-column: span 6; }          /* auto row, six columns wide */
.item         { grid-column: 1 / 7; grid-row: 2 / span 2; }
.full         { grid-column: 1 / -1; }          /* first to last line */

/* named areas */
.page {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: 240px 1fr;
  grid-template-areas:
    'header header'
    'nav    main'
    'footer footer';
}
.page > header { grid-area: header; }
.page > nav    { grid-area: nav; }
.page > main   { grid-area: main; }
.page > footer { grid-area: footer; }
@media (max-width: 700px) {
  .page { grid-template-columns: 1fr; grid-template-areas: 'header' 'nav' 'main' 'footer'; }
}

Alignment

  • justify-items / align-items align content inside each cell.
  • justify-content / align-content distribute the whole grid inside the container.
  • place-items and place-content combine both axes: place-items: center centres everything.

Marketing layout example

<section class="hero">
  <div class="copy">
    <h1>Design systems that scale</h1>
    <p>Unify design and engineering with a shared language.</p>
    <a class="cta" href="#">Get started</a>
  </div>
  <div class="visual">
    <h2>Release highlights</h2>
    <ul><li>Theme builder</li><li>Usage analytics</li><li>Accessibility tracking</li></ul>
  </div>
</section>
<section class="features">
  <article><h3>Token management</h3><p>...</p></article>
  <article><h3>Component lifecycles</h3><p>...</p></article>
  <article><h3>Design reviews</h3><p>...</p></article>
</section>
.hero {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(12, minmax(0, 1fr));
  gap: 24px;
  padding: 88px clamp(24px, 6vw, 80px);
  background: linear-gradient(120deg, #2563eb 0%, #7c3aed 50%, #0f172a 100%);
  color: #fff;
}
.hero .copy   { grid-column: span 6; max-width: 480px; }
.hero .visual { grid-column: span 6; background: rgba(255,255,255,0.09); border-radius: 24px; padding: 40px; }
.features {
  display: grid;
  gap: 24px;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(220px, 1fr));
  padding: clamp(32px, 5vw, 80px);
}
.features article { border: 1px solid #e2e8f0; border-radius: 20px; padding: 28px; background: #fff; }
@media (max-width: 900px) {
  .hero .copy, .hero .visual { grid-column: 1 / -1; }
}

The hero spans six columns per side on large screens and collapses to full width through the media query; the feature grid adapts its card count automatically.

Lesson 21: Layout patterns

A few patterns cover most pages. Copy them and adjust the numbers.

/* 1. Centred content column */
.container { width: min(100% - 2rem, 70rem); margin-inline: auto; }

/* 2. Holy grail: header, sidebar, content, footer */
.holy { display: grid; grid-template-rows: auto 1fr auto; grid-template-columns: 16rem 1fr; min-height: 100vh; }
.holy > header, .holy > footer { grid-column: 1 / -1; }

/* 3. Auto grid of cards */
.grid { display: grid; gap: 1.5rem; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(16rem, 1fr)); }

/* 4. Sidebar that stacks when narrow (no media query) */
.with-sidebar { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 2rem; }
.with-sidebar > aside { flex: 1 1 15rem; }
.with-sidebar > main  { flex: 999 1 25rem; }

/* 5. Cluster of tags/buttons */
.cluster { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: .5rem; align-items: center; }

/* 6. Stack with consistent vertical rhythm */
.stack > * + * { margin-block-start: 1rem; }

/* 7. Cover: hero with centred content */
.cover { min-height: 100vh; display: grid; place-items: center; }

/* 8. Full-bleed section inside a narrow column */
.full-bleed { width: 100vw; margin-inline: calc(50% - 50vw); }

Lesson 22: Responsive design

  • Add <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"> - without it nothing else works on phones.
  • Design mobile-first: write styles for narrow screens first, then add min-width media queries for tablets and desktops.
  • Use relative units (rem, %, vw, ch) so elements scale naturally.
  • A breakpoint is the width where your layout needs to change. Choose breakpoints from your content, not from device names.

Mobile-first media queries

:root { --space: clamp(1rem, 2vw, 1.5rem); }
.page { display: grid; gap: var(--space); }
@media (min-width: 768px) {
  .page { grid-template-columns: 240px 1fr; }
}
@media (min-width: 1200px) {
  .page { grid-template-columns: 280px 2fr 1fr; }
}

Fluid grids and typography

.cards { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(220px, 1fr)); gap: 1.5rem; }
h1 { font-size: clamp(1.75rem, 1.2rem + 2.5vw, 3rem); }   /* min, preferred, max */
p  { max-width: 65ch; }

Container queries

.card-holder { container-type: inline-size; }
@container (min-width: 500px) {
  .card { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 160px 1fr; }
}

Container queries watch the size of a parent element instead of the whole screen, so a component adapts wherever it is placed.

Responsive media

img, video, iframe { max-width: 100%; height: auto; }
.video-wrap { aspect-ratio: 16 / 9; }
.video-wrap iframe { width: 100%; height: 100%; }

Other media features

@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { *, *::before, *::after { animation: none !important; transition: none !important; } }
@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { ... }
@media (hover: hover) { .card:hover { transform: translateY(-4px); } }   /* only devices with a mouse */
@media print { nav, footer { display: none; } }
@media (orientation: landscape) { ... }

Testing

  • Use DevTools device mode (Ctrl+Shift+M) to preview breakpoints.
  • Test on a real phone when possible; check touch target size (at least 44x44px) and both orientations.
  • Check text at 200% zoom: nothing should overlap or be cut off.

Lesson 23: Responsive components

/* Navigation that becomes a hamburger menu without JavaScript */
<nav class="nav">
  <input type="checkbox" id="menu" class="nav__toggle" hidden>
  <label for="menu" class="nav__button" aria-label="Menu">&#9776;</label>
  <ul class="nav__list">
    <li><a href="/">Home</a></li>
    <li><a href="/books/">Books</a></li>
    <li><a href="/contact/">Contact</a></li>
  </ul>
</nav>

<style>
.nav__list { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; display: none; }
.nav__toggle:checked ~ .nav__list { display: block; }
@media (min-width: 700px) {
  .nav__button { display: none; }
  .nav__list { display: flex !important; gap: 1rem; }
}
</style>
/* Responsive table (see the Lists and tables chapter) */
.table-wrapper { overflow-x: auto; }

/* Responsive card: image beside text when there is room */
.card { display: grid; gap: 1rem; }
@container (min-width: 480px) { .card { grid-template-columns: 200px 1fr; } }

/* Responsive embed */
.embed { aspect-ratio: 16 / 9; width: 100%; }

/* Responsive form: labels beside fields on wide screens */
.form-row { display: grid; gap: .5rem; }
@media (min-width: 600px) { .form-row { grid-template-columns: 10rem 1fr; align-items: center; } }

Lesson 24: Custom properties (CSS variables)

Custom properties store a value under a name that starts with two dashes. Read it with var(). They cascade and inherit like other properties, can be changed in media queries or on a class, and can be read and set from JavaScript.

:root {
  --brand: #b90000;
  --radius: 12px;
  --shadow: 0 10px 25px rgb(15 23 42 / 8%);
}
.btn { background: var(--brand); border-radius: var(--radius); }
.card { box-shadow: var(--shadow); padding: var(--card-padding, 1rem); }   /* fallback value */

/* theming by scope */
.theme-green { --brand: #04AA6D; }

/* change on state */
.btn:hover { --brand: #900; }

/* JavaScript */
document.documentElement.style.setProperty('--brand', '#0055aa');

Typed properties with @property

@property --angle {
  syntax: '<angle>';
  inherits: false;
  initial-value: 0deg;
}
.spin { background: conic-gradient(from var(--angle), red, blue); transition: --angle 1s; }
.spin:hover { --angle: 360deg; }

Lesson 25: calc() and CSS functions

FunctionPurposeExample
calc()Arithmetic mixing unitswidth: calc(100% - 2rem)
min()Smallest of several valueswidth: min(90%, 60rem)
max()Largest of several valuesfont-size: max(1rem, 2vw)
clamp()Value between a minimum and maximumfont-size: clamp(1rem, 2vw, 1.5rem)
var()Read a custom propertycolor: var(--brand, black)
attr()Read an HTML attribute (content only)content: attr(data-label)
url()Reference a filebackground: url('bg.png')
rgb() hsl() oklch() color-mix()Colourscolor-mix(in oklab, red, white 30%)
linear-gradient() radial-gradient() conic-gradient()Gradient imagesbackground: linear-gradient(90deg, red, blue)
repeat() minmax() fit-content()Grid tracksrepeat(auto-fit, minmax(200px, 1fr))
translate() rotate() scale()Transformstransform: rotate(45deg)
counter()Generated numberingcontent: counter(item)
env()Environment values (phone notches)padding-bottom: env(safe-area-inset-bottom)
round() mod() rem() abs() sign()Mathswidth: round(down, 33.3%, 1px)
.sidebar { width: calc(100% / 3 - 1rem); }
.container { width: min(100% - 2rem, 70rem); }
h1 { font-size: clamp(1.75rem, 1rem + 3vw, 3rem); }
.hero { min-height: calc(100vh - var(--header-height)); }

Lesson 26: Transitions

A transition animates a property smoothly from its old value to its new value when the value changes (on hover, focus, class change...). Set it on the element's normal state, not on the :hover state, so it plays both ways.

.btn {
  background: #b90000;
  transition: background-color .2s ease, transform .15s ease;
}
.btn:hover { background: #900; transform: translateY(-2px); }

/* longhands */
.panel {
  transition-property: opacity, transform;
  transition-duration: 300ms;
  transition-timing-function: cubic-bezier(.2, .8, .2, 1);
  transition-delay: 0s;
}
Timing functionFeel
ease (default)Fast start, slow end
linearConstant speed
ease-inSlow start
ease-outSlow end (best for entering)
ease-in-outSlow both ends
steps(4)Jumps in 4 steps
cubic-bezier(x1,y1,x2,y2)Custom curve
  • Animate only transform and opacity when possible; they are cheap for the browser. Animating width, height or top causes layout work.
  • Keep durations short: 150-300ms for interface feedback.
  • Respect prefers-reduced-motion.
  • display cannot be transitioned; use opacity/visibility or the newer transition-behavior: allow-discrete with @starting-style.

Lesson 27: Transforms

.a { transform: translate(20px, 10px); }      /* move */
.b { transform: rotate(15deg); }              /* turn */
.c { transform: scale(1.1); }                 /* grow 10% */
.d { transform: skewX(10deg); }               /* slant */
.e { transform: rotate(45deg) scale(.8); }    /* combined, applied right to left */
.f { transform-origin: top left; }            /* pivot point */

/* individual properties (no ordering problems) */
.g { translate: 0 -4px; rotate: 3deg; scale: 1.05; }

/* 3D */
.scene { perspective: 800px; }
.card3d { transform: rotateY(30deg); transform-style: preserve-3d; backface-visibility: hidden; }
  • Transforms do not affect the layout of other elements; the box keeps its original space.
  • They create a stacking context and a containing block for fixed children.
  • Combine with transition for hover lift effects: .card:hover { transform: translateY(-4px); }

Lesson 28: Animations

@keyframes fade-up {
  from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(12px); }
  to   { opacity: 1; transform: none; }
}
.reveal { animation: fade-up .5s ease-out both; }

@keyframes pulse {
  0%, 100% { transform: scale(1); }
  50%      { transform: scale(1.06); }
}
.badge { animation: pulse 1.5s ease-in-out infinite; }

/* longhands */
.spinner {
  animation-name: spin;
  animation-duration: 1s;
  animation-timing-function: linear;
  animation-iteration-count: infinite;
  animation-direction: normal;      /* reverse | alternate */
  animation-fill-mode: forwards;    /* keep final state */
  animation-play-state: running;    /* paused */
  animation-delay: 0s;
}
@keyframes spin { to { transform: rotate(1turn); } }

/* scroll-driven (new) */
.progress { animation: grow linear; animation-timeline: scroll(); }
@keyframes grow { from { scale: 0 1; } to { scale: 1 1; } }
  • Use transitions for state changes and animations for things that run on their own or loop.
  • Pause or remove animations for users who set prefers-reduced-motion.
  • Avoid animating more than a few elements at once on mobile.

Lesson 29: Effects and filters

.card { box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgb(0 0 0 / 8%), 0 8px 24px rgb(0 0 0 / 12%); }
.text { text-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgb(0 0 0 / 40%); }
.round { border-radius: 16px; }   /* 50% for a circle */
.glass { background: rgb(255 255 255 / 60%); backdrop-filter: blur(12px); }
.grey { filter: grayscale(100%); }
.grey:hover { filter: none; }
.dim { filter: brightness(.8) contrast(1.1) saturate(1.2); }
.blurred { filter: blur(4px); }
.shadowed-png { filter: drop-shadow(0 4px 6px rgb(0 0 0 / 30%)); }   /* follows transparent shape */
.fade { opacity: .6; }
.blend { mix-blend-mode: multiply; }
.gradient-text {
  background: linear-gradient(90deg, #b90000, #ff7a00);
  -webkit-background-clip: text; background-clip: text; color: transparent;
}
.clipped { clip-path: circle(50%); }
.cut { clip-path: polygon(0 0, 100% 0, 100% 80%, 0 100%); }

Lesson 30: Accessibility

  • Use semantic HTML first: headings, lists, tables, buttons, links and landmarks give screen readers structure for free.
  • Every image needs alt text; decorative images use alt="".
  • Every form control needs a label. Error messages must be text, associated with the field via aria-describedby.
  • Keyboard: everything clickable must be reachable with Tab and operable with Enter/Space. Never remove :focus outlines without a visible replacement (:focus-visible).
  • Colour contrast at least 4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for large text and UI components. Do not use colour alone to convey meaning.
  • Set lang on <html>; use dir="rtl" for Arabic and Hebrew.
  • Respect user preferences: prefers-reduced-motion, prefers-color-scheme, prefers-contrast.
  • Use ARIA only when no native element does the job. aria-label, aria-labelledby, aria-describedby, aria-current, aria-expanded and role are the most common.
  • Hide content properly: display: none / hidden attribute hides from everyone; the .sr-only pattern hides visually but keeps it for screen readers.
  • Test with the keyboard alone, with a screen reader (NVDA on Windows, VoiceOver on Mac/iOS, TalkBack on Android) and with an automatic checker (Lighthouse, axe).
.sr-only {
  position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding: 0; margin: -1px;
  overflow: hidden; clip: rect(0 0 0 0); white-space: nowrap; border: 0;
}
.skip-link { position: absolute; top: -100px; }
.skip-link:focus { top: 0; }

<a class="skip-link" href="#main">Skip to content</a>
<button aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="menu">Menu</button>
<ul id="menu" hidden>...</ul>

Lesson 31: Design systems

A design system is the set of tokens (colours, spacing, type scale), components and rules a site is built from. Even a small site benefits: decide once, reuse everywhere.

:root {
  /* colour tokens */
  --c-brand: #b90000; --c-ink: #1b2431; --c-muted: #5b6472; --c-line: #d9d2c3; --c-surface: #fff; --c-bg: #faf8f3;
  /* type scale (1.25 ratio) */
  --fs-0: 1rem; --fs-1: 1.25rem; --fs-2: 1.563rem; --fs-3: 1.953rem; --fs-4: 2.441rem;
  /* spacing scale */
  --s-1: .25rem; --s-2: .5rem; --s-3: 1rem; --s-4: 1.5rem; --s-5: 2rem; --s-6: 3rem;
  /* shape */
  --radius: 12px; --shadow: 0 10px 25px rgb(15 23 42 / 8%);
}

Naming conventions

ConventionExampleIdea
BEM.card, .card__title, .card--featuredBlock, element, modifier
Utility classes.mt-3, .flex, .text-centerOne class = one declaration
State classes.is-open, .is-activeToggled by JavaScript
Data attributes[data-state="open"]State without class juggling

File organisation

css/
  reset.css        /* box-sizing, margins, images */
  tokens.css       /* :root variables */
  base.css         /* body, headings, links, tables, forms */
  components/      /* card.css, button.css, nav.css */
  utilities.css    /* .sr-only, .container, .stack */

/* one entry file */
@layer reset, tokens, base, components, utilities;
@import url('reset.css') layer(reset);
@import url('tokens.css') layer(tokens);
...

Lesson 32: Performance

  • Put CSS in <head> (render-blocking but needed first) and scripts at the end of <body> or with defer.
  • Compress images: AVIF/WebP, correct dimensions, loading="lazy" below the fold, width/height attributes to avoid layout shift.
  • Use font-display: swap and preload the main font: <link rel="preload" href="font.woff2" as="font" type="font/woff2" crossorigin>.
  • Keep CSS small: remove unused rules, avoid deep selectors, use one style sheet per site.
  • Prefer transform/opacity animations; use will-change sparingly.
  • content-visibility: auto on long lists skips rendering off-screen sections.
  • Preconnect to third-party origins you will use soon: <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin>.
  • Measure with Lighthouse (DevTools > Lighthouse) and aim for good Core Web Vitals: LCP under 2.5s, CLS under 0.1, INP under 200ms.
<link rel="preload" as="image" href="hero.avif" fetchpriority="high">
<img src="hero.avif" alt="..." width="1600" height="900" fetchpriority="high">
<img src="later.jpg" alt="..." width="800" height="600" loading="lazy" decoding="async">
<script src="app.js" defer></script>

Lesson 33: Debugging and testing

DevTools checklist

  • Elements panel: is the HTML what you expected? Unclosed tags show up as unexpected nesting here.
  • Styles panel: which rules apply? Crossed-out declarations are overridden (specificity/order) or invalid (typo). A yellow warning triangle means the property or value is unknown.
  • Computed panel: the final value of every property and the box model diagram.
  • Toggle :hov to force :hover/:focus states; edit values live and copy them back to your file.
  • Console: red messages for 404 (file not found - check paths and spelling) and script errors.
  • Network panel: is styles.css actually loading? Status 200 is good; 404 means the path is wrong.

Common CSS bugs and fixes

SymptomLikely causeFix
Nothing changesStyle sheet not loaded, cached, or selector does not matchCheck Network panel; hard reload (Ctrl+F5); inspect the element
Property ignoredTypo, invalid value, or property does not apply to that display typeLook for the warning icon; check width on inline elements, vertical-align on blocks
Margin does not workMargin collapse or inline elementUse padding, display: block/flow-root, or gap
Element wider than screen100% width plus padding (content-box)box-sizing: border-box; max-width: 100%
z-index has no effectElement not positioned or trapped in a stacking contextAdd position: relative; move it out of the transformed/opacity parent
Centre does not workmargin: auto on an element without width, or on inlineSet a width or use flex/grid centring
Text overflows boxLong word/URLoverflow-wrap: anywhere; or <wbr>
Font not appliedWrong name, quotes, or font not loadedCheck @font-face URL in Network panel; quote multi-word names

Validate and test

  • HTML validator: https://validator.w3.org/ - CSS validator: https://jigsaw.w3.org/css-validator/
  • Test in at least Chrome and Firefox; check Safari on an iPhone if you can.
  • Test keyboard navigation and zoom to 200%.
  • Print preview (Ctrl+P) to check @media print styles.

Lesson 34: Tooling and automation (optional)

None of this is required to build a site, but as projects grow these tools save time.

ToolWhat it does
Editor extensions (Prettier, Emmet, Live Server)Auto-format, expand abbreviations (ul>li*3), reload the browser on save
GitVersion control: keep history, undo mistakes, collaborate
Sass / PostCSSPre-processors adding nesting, mixins, autoprefixing (CSS now has native nesting)
Stylelint / HTMLHintCatch errors and enforce style rules automatically
LighthouseAudits for performance, accessibility, SEO
Bundlers (Vite, esbuild)Combine and minify files for production
Static hosting (GitHub Pages, Netlify)Publish a folder of HTML/CSS for free

Native CSS nesting

.card {
  padding: 1rem;
  & h3 { margin: 0; }
  &:hover { box-shadow: var(--shadow); }
  & .btn { margin-top: .5rem; }
  @media (min-width: 600px) { padding: 2rem; }
}

Lesson 35: Project - a complete landing page

This project combines everything: semantic structure, a responsive navigation, a hero built with Grid, a features section with Flexbox cards, a pricing table, a form and a footer. Copy both files, open index.html, then change the words, colours and images.

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>Cairo Book Shop - Learn HTML and CSS</title>
  <meta name="description" content="PDF and printed books about web development, in Arabic and English.">
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css">
</head>
<body>

        <li><a href="#features">Why us</a></li>

  <main id="main">
    <section class="hero">

    </section>

    <section id="features" class="features">

      <div class="cards">
        <article class="card"><h3>Step by step</h3><p>Every chapter builds on the last.</p></article>
        <article class="card"><h3>Searchable PDF</h3><p>Find any tag or property in seconds.</p></article>

        <div class="form-row"><label for="e">Email</label><input id="e" name="email" type="email" required autocomplete="email"></div>
        <div class="form-row"><label for="m">Message</label><textarea id="m" name="message" rows="4" required></textarea></div>
