/* styles.css */
@layer reset, base, layout, components;

@layer reset {
  *, *::before, *::after { box-sizing: border-box; }
  body, h1, h2, h3, p, ul { margin: 0; }
  img { max-width: 100%; height: auto; display: block; }
}

@layer base {
  :root {
    --brand: #b90000; --ink: #1b2431; --muted: #5b6472; --line: #d9d2c3; --bg: #faf8f3; --surface: #fff;
    --radius: 14px; --shadow: 0 10px 25px rgb(15 23 42 / 8%);
    --space: clamp(1rem, 2vw, 1.5rem);
  }
  body { font: 1.05rem/1.6 Georgia, serif; color: var(--ink); background: var(--bg); }
  h1, h2, h3 { font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; line-height: 1.15; }
  h1 { font-size: clamp(2rem, 1.4rem + 3vw, 3.25rem); }
  h2 { font-size: 1.75rem; margin-bottom: var(--space); }
  a { color: var(--brand); }
  a:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #ffbf47; outline-offset: 2px; }
  .lead { font-size: 1.2rem; color: var(--muted); }
}

@layer layout {
  .site-header { position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: 10; background: var(--surface); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line);
                 display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: var(--space); align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; padding: .75rem var(--space); }
  .nav { display: flex; gap: .25rem; list-style: none; padding: 0; }
  .nav a { display: block; padding: .5rem .9rem; border-radius: 999px; text-decoration: none; color: var(--ink); }
  .nav a:hover { background: var(--bg); }
  main > section { padding: clamp(2rem, 6vw, 5rem) var(--space); max-width: 70rem; margin-inline: auto; }
  .hero { display: grid; gap: var(--space); align-items: center; }
  @media (min-width: 800px) { .hero { grid-template-columns: 1.1fr 1fr; } }
  .hero__image { border-radius: var(--radius); box-shadow: var(--shadow); }
  .cards { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: var(--space); }
  .card { flex: 1 1 220px; }
  .site-footer { border-top: 1px solid var(--line); padding: var(--space); text-align: center; color: var(--muted); font-size: .9rem; }
}

@layer components {
  .btn { display: inline-block; padding: .7rem 1.4rem; border-radius: 999px; border: 0; background: var(--brand); color: #fff;
         font: inherit; font-weight: 600; text-decoration: none; cursor: pointer; transition: transform .15s, background-color .2s; }
  .btn:hover { background: #900; transform: translateY(-2px); }
  .card { background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: var(--radius); padding: var(--space); box-shadow: var(--shadow); }
  .card h3 { margin-bottom: .5rem; }
  .table-wrapper { overflow-x: auto; }
  table { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; background: var(--surface); }
  caption { text-align: left; padding: .5rem 0; color: var(--muted); }
  th, td { padding: .8rem 1rem; text-align: left; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line); }
  thead th { background: var(--brand); color: #fff; }
  tbody tr:nth-child(even) { background: #fcfbf8; }
  .form { display: grid; gap: 1rem; max-width: 36rem; }
  .form-row { display: grid; gap: .3rem; }
  @media (min-width: 600px) { .form-row { grid-template-columns: 8rem 1fr; align-items: start; } }
  label { font-weight: 600; }
  input, textarea { width: 100%; padding: .6rem .8rem; border: 1px solid #bbb; border-radius: 8px; font: inherit; }
  input:focus-visible, textarea:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #ffbf47; border-color: var(--brand); }
  .skip-link { position: absolute; top: -100px; left: 1rem; background: var(--brand); color: #fff; padding: .5rem 1rem; }
  .skip-link:focus { top: 1rem; }
  @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .btn { transition: none; } }
}

Exercises

  • Change the colour tokens to your own brand and watch every component update.
  • Add a fourth card and confirm the row wraps correctly on a narrow window.
  • Add an Arabic version: set lang="ar" dir="rtl" and replace left/right properties with logical ones (inline-start / inline-end).
  • Add a dark mode with prefers-color-scheme.
  • Run the page through the HTML validator and Lighthouse; fix every warning.

Lesson 36: Quick quiz and answers

QuestionAnswer
Which element creates an ordered list?<ol> (with <li> items)
Which attribute connects a <label> to its control?for, matching the control's id
What does border-collapse: collapse do?Merges adjacent cell borders into single lines
What is the specificity of #a .b p?1,1,1
Which CSS property makes a flex container?display: flex
How do you make images never overflow?img { max-width: 100%; height: auto; }
What does the viewport meta tag do?Makes the page use the real device width on phones
Which unit is relative to the root font size?rem
What does gap do?Adds space between flex/grid items without margins
How do you centre a block horizontally?Give it a width and margin-inline: auto (or use flex/grid)
Where should <main> appear?Once per page, containing the unique content
What is the difference between <b> and <strong>?<strong> means importance; <b> is only visual/keyword
Which selector matches every second row?tr:nth-child(even)
What does box-sizing: border-box change?width/height include padding and border
What replaces the bgcolor attribute?CSS background-color

Part 13: Practical Guides

Building a complete page step by step

This guide walks through building a small, correct web page using the elements from this book, in the order you would type them.

Step 1: The skeleton

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>My Book Store</title>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css">
</head>
<body>

</body>
</html>

Step 2: Landmarks

<body>
  <header>
    <h1>My Book Store</h1>
    <nav aria-label="Main">
      <ul>
        <li><a href="index.html" aria-current="page">Home</a></li>
        <li><a href="books.html">Books</a></li>
        <li><a href="contact.html">Contact</a></li>
      </ul>
    </nav>
  </header>

  <main>
    <!-- unique content goes here -->
  </main>

  <footer>
    <p><small>&copy; 2026 My Book Store</small></p>
  </footer>
</body>

Step 3: Content

<main>
  <section aria-labelledby="new">
    <h2 id="new">New this week</h2>
    <article class="card">
      <img src="html-book.jpg" alt="Cover of Learn HTML" width="200" height="300">
      <h3>Learn HTML</h3>
      <p>A complete beginner's guide. <span class="price">120 EGP</span></p>
      <button type="button">Add to cart</button>
    </article>
  </section>

  <section aria-labelledby="prices">
    <h2 id="prices">Price list</h2>
    <table>
      <caption>PDF books</caption>
      <thead><tr><th scope="col">Title</th><th scope="col">Price (EGP)</th></tr></thead>
      <tbody>
        <tr><td>Learn HTML</td><td>120</td></tr>
        <tr><td>Learn CSS</td><td>140</td></tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>
  </section>
</main>

Step 4: A form

<section aria-labelledby="contact">
  <h2 id="contact">Contact us</h2>
  <form action="/contact" method="post">
    <div class="field">
      <label for="name">Name</label>
      <input id="name" name="name" required autocomplete="name">
    </div>
    <div class="field">
      <label for="email">Email</label>
      <input id="email" name="email" type="email" required autocomplete="email">
    </div>
    <div class="field">
      <label for="msg">Message</label>
      <textarea id="msg" name="message" rows="4" required></textarea>
    </div>
    <button type="submit">Send</button>
  </form>
</section>

Step 5: The style sheet

/* style.css */
*, *::before, *::after { box-sizing: border-box; }
body { margin: 0; font-family: system-ui, Arial, sans-serif; line-height: 1.6; color: #1b2431; background: #f6f1e7; }
header, main, footer { padding: 1rem; }
header { background: #fff; box-shadow: 0 1px 0 #e7ddcb; }
nav ul { display: flex; gap: 1rem; list-style: none; padding: 0; margin: 0; }
nav a[aria-current="page"] { font-weight: bold; }
main { max-width: 960px; margin: 0 auto; }
.card { background: #fff; border-radius: 12px; padding: 1rem; display: grid; gap: 0.5rem; max-width: 260px; }
.price { color: #e60000; font-weight: bold; }
table { border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; background: #fff; }
th, td { padding: 0.5rem; border-bottom: 1px solid #e7ddcb; text-align: left; }
.field { display: grid; gap: 0.25rem; margin-bottom: 1rem; }
input, textarea { padding: 0.5rem; border: 1px solid #ccc; border-radius: 6px; font: inherit; }
button { background: #e60000; color: #fff; border: 0; border-radius: 6px; padding: 0.6rem 1.2rem; cursor: pointer; }
footer { text-align: center; color: #6b7280; }

Step 6: Check it

  • Open the file in a browser and resize the window.
  • Press Tab repeatedly: every link, input and button should receive a visible focus ring in a sensible order.
  • Validate at validator.w3.org.
  • Run Lighthouse (in Chrome DevTools) for accessibility and performance scores.

Lists in depth

HTML has three list elements: <ul> for unordered lists, <ol> for ordered lists and <dl> for description lists. Items of ul and ol are <li>; a dl uses <dt> for terms and <dd> for descriptions.

Choosing the right list

QuestionUse
Does the order matter (steps, ranking)?<ol>
Is it a set of items where order is irrelevant?<ul>
Are they name-value pairs (term and definition, label and data)?<dl>
Is it a toolbar of actions?<menu>
Is it navigation links?<nav> containing a <ul>

Numbering control on ordered lists

Attribute / CSSEffectExample
type="1"1, 2, 3 (default)<ol type="1">
type="a" / "A"a, b, c / A, B, C<ol type="A">
type="i" / "I"i, ii, iii / I, II, III<ol type="I">
start="5"Begin at 5<ol start="5">
reversedCount down<ol reversed>
<li value="10">Set this item's number
list-style-type: lower-greekCSS: alpha, beta, gammaol { list-style-type: lower-greek; }
list-style-type: arabic-indicCSS: Arabic-Indic digitsol { list-style-type: arabic-indic; }

CSS list-style-type values

For <ul>: disc (default), circle, square, none, or any string such as '→ '. For <ol>: decimal, decimal-leading-zero, lower-roman, upper-roman, lower-alpha, upper-alpha, lower-greek, armenian, georgian, arabic-indic, persian, bengali, devanagari, cjk-decimal, japanese-informal, and more. list-style-position: inside puts the marker inside the item's box; outside (default) hangs it in the margin. list-style-image: url(icon.svg) uses an image; ::marker is the modern way to style markers.

Nested lists

<ol>
  <li>Prepare
    <ul>
      <li>Install an editor</li>
      <li>Create a folder</li>
    </ul>
  </li>
  <li>Write HTML
    <ol type="a">
      <li>Skeleton</li>
      <li>Content</li>
    </ol>
  </li>
</ol>

Description lists for metadata

<dl>
  <dt>Author</dt><dd>Sara Ali</dd>
  <dt>Published</dt><dd><time datetime="2026-09">September 2026</time></dd>
  <dt>Pages</dt><dd>2000</dd>
</dl>

Common mistakes

  • Text directly inside <ul> or <ol> that is not in an <li>.
  • A nested list placed between <li> elements instead of inside one.
  • Using <br> or paragraphs starting with '-' instead of a real list.
  • Using <dl> for dialogue or for layout.

Tables in depth

Use tables for data whose meaning depends on rows and columns. A well-built table has a caption, header cells with scope, and grouped rows.

Element roles

ElementRole
<table>The table container
<caption>Title, first child
<colgroup> / <col>Column groups for styling
<thead>Header rows
<tbody>Data rows (one or more)
<tfoot>Summary rows
<tr>A row
<th>Header cell, with scope=col|row|colgroup|rowgroup
<td>Data cell

colspan and rowspan

colspan="n" makes a cell span n columns; rowspan="n" makes it span n rows. Every row must still add up to the same number of columns. Sketch the grid on paper for complex tables.

<table>
  <tr><th rowspan="2">Product</th><th colspan="2">Sales</th></tr>
  <tr><th>2025</th><th>2026</th></tr>
  <tr><td>Books</td><td>120</td><td>150</td></tr>
</table>

HTML 3.2/4 attributes and their CSS replacements

Old attributeCSS replacement
border="1"th, td { border: 1px solid; }
cellpadding="5"th, td { padding: 5px; }
cellspacing="0"table { border-collapse: collapse; } or border-spacing: 0
width="100%"table { width: 100%; }
bgcolor="#eee"background-color: #eee
align="center" on tabletable { margin: 0 auto; }
align="right" on tdtd { text-align: right; }
valign="top"vertical-align: top
nowrapwhite-space: nowrap
summary="..."<caption> or aria-describedby

Making tables responsive

  • Wrap the table in a div with overflow-x: auto so it scrolls horizontally on phones.
  • Hide less important columns on small screens with a media query.
  • Stack cells into blocks with display: block and data-label attributes (see the CSS cookbook).
  • Use font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums so digits line up.

Sorting and filtering

HTML has no built-in sorting. Add it with JavaScript by reading rows from tbody, sorting the array and re-appending, and mark the sorted column header with aria-sort="ascending" or "descending".

Forms in depth

A form collects input and sends it to a server or a script. Building a good form is mostly about labels, the right input types, validation and clear feedback.

Checklist

  • Every control has a <label> linked by for/id or wrapping.
  • Every control that must be submitted has a name.
  • Use the most specific type: email, tel, url, number, date, and so on.
  • Use autocomplete tokens so browsers can fill in addresses and cards.
  • Group radio buttons and checkboxes with <fieldset> and <legend>.
  • Mark required fields with required and say so visibly.
  • Use pattern with a title explaining the format.
  • Show errors next to the field and link them with aria-describedby; do not rely on colour alone.
  • Use method="post" for anything that changes data; enctype="multipart/form-data" for files.
  • Validate again on the server; client validation is only a convenience.

GET versus POST

GETPOST
Data locationIn the URL (?a=1&b=2)In the request body
BookmarkableYesNo
Size limitAbout 2000 charactersPractically none
Use forSearches, filtersLogins, orders, uploads, anything with side effects
SecurityVisible in history and logsNot in URL (still needs HTTPS)

Built-in validation attributes

AttributeApplies toChecks
requiredMost inputs, select, textareaNot empty / selected
minlength / maxlengthText-like inputs, textareaLength
min / maxnumber, range, date, time...Range
stepnumber, range, date, time...Granularity
patterntext, search, url, tel, email, passwordRegular expression (whole value)
type=email / urlinputFormat

Styling validation states

input:required { border-left: 3px solid #999; }
input:user-invalid { border-color: #b90000; }
input:user-valid { border-color: #0f8a4c; }
.error { color: #b90000; font-size: 0.9em; }

Custom validation messages

<input id="zip" pattern="[0-9]{5}" required>
<script>
  const zip = document.getElementById('zip');
  zip.addEventListener('invalid', () => zip.setCustomValidity('Enter exactly five digits.'));
  zip.addEventListener('input', () => zip.setCustomValidity(''));
</script>

Semantic layout and accessibility

Semantic HTML means choosing elements for what they mean, not how they look. It is the foundation of accessibility: screen readers, keyboard navigation, reader modes and search engines all depend on it.

Landmark map

ElementLandmark roleHow many per page
<header> (top level)banner1
<nav>navigationSeveral; label each
<main>mainExactly 1
<aside>complementarySeveral
<footer> (top level)contentinfo1
<form> with a nameformSeveral
<search>searchSeveral
<section> with a nameregionSeveral

Heading outline

One <h1> per page, then h2 for sections, h3 inside them and so on, never skipping levels. Users of screen readers navigate by headings more than by any other means.

Images

  • Informative image: alt describes the content.
  • Functional image (in a link or button): alt describes the action.
  • Decorative image: alt="" (empty).
  • Complex image (chart): short alt plus a full description in text or a linked page.

Keyboard

  • Everything clickable must be reachable with Tab and operable with Enter or Space: use <a>, <button> and form controls, not <div onclick>.
  • Never remove the focus outline without providing a visible replacement (:focus-visible).
  • Provide a skip link to <main>.
  • Manage focus in dialogs and after dynamic changes.

Colour and motion

  • Text contrast at least 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text).
  • Never convey information by colour alone.
  • Respect prefers-reduced-motion; avoid flashing content.

ARIA in three rules

  • Do not use ARIA if a native element does the job.
  • Do not change native semantics unless you must.
  • All interactive ARIA controls must be keyboard usable.

Media: images, audio and video

Choosing an image format

FormatBest forNotes
AVIFPhotos, smallest filesNewest; use with fallback
WebPPhotos and graphicsWidely supported
JPEGPhotos, universal fallbackNo transparency
PNGScreenshots, logos with transparencyLarge for photos
SVGIcons, logos, diagramsScales perfectly; can be styled
GIFSimple animationsPrefer video or animated WebP/AVIF

Responsive image decision

  • Same image, different sizes: <img srcset sizes>.
  • Different crops or formats: <picture> with <source>.
  • High-DPI only: srcset with 1x/2x.
  • Always: alt, width, height, and loading="lazy" below the fold.

Audio and video checklist

  • Provide MP4 (H.264) plus WebM.
  • Add controls.
  • Add <track kind="captions">.
  • Set poster and preload="metadata".
  • For background video: autoplay muted loop playsinline, and pause it for prefers-reduced-motion.
  • Provide a transcript.

Embedding third-party media

YouTube, Vimeo and maps are embedded with <iframe>. Always add title, loading="lazy" and only the allow permissions you need. Consider a click-to-load facade to save bandwidth.

SEO essentials in HTML

  • Unique, descriptive <title> under 60 characters.
  • <meta name="description"> under 160 characters.
  • One <h1> matching the page topic; logical heading structure.
  • Semantic landmarks so crawlers understand the page.
  • Descriptive link text; internal links between related pages.
  • alt text on images; descriptive file names.
  • <link rel="canonical"> to avoid duplicates; hreflang alternates for translations.
  • Structured data with JSON-LD (schema.org) for rich results.
  • Fast loading: compressed images, lazy loading, deferred scripts, preconnect for fonts.
  • Mobile friendly: the viewport meta tag and responsive CSS.
  • Open Graph and Twitter tags for attractive sharing previews.

Migrating old HTML (2, 3.2, 4) to HTML5

OldNew

<meta http-equiv="Content-Type" content="text/html; charset=utf-8"><meta charset="utf-8">
<script type="text/javascript"><script>
<style type="text/css"><style>
<font size color face>CSS font-size, color, font-family
<center>CSS text-align: center / margin: auto
<b> for importance<strong>
<i> for emphasis<em>
<u>CSS text-decoration or <ins>
<strike><s> or <del>
<tt><code>, <kbd>, <samp>
<big>CSS font-size
<div id="header"><header>
<div id="nav"><nav>
<div id="content"><main>
<div class="sidebar"><aside>
<div id="footer"><footer>
<div class="post"><article>
<table> for layoutCSS grid / flexbox
<frameset> / <frame>CSS layout; <iframe> if needed
<applet>, <embed> Flash<video>, <audio>, <canvas>, JavaScript
<a name="x">id="x" on any element
<acronym><abbr>
<dir>, <menu> as list<ul>

<br clear="all">CSS clear or flow-root

Part 14: Glossary

Glossary

TermDefinition
Accessibility (a11y)Designing pages so that people with disabilities can use them, including with screen readers, keyboards, magnifiers and voice control.
ARIAAccessible Rich Internet Applications: a set of role and aria-* attributes that describe widgets and states to assistive technology.
AttributeA name=value pair inside an opening tag that configures the element, for example href="page.html".
Block-level elementAn element that starts on a new line and fills the available width, such as <div>, <p>, <h1>, <footer>.
Boolean attributeAn attribute whose presence means true and absence means false, such as disabled, checked, required.
BrowserThe program that reads HTML, CSS and JavaScript and displays web pages: Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge.
CascadeThe CSS mechanism that decides which of several conflicting rules applies, based on importance, specificity and order.
Character reference / entityA way to write a character by name or number, such as &amp; or &#169;.
Child / parent / sibling / ancestor / descendantFamily terms describing element nesting in the document tree.
ClassA reusable label applied with the class attribute and targeted in CSS with a dot: .name.
Content modelThe rules stating which children an element may contain.
CSSCascading Style Sheets: the language that describes presentation.
DeprecatedStill supported but discouraged; may be removed in future.
DOCTYPEThe declaration at the top of a document (<!DOCTYPE html>) that switches the browser to standards mode.
DOMDocument Object Model: the tree of objects the browser builds from HTML, which JavaScript can read and modify.
ElementAn opening tag, its content and its closing tag together (or a void tag alone).
Empty / void elementAn element with no content and no closing tag, such as <br>, <img>, <input>.
Flow contentElements allowed in the body: most elements.
FocusThe state of the element that currently receives keyboard input, moved with Tab.
FragmentThe part of a URL after #, pointing to an element id.
Global attributeAn attribute allowed on every element, such as id, class, style, title, lang, hidden.
HTMLHyperText Markup Language: the language that structures web pages.
HTTP / HTTPSThe protocol browsers use to fetch pages; HTTPS is the encrypted version.
HyperlinkA reference to another resource that the user can follow, created with <a href>.
IdA unique identifier for one element, targeted in CSS with # and in links with #.
Inline elementAn element that flows within text and takes only the width of its content: <span>, <a>, <em>.
JavaScriptThe programming language of the web, which adds behaviour to pages.
LandmarkA region of the page (banner, navigation, main, contentinfo...) that assistive technology can jump to.
Living StandardThe continuously updated HTML specification maintained by the WHATWG.
MDNMozilla Developer Network (developer.mozilla.org), the most complete free web documentation.
MetadataData about the document, placed in <head>.
MIME typeA label such as text/html or image/png that identifies the type of a file.
NestingPlacing elements inside other elements.
ObsoleteRemoved from the standard; must not be used.
Phrasing contentText and inline elements that can appear inside a paragraph.
Pseudo-class / pseudo-elementCSS selectors for states (:hover) or generated parts (::before).
Quirks modeA compatibility rendering mode triggered by a missing DOCTYPE that imitates 1990s browser bugs.
RenderingThe process of turning HTML and CSS into pixels.
Responsive designLayouts that adapt to any screen size, using fluid widths, flexible images and media queries.
Screen readerSoftware that reads the page aloud or in braille for blind users (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver, TalkBack).
Sectioning content<article>, <aside>, <nav>, <section>: elements that define the scope of headings and footers.
SelectorThe part of a CSS rule that chooses which elements to style.
Semantic HTMLUsing elements according to their meaning.
SpecificityThe weight of a CSS selector, used by the cascade to resolve conflicts.
TagThe markup in angle brackets, <p> or </p>, that starts or ends an element.
URLUniform Resource Locator: the address of a resource on the web.
UTF-8The character encoding that supports every language; always use it.
ValidatorA tool that checks HTML for errors (validator.w3.org).
ViewportThe visible area of the page in the browser window.
W3CWorld Wide Web Consortium, the standards body that published HTML 3.2 to HTML 5.2.
WCAGWeb Content Accessibility Guidelines, the international accessibility standard.
WHATWGThe browser vendor group that maintains the HTML Living Standard.
XHTMLHTML written with XML syntax rules.
No entries match. Try another word, a tag name without brackets, or an attribute name.
